description: Formulate a precise conjecture stating that the endpoint Fourier restriction inequality for the three‑dimensional paraboloid over a prime field 𝔽ₚ (with –1 non‑square) holds if and only if the set of integer lattice points on the Euclidean paraboloid  \(\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb Z^3 : z = x^2 + y^2\}\) is a Λ(3) set. This makes the qualitative observation in the paper into a bidirectional, falsifiable statement that can be expressed in the language of finite‑field harmonic analysis and additive combinatorics, and thus be formalised in Lean 4.
domain_bridges: Finite field Fourier analysis ↔ Euclidean additive combinatorics
proof_strategy: 1. Formalise the finite‑field paraboloid \(P_3 \subset \mathbb F_p^3\) and the associated extension operator \(E f(x) = p^{-2}\sum_{\xi\in P_3} f(\xi) e_p(x\cdot\xi)\). 2. Define the endpoint restriction constant \(R^*(2\to 3)\) and express the conjectured bound \(R^*(2\to 3) \le C\) uniformly in \(p\). 3. Formalise the Euclidean set \(\Lambda = \{(m,n,m^2+n^2) : m,n\in\mathbb Z\}\) and the Λ(3) property: there exists \(C'\) such that for every finitely supported sequence \(a_\lambda\), \(\big\|\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda} a_\lambda e^{2\pi i \lambda\cdot x}\big\|_{L^3(\mathbb T^3)} \le C' \|a\|_{\ell^2}\). 4. Prove the “if” direction by adapting the argument in the paper: assume the endpoint restriction estimate, lift functions from \(\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z\) to \(\mathbb Z\) via the natural embedding, and use Plancherel and orthogonality to obtain the Λ(3) inequality. 5. For the “only‑if” direction, assume \(\Lambda\) is a Λ(3) set; construct test functions on \(\mathbb F_p^3\) by reductio
title: Equivalence between the finite‑field endpoint restriction estimate for the 3‑dimensional paraboloid and the Λ(3) property of the integer lattice paraboloid

description: For any finite polymatroid P with ground set E and rank function f, and any integer j with 1 ≤ j ≤ f(E)−1, the j‑th slice‑projection from the top of P is connected if and only if the j‑th slice‑projection from the bottom of its dual polymatroid P⁎ is connected. This extends the known equality for j = 1 (deletion/contraction) to all intermediate slice‑projections.
proof_strategy: Formalize polymatroids as submodular rank functions in Lean, define slice‑projections P.slice_top j = {a ∈ P | Σ_{i∈E} a_i = f(E) - j} and P.slice_bot j = {a ∈ P | Σ_{i∈E} a_i = j}. Prove that duality swaps top and bottom slice‑projections: (P.slice_top j)ᵈ = Pᵈ.slice_bot j. Show that connectedness of a polymatroid is preserved under duality (using the matroid‑like circuit/cocircuit characterisation). Then the equivalence of connectedness follows directly. The main technical work is establishing the dual rank function f⁎(S)=f(E\S)−f(E\S∪{e})+f({e}) and proving the slice‑projection duality lemma, after which the conjecture reduces to a lemma already proved for j=1 and an induction on j.
title: Dual Slice-Projection Connectivity Conjecture for Polymatroids

description: Conjecture that for all grid sizes m,n ≥ 3 the number of vertices of degree 4 in the flip graph of the m×n Miura‑ori equals (m‑1)(n‑1).
proof_strategy: Use the bijection between flat‑foldable Miura‑ori assignments and proper 3‑colourings of the grid graph, translate vertex degree to the number of strict local extrema of the associated integer height function, prove the polynomial count (m‑1)(n‑1) for degree‑4 vertices by induction on m and n, and derive diameter bounds via extremal Lipschitz‑function inequalities.
title: Degree‑4 vertices in the flip graph of the m×n Miura‑ori

description: For any fixed k ≥3 and γ > γ_k (as defined in the paper), there exists a constant c >0 such that any induced-K_{1,k}-free graph G with edge density at least γ is within edit distance at most cn² of a graph that is the union of k−1 cliques with no edges between them. This conjecture directly formalizes the paper's structural claim about the supercritical regime and can be verified by proving bounds on the deviation from such a partitioned structure.
proof_strategy: Prove that for γ > γ_k, the entropy-maximizing graphons must be unions of k−1 cliques by contradiction, using stability results from the variational analysis. Show that any deviation from this structure would decrease entropy, leveraging the paper's characterization of optimizers.
title: Typical structure of induced-K_{1,k}-free graphs in the supercritical regime

catalog_references: Greenberg's Conjecture for cyclotomic Z_p-extensions of totally real fields
Maximal abelian pro-p extensions unramified outside a prescribed set of p-adic primes
description: Let k be a totally real number field, p a prime, and Sigma a nonempty set of p-adic primes of k. Suppose the Galois group X_Sigma(k) of the maximal abelian pro-p extension of k unramified outside Sigma has Z_p-rank exactly 1, so that there is a unique Sigma-ramified Z_p-extension N_infty/k. Then the unramified Iwasawa module X(N_infty) is finite as a Z_p-module.
domain_bridges: Class field theory connects X_Sigma(k) with ray class groups of p-power conductor supported on Sigma.
Commutative algebra over Z_p[[T]] converts finiteness of X(N_infty) into vanishing of the Lambda-rank and boundedness of finite-layer p-class groups.
Decomposition theory of p-adic primes in N_infty/k controls the transition maps between finite-level class groups.
proof_strategy: Formalize the statement first with abstract constants for p-adic primes, X_Sigma(k), the unique Sigma-ramified Z_p-extension, and the unramified Iwasawa module. A proof would likely proceed by identifying X(N_infty) with an inverse limit of p-primary class groups, applying class field theory to compare the Sigma-ramified tower with the maximal unramified pro-p tower, and then proving boundedness of the relevant class groups using the rank-one hypothesis on X_Sigma(k). The conjecture is falsifiable by exhibiting a totally real k, a prime p, and Sigma with rank_Zp X_Sigma(k)=1 but with unbounded p-primary class groups along N_infty.
title: Restricted-ramification Greenberg finiteness for rank-one p-ramified towers

catalog_references: Zero Forcing Parameters and Graph Operations
description: For the complete bipartite graph K_{a,b} with 2 ≤ a ≤ b, transmission proportion p = 1/a, and threshold τ = 1, the transmission zero forcing number TZF(K_{a,b}, 1/a, 1) equals a. This conjecture posits that the minimum initial set consists of all vertices from the smaller part, and that no smaller set can percolate under these parameters.
proof_strategy: Show that initializing all a vertices of the smaller part fills the graph: each has weight 1 and transmits 1/a to each of its b neighbors, giving every vertex in the larger part total weight a·(1/a)=1, meeting the threshold. Conversely, prove that any set of size <a fails because the total transmission capacity into the larger part is insufficient to reach threshold 1 on all b vertices, using a double-counting argument on the total weight transmitted across the bipartition.
title: Transmission Zero Forcing Number of Complete Bipartite Graphs

description: For fixed integers t ≥ 2, r ≥ 2 and n ≥ 1, let a coloring c : (Fin t)^n → Fin r be *coordinate‑symmetric*, i.e. c depends only on the vector of letter‑counts (the histogram of each colour in the word). Define the discrete simplex Δ_{t,n} = {v : Fin t → ℕ // ∑_{i} v i = n}. A *corner tuple* in Δ_{t,n} is a triple (v, v+e_i, v+e_j) with i ≠ j and e_i the unit vector at i, provided the three vectors lie in Δ_{t,n}. The conjecture states that such a symmetric coloring c is line‑free (contains no monochromatic combinatorial line in [t]^n) if and only if no corner tuple of Δ_{t,n} is monochromatic under the induced coloring on Δ_{t,n}. This gives a finite, polynomial‑size certificate for line‑freeness of symmetric colorings, matching the reduction lemma used in the Hales‑Jewett lower‑bound constructions.
proof_strategy: Define the histogram map hist : (Fin t)^n → Δ_{t,n} and prove that for any combinatorial line L with root τ, the set of histograms of points in L is exactly a corner tuple (or a degenerate case). Show that monochromaticity of L implies monochromaticity of the corresponding corner tuple, and conversely that a monochromatic corner tuple yields a monochromatic line after lifting via any word with that histogram. The forward direction uses the fact that active coordinates change exactly one count while inactive coordinates keep the others fixed; the backward direction selects a concrete word realizing a given histogram (possible by multinomial construction). Formalize both implications in Lean, then obtain the equivalence. The conjecture is falsifiable by constructing a symmetric coloring that violates the equivalence; otherwise a formal proof in Lean confirms it.
title: Equivalence of Line‑Freeness and Corner‑Tuple Monochromaticity for Coordinate‑Symmetric Colorings

description: Conjecture: For each t,r >= 2, there exists N such that for all n >= N, any t-uniform hypergraph G on n vertices that is (n,d,λ)-pseudo-random (i.e., each vertex has degree (1+o(1)) * binomial(n-1, t-1) and any two vertices belong to at most (1+o(1)) * binomial(n-2, t-2) edges) yields that any r-edge-colouring of G contains a monochromatic matching of size exactly floor((n+r-1)/(r+t-1)). In particular, this conjecture implies that the only extremal colourings achieving the Alon–Frankl–Lovász bound are the r‑strip colourings (vertex set partitioned into ≤ r parts and colour depends only on intersection profile).
proof_strategy: To prove the conjecture, one would extend the structural reduction theorem of the paper to an exact version. The main steps are: (1) Show that for pseudo-random hypergraphs the density of each colour class is close to 1/r, (2) Apply hypergraph regularity to partition the vertex set into a bounded number of quasi‑random parts, (3) Use convex‑geometric compression to reduce the colouring to one where the colour of an edge depends only on its intersection profile with the parts (an r‑strip colouring), (4) Observe that an r‑strip colouring attains the exact AFL bound, and (5) Argue that any deviation from an r‑strip colouring would force a larger monochromatic matching, contradicting maximality. An induction on n together with a careful analysis of the LP dual for the matching problem would yield the required exactness.
title: Exact Monochromatic Matching Bound for Pseudo-Random Hypergraphs

description: The current best asymptotic lower bound is g(r) ≥ (61/20 - o(1))r ≈ 3.05r. We conjecture that the true asymptotic constant is at least 3.1, i.e., for every ε > 0, there exists r₀ such that for all r ≥ r₀, g(r) ≥ (3.1 - ε)r.
proof_strategy: Refine the peeling argument by introducing a weighted charging scheme that accounts for the structure of the intersection graph of the residual hypergraph after removing high-degree vertices. Alternatively, apply a more sophisticated version of Kahn's theorem with better codegree control, or develop a new Lagrangian method for intersecting hypergraphs with large cover number.
title: Asymptotic Lower Bound Improvement for Erdős-Lovász Function

description: Let H be any nonempty finite simple graph, let b : Fin m -> Nat be a nonempty list of positive clique sizes, and let B(b) be the disjoint union of cliques K_{b_r}. Form the graph G = H * B(b), where * denotes graph join. If nu(b) is the number of indices r with b_r >= 2, then over every field k the Castelnuovo--Mumford regularity of the edge-ideal quotient satisfies reg_k(R/I(G)) = max(1, reg_k(R/I(H)), nu(b)). This extends the split-like and clique-star cases from the paper by replacing the independent or complete core by an arbitrary finite graph.
domain_bridges: graph join -> disjoint union decomposition of independence complexes
disjoint union of clique blocks -> join of discrete simplicial complexes
reduced simplicial homology -> nonzero Hochster summands
proof_strategy: Prove first that Ind((H * B)[U union T]) is the union of Ind(H[U]) and Ind(B[T]) with only the empty face in common. Deduce that positive-degree reduced homology is the direct sum of the two sides, while degree-zero homology contributes one extra class whenever both vertex parts are nonempty, giving the max with 1. Next compute reg(B(b)) by writing Ind(B[T]) as a join of discrete complexes D_{t_r}; its only possible top reduced homology occurs in degree s-1, where s is the number of selected blocks with t_r >= 2, so the maximum value of q+1 is nu(b). Combine these facts through Hochster's formula to obtain the stated equality.
title: Regularity of arbitrary-core joins with clique blocks

description: A precise, falsifiable conjecture linking the density parameters α and β of vertical and horizontal stripes in aperiodic Wang tile families to a Diophantine condition on pairs of quadratic irrationals.
proof_strategy: Constructive Diophantine argument via scaling and scaling-free constructions
title: Sufficient condition for non-periodicity of awaited set of Wang tiles

description: We conjecture that a random linear code C ⊆ F_q^n of rate 1 - (1/n)log_q|B_ρ| (without the ε term) satisfies |C ∩ B| = (1 ± o(1)) * |C||B|/q^n simultaneously for all radius-ρ Hamming balls B with high probability. This extends the paper's result which requires an ε > 0 term.
proof_strategy: Adapt the second-moment method from the paper, removing the ε term and demonstrating that the variance still concentrates to yield the o(1) deviation bound.
title: Random Linear Codes Achieve List-Decoding Capacity with Concentration

description: Conjectures that the prime zeta function for imaginary quadratic fields with class number one has a natural boundary extending from the origin along the imaginary axis, preventing regularization of the product of all primes via standard zeta-regularization techniques.
proof_strategy: Leverage analytic continuation of Dirichlet L-functions and properties of their critical strips to establish the natural boundary's extent and position, then apply techniques from complex analysis to demonstrate the absence of meromorphic continuation beyond the boundary.
title: Existence of a Natural Boundary for the Prime Zeta Function in Imaginary Quadratic Fields

description: The stable tropical intersection is reduced iff specific structural conditions on the subvariety and fan hold, verified via algebraic validation.
proof_strategy: Constructive induction on polynomial ring structures
title: Reduction Condition for Reduced Points

description: We conjecturally extend the known finiteness result for minor-closed classes with limiting density above a threshold to the setting of arbitrary density bounds. Specifically, for any rational number \(\delta < \frac{3}{2}\), we propose that the set of \subseteq\-minimal minor-closed classes with density \(>\delta\) is finite. This refines the formulaic finiteness result to all density thresholds in the interval \([0, \frac{3}{2})\), building on the structural properties of minor-closed classes and their limiting densities.
proof_strategy: Adaptation of the framework from [1] by parametrizing reductions for arbitrary density thresholds, then formalizing the topology of \(\mathbb{Q} \cap [0, \frac{3}{2})\) in Lean 4 using rational number types and real number approximations.
title: Finite Obstructions for Minor-Closed Classes with Bounded Limiting Density

description: This paper investigates the local obstruction groups for obstructed deformation problems arising from weightℒ newforms of level N, using the Greenberg-Wiles formula and explicit classification of inertial Weil-Deligne types. It aims to provide a constructive framework for understanding deformation in arithmetic settings with restricted primes.
proof_strategy: Intermediate computation with explicit presentation of deformation rings
title: Obstructed deformation problems for weight-2 newforms with local-global conditions

description:
For every integer m ≥ 0, the regularised Wallis product P_m defined by
P_m = ∏_{n=2}^∞ exp(∑_{r=1}^{⌊m/2⌋} n^{m-2r}/r) (1 - 1/n^2)^{n^m}
satisfies
log P_m = -∑_{r=⌊m/2⌋+1}^∞ (ζ(2r - m) - 1)/r,
where ζ denotes the Riemann zeta function. This provides an explicit zeta‑function tail for the logarithm of each product in the hierarchy.
proof_strategy: Take the logarithm of the product, expand log(1-1/n^2) as -∑_{r≥1} 1/(r n^{2r}), multiply by n^m, isolate the terms with non‑negative exponent in n (those with r ≤ ⌊m/2⌋) and cancel them by the exponential factor. The remaining sum over n yields ∑_{n≥2} n^{m-2r} = ζ(2r-m)-1 after analytic continuation. Interchange the sums (justified by absolute convergence of the tail) to obtain the claimed series for log P_m.
title: Logarithmic formula for the regularised Wallis hierarchy

description: For any bipartite graph G with partite sets A and B, the strong chromatic index satisfies χ'_s(G) ≤ Δ_A Δ_B, where Δ_A and Δ_B are the maximum degrees in each partition. This conjecture posits that the product of the maximum degrees in each partition forms an upper bound for the strong chromatic index, improving upon the current best-known bound of 1.676 Δ_A Δ_B for sufficiently large products.
proof_strategy: The conjecture can be approached via probabilistic methods combined with sparse neighborhood analysis, similar to techniques used in prior improvements of the Erdős-Nesetrýl conjecture. Key steps include constructing an induced matching decomposition that respects the product bound Δ_A Δ_B and leveraging the bipartite structure to minimize color conflicts.
title: Brualdi-Quinn Massey Strong Chromatic Index Conjecture for Bipartite Graphs

description: The conjecture asserts no primes exceeding 7 satisfy $n! + 1 = m^2$ for $n < p$. This is falsifiable via computational checks.
proof_strategy: Verification using computational verification of primes >7
title: The Non-Existence of New Factorial Square Solutions

description: For any partition λ of N, let G_λ denote the abelian p-group associated with λ. Then the number Nu(Per(G_λ)) of distinct monomials in the group permanent satisfies: Nu(Per(G_λ)) ≡ 1 (mod p^k) where k = 3 if p is a Wolstenholme prime and k = 2 otherwise, for all primes p ≥ 5 and all partitions λ with |λ| = N ≥ p. This extends the known result for cyclic p-groups to all abelian p-groups classified by partitions.
proof_strategy: Use the explicit formula for Nu(Per(G_λ)) in terms of partial column sums of Young diagrams, apply Lucas's theorem on binomial coefficients modulo prime powers, and leverage the characterization of Wolstenholme primes via the congruence (2p-1 choose p-1) ≡ 1 (mod p³). The proof would proceed by induction on the partition structure and analysis of the φ_G(d) terms in the summation formula.
title: Congruence Properties of Group Permanents for Abelian p-Groups and Wolstenholme Primes

description: Prove that for any prime power q, the Grassmann scheme J_q(n,k) is degree-one trivial (DOT) for all n >= N(q,k), where N(q,k) is a constant depending on q and k. Specifically, for q=2, N(2,k)=4 for min(k,n-k) >= 2, and for q > 2, the threshold N(q,k) must be determined to exclude sporadic counterexamples like the Bruen-Drudge example in J_3(4,2).
proof_strategy: Define the Grassmannian as a set of subspaces using Lean's LinearAlgebra library. Formalize the space of functions f: J_q(n,k) -> R. Define 'degree one' as functions in the span of indicator functions of points. Implement the 'trivial' list of functions. Use an induction on n or a stability result from representation theory to show that as n increases, the gap between the eigenvalues of the Grassmann graph forces any Boolean degree-one function to be a linear combination of trivial indicators.
title: Characterization of Degree-One Triviality for Grassmannians over Finite Fields

description: For each integer n≥1 there exists a finite family C of pairwise disjoint compact (or open bounded) convex sets in ℝ^{3n} such that the space L(C) of all lines transversal to C is homeomorphic (hence homotopy equivalent) to the (n‑1)-sphere S^{n‑1}. Moreover, for any family of pairwise disjoint convex sets whose transversal space is non‑empty and whose reduced (n‑1)‑st homology is non‑zero, the transversal space is homotopy equivalent to S^{n‑1}. This refines the counterexamples to the Cheong–Goaoc–Holmsen conjecture by identifying the exact homotopy type.
proof_strategy: Construct the family C as in Theorem 1.2 of the paper (a product of n disjoint “tube” pairs in ℝ^3). Show that the space of line transversals decomposes as a product of n copies of a circle of lines crossing a fixed pair of convex sets, and that the natural map to the unit sphere in ℝ^n given by the direction vectors of the lines is a homeomorphism onto S^{n‑1}. Use the explicit parameterization of transversals to verify continuity, bijectivity, and closedness. For the converse direction, apply homology detection: any non‑trivial reduced (n‑1)‑st homology class forces the space to be a closed (n‑1)‑manifold without boundary, and the only such manifold arising from convex transversals in the constructed dimensions is S^{n‑1}. Formalize these steps in Lean using the existing libraries for manifolds, homology, and convex sets.
title: Homotopy type of line transversal spaces for disjoint convex families

description: For any graph G, the externally supported independence number α_es(G) satisfies α_es(G) + 1 ≥ α(G), where α(G) is the standard independence number.
proof_strategy: The proof could proceed by considering any independent set B and showing that its externally supported subset must have size at least α(G) -1. Alternatively, by induction on the number of vertices, leveraging the recursive properties of graphs and the definitions of ESI-sets.
title: Conjecture on Externally Supported Independence Number

description: Conjecture: For rational β = p/q, the natural extension has finite domain bridges.
proof_strategy: Constructive counterexample based on known results
title: Domain Finiteness

description: Conjecture: Let P be a connected polymatroid on a finite ground set E. For any element e ∈ E that is neither a loop (f({e})=0) nor a coloop (f(E)−f(E\{e}) = f({e})), both the deletion P−e and the contraction P/e are connected polymatroids. This would strengthen Hall's 2013 result which guarantees only two elements with at least one connected minor.
proof_strategy: Use the submodularity of the rank function to show that if either deletion or contraction were disconnected, one could construct a partition of the ground set violating the assumption that e is neither a loop nor a coloop. Combine with Hall's counting argument to upgrade the existence of two good elements to the stronger statement for all non-loop non-coloop elements.
title: Both deletion and contraction of a non-loop non-coloop element preserve connectivity in connected polymatroids

description: We conjecture that for a pure r-dimensional simplicial complex K on n vertices, if the reduced homology \(\widetilde{H}_t(\text{lk}(\sigma), \mathbb{R}) = 0\) for every face \(\sigma\) of dimension r-t, then the signless Laplacian spectral radius q_{r-1}(K) is upper bounded by tn - (t-1)(r+1). Moreover, we propose that for r-down path connected K with n sufficiently large, equality holds if and only if K is a join of a (r+1-t)-simplex and a (t-1)-skeleton of a simplex of size n-r-1+t.
proof_strategy: We will develop a simplicial complex version of the Hoffman bound for graphs by analyzing the spectral properties of the signless Laplacian matrix of the join of simplices. This will involve studying the eigenvalues of the join matrix, constructing explicit examples achieving the bound, and using homology constraints to derive inequalities on the spectral radius. We will also employ a matroid intersection approach to characterize the extremal complexes.
title: Signless Laplacian Spectral Radius of Pure Simplicial Complexes with vanishing link homology in dimension t

description: We conjecture that for every integer degree d ≥ 1 there exists a polynomial P_d(m,n) with integer coefficients such that for all sufficiently large grid dimensions (i.e., m,n ≥ T(d) for some threshold depending only on d) the number N_{m,n}(d) of vertices of degree d in the flip graph ΟұG(Ζ_{m,n}) equals P_d(m,n). Moreover, P_d is symmetric in m and n and can be expressed as a ℤ‑linear combination of binomial coefficients.
proof_strategy: The conjecture is approached by induction on d. Using the height‑function reduction, a vertex of degree d corresponds to a height function with exactly d strict local extrema. For d ≤ 5 the explicit polynomial formulas are known. For larger d we decompose a height function into a connected component of extrema surrounded by a “valley” or “mountain” region, reducing the counting problem to a convolution of lower‑degree counts. This yields a recurrence that forces N_{m,n}(d) to be a polynomial in m,n. Verifying the recurrence against the known low‑degree cases and proving polynomiality via generating‑function arguments establishes the conjecture.
title: Polynomial degree sequence for all degrees in the Miura‑ori flip graph

description: The critical density γ_k must exactly equal n²/k for the phase transition to occur.
proof_strategy: explicit_calculation
title: Critical Density Determination

description: For any integer n ≥ 2, the number of irreducible FAT colorings of the complete graph on n vertices is equal to the number of positive divisors of n minus 1.
proof_strategy: Analyze the structure of FAT colorings in complete graphs, showing that each divisor d of n (excluding 1) corresponds to an irreducible FAT d-coloring where the vertex set is partitioned into d equal parts.
title: Number of Irreducible FAT Colorings in Complete Graphs

catalog_references: Observation 1: monotonicity of gamma_k^L and stabilization at ordinary domination for k >= Delta(G)
Theorem 2: general lower bound gamma_k^L(G) >= ceil(n(G)/(k+1)) via domination-edge counting
Paper results on rook graphs K_m □ K_n, viewed as the d=2 Hamming graph case
description: For every pair of integers q >= 2 and d >= 1, let H(d,q) be the d-fold Cartesian product of K_q, with vertex set Fin d -> Fin q and adjacency given by differing in exactly one coordinate. Then the (q-1)-limited domination number of H(d,q) is exactly q^(d-1). Equivalently, a single coordinate layer is optimal: gamma^{L}_{q-1}(K_q □ ... □ K_q) = q^(d-1).
domain_bridges: k-limited domination ↔ edge-boundary counting between a set and its complement
Cartesian products of complete graphs ↔ Hamming graphs
domination in Hamming graphs ↔ coding-theoretic covering layers
proof_strategy: Upper bound: fix one coordinate value, for example D = {x : x 0 = 0}. This layer has cardinality q^(d-1), dominates H(d,q), and every vertex in D has exactly q-1 neighbors outside D, so it is (q-1)-limited. Lower bound: for any (q-1)-limited dominating set D, every vertex outside D has at least one edge to D, while each vertex of D has at most q-1 edges to the complement. Hence |V \ D| <= (q-1)|D|, so q^d = |V| <= q|D|, giving |D| >= q^(d-1).
title: Layer threshold for limited domination in Hamming graphs

description: For any finite simple graph G, let Z(G) denote its standard zero forcing number and TZF(G) its transmission zero forcing number as defined in the paper. We conjecture that TZF(G) ≤ Z(G) for all graphs. Moreover, equality holds for all trees.
proof_strategy: Show that any zero forcing set B can be used as an initial set of unit‑weight vertices in the transmission process. Since each forced vertex in the classical process is forced by a unique neighbor, the same neighbor will eventually transmit enough weight to exceed the threshold, possibly requiring multiple transmission steps but never needing additional initial vertices. Formalize the transmission dynamics as a monotone process and prove by induction on the number of forced vertices that the classical forcing sequence yields a successful transmission sequence. For trees, use the leaf‑removal characterization of zero forcing sets to prove equality by constructing a minimal transmission set that matches the classical one.
title: Transmission zero forcing number is bounded above by the classical zero forcing number

description: This paper establishes improved lower bounds for the Hales-Jewett number through combinatorial line methods. The goal is to derive tight estimates by exploiting symmetry and constraint satisfaction, a task suitable for precise formalization in Lean with polynomial-size proofs.
proof_strategy: Construct a theorem with a bounded search space and verify termination via Lean's SMT solver
title: Formalizing Hales-Jewett lower bounds via symmetric coloring in Lean

catalog_references: Vertex operator algebras and symmetric functions
description: The shifted t-Schur functions indexed by strict partitions satisfy an explicit Pfaffian Giambelli formula expressing s_λ^Q(t) as a Pfaffian of Y-operator modes applied to the vacuum, generalizing the classical Schur Q-function case at t=0. Specifically, for strict partition λ = (λ₁, λ₂, ..., λ_k) with λ₁ > λ₂ > ... > λ_k ≥ 0, the formula takes the form s_λ^Q(t) = Pf[Y_{λ_i - i + j}(t) + Y_{λ_j - j + i}(t)]_{1≤i<j≤k} · vac where the Pfaffian entries are determined by the Clifford algebra structure of the odd GJZ operators.
domain_bridges: Vertex operator methods in symmetric function theory
Clifford algebra representations and spin characters
Combinatorial formulas for strict partition symmetric functions
proof_strategy: Formalize the operator construction in Lean 4, prove the Clifford algebra relation [Y_m(t), Y_n(t)]₊ = 2(-1)^mδ_{m,-n}, then establish the Pfaffian determinant formula using standard Pfaffian identities and the operator product expansion, verifying the t=0 specialization recovers the classical Schur Q-function identity.
title: Pfaffian Giambelli Formula for Shifted t-Schur Functions

description: For integers d≥2 and 0≤s≤d, let ℱ⊆[n]^{(d+1)} be a (d+1)-uniform family such that every F∈ℱ has a missing trace of size exactly s (i.e. there exists B_F⊂F with |B_F|=s and B_F∉Tr_ℱ(F)). Define  W(d,s,n) = \binom{n-1}{d} + \binom{n-2(d+1-s)-2}{2s-d-2}  when the second term is defined (otherwise treat it as 0). The conjecture states that |ℱ| ≤ W(d,s,n) for all n≥2(d+1). Moreover, equality holds precisely for the constructions given by Chao‑Xu‑Yip‑Zhang and by the recent disproof for ⌈(d+2)/2⌉≤s≤d‑1.
proof_strategy: Formalize the missing‑trace condition as a predicate on (d+1)-subsets of a finite type. Prove a compression lemma that any extremal family can be shifted to a left‑compressed one without decreasing size. Use induction on n and on s, together with the known cases s≤d/2 (proved by Chao‑Xu‑Zakharov) and s=d (trivial). For the induction step, split the family according to whether a fixed element belongs to the missing trace; apply the induction hypothesis to the link and the shadow families, and combine the resulting bounds with binomial identities. Finally, show that the construction attaining the bound matches the extremal families in the equality case.
title: Corrected Uniform Witness Bound for (d+1)-Uniform Families

description: Conjecture that for every finite poset P of size n and width w ≥ 2, the number of strict alternating cycles satisfies s_w(P) ≤ 4·(w−1)!·(n(n+w)/(2w^2))^w.
proof_strategy: Inductive counting using chain decomposition and Stirling's approximation
title: Upper bound on the number of strict alternating cycles in posets of bounded width

description: Conjecture that for any finite transitively antisymmetrically ordered set S, the nilpotent Lie algebra L(S) constructed via the incidence algebra admits a left‑invariant Ricci soliton metric whose Ricci scalar curvature equals minus the ratio of the number of comparable pairs in S to the dimension of L(S). In particular, Ric = -((#comparable_pairs S) / (dim L(S)))·g.
proof_strategy: Compute the Ricci curvature using explicit Lie bracket formulas for L(S), express it in terms of the combinatorial data of S (number of comparable pairs), and verify the resulting scalar curvature matches the conjectured formula; check counterexamples by brute force for small S.
title: Scalar curvature formula for incidence-algebra nilpotent Lie algebras

description: For RSA modulus n=p*q with primes p>q, if the private exponent d satisfies d < n^{(1+δ)/2} and a δ-fraction of the most significant bits of p+q is known, then the modulus n can be factored using a modified Wiener's continued fraction attack.
proof_strategy: Formalize the attack by combining bounds on d, δ-known bits of p+q, and continued fraction convergents of e/n to show existence of a convergent yielding φ(n), then derive p and q.
title: RSA Factorization with Partial p+q Knowledge and Small Private Exponent

description: For any odd prime p and any integer ℓ with 1 ≤ ℓ ≤ (p-1)/2, if p > 2ℓ + 1 then the maximum size of a symmetric subset S ⊆ Z_p with 0 ∉ S and Cay(Z_p, S) containing no odd cycle C_{2ℓ+1} is exactly 2⌊(p + 28 + 12)/(2(28 + 12))⌋.
proof_strategy: Use additive combinatorial tools (Cauchy-Davenport, EGZ) to bound the size of S, then construct a tight example using arithmetic progressions in Z_p.
title: Odd cycle extremal conjecture for Cayley graphs over prime cyclic groups

description: For any alpha ≥ 0 and any n ≥ 3, the H_alpha index of a binary phylogenetic tree with n leaves is uniquely minimized by the caterpillar tree and uniquely maximized by the fully balanced tree.
proof_strategy: Use induction on n, leveraging the grafting property of H_alpha to decompose the index into contributions from subtrees. Show that the caterpillar structure minimizes the index by concentrating probabilities unevenly, while the balanced tree maximizes it by distributing probabilities uniformly. Base cases (n=3,4) can be verified explicitly, and the inductive step would rely on comparing structural cases under the grafting decomposition.
title: Extremal trees for H_alpha indices

description: For any prime power q and integer h ≥ 2, let n_min(q,h,k) denote the minimum length of a nondegenerate minimal additive code of dimension k over F_{q^h}. Then the limit lim_{k→∞} n_min(q,h,k)/k exists and equals h·(q^h - 1)/(q - 1).
proof_strategy: Establish the geometric correspondence between minimal additive codes and additive strong blocking sets. Derive the asymptotic size of minimal additive strong blocking sets in PG(k-1, q) using probabilistic methods (random constructions) for the upper bound and combinatorial arguments (e.g., polynomial method or double counting) for the lower bound. Show that the constant h·(q^h - 1)/(q - 1) arises from the size of an h-projective system (i.e., PG(h-1, q)).

description:
We conjecture that for every integer n ≥ 3 and real nonzero p,q, the two hypergeometric series expansions of a root of the trinomial x^n + p x + q = 0—in powers of the discriminant D and in powers of its reciprocal—satisfy a Kummer-like transformation. Precisely, if the D‑expansion is expressed as the {}_nF_{n-1} series with parameters (a_i)_{i=1}^n and (b_j)_{j=1}^{n-1}, then there exists an identity of the form:
{}_nF_{n-1}(a_1,...,a_n; b_1,...,b_{n-1}; D) = (1-D)^γ {}_nF_{n-1}(b_1-a_1,...,b_{n-1}-a_{n-1},1; a_1,...,a_{n-1}; 1/D),
where γ = Σ_{j=1}^{n-1}(b_j - a_j) + 1 - a_n. This reduces to the classical Kummer identities for n=3 and would provide a systematic higher-order analogue for all n≥3.
proof_strategy:
1. Derive the explicit parameters (a_i,b_j) of the {}_nF_{n-1} series from the known hypergeometric representation of the roots of the trinomial in powers of the discriminant D (using the formulas from the paper).
2. Verify the conjectured transformation for small n (n=3,4,5) with computer algebra (e.g., Mathematica, Maple, or Sage) by expanding both sides as power series in D and checking equality term-by-term.
3. Once the pattern holds for these cases, use known results on higher-order Kummer transformations (e.g., Karlsson-Minton theorem) to argue that the conjectured identity follows from the general transformation theory for Saalschützian {}_nF_{n-1} series.
4. Formalise the conjecture in Lean 4: define the hypergeometric series in mathlib, encode the parameters as dependent types, and state the identity as a theorem. Use the existing hypergeometric transformation lemmas to attempt a proof, or develop new lemmas for the specific parameter shifts.
5. Aim to complete a machine-check
title: Higher-order Kummer transformation for trinomial root series

description:
For any integer parameters \(a,b,c,d\) with \(a,b,c,d\ge 0\) and any base \(q\) with \(|q|<1\), define the rank‑four Nahm sum
\[\Phi_{a,b,c,d}(q) \;:=\; \sum_{i,j,k,l\ge 0}\frac{q^{\frac12(i^2+aj^2+bk^2+cl^2)-ij-jk-kl-dj+ek+fl}}{(q;q)_i\,(q;q)_j\,(q;q)_k\,(q;q)_l} .\]
The conjecture asserts that when the coefficient matrix of the quadratic form is positive‑definite and the linear terms satisfy a certain balance condition (namely \(e=\frac{a+b}{2}\) and \(f=\frac{b+c}{2}\)), the sum collapses to a simple product of Euler functions:
\[\Phi_{a,b,c,d}(q) \;=\; C_{a,b,c,d}\, q^{\kappa_{a,b,c,d}}\,\frac{J_{m}^{\,s}}{J_{1}^{\,t}},\]
where \(J_m = (q^m; q^m)_\infty\), the exponent \(\kappa_{a,b,c,d}\) and the constants \(C_{a,b,c,d}, m, s, t\) are explicit rational functions of \(a,b,c,d\). This family contains the four identities proved in the paper as the special cases
\((a,b,c,d) = (1,0,0,2), (0,2,2,2), (1,0,0,1), (2,2,2,2)\).

**Conjecture (Precise Form).** Let \(A=\begin{pmatrix}1 & -\frac12 & 0 & -\frac12\\ -\frac12 & 1 & -\frac12 & -\frac12\\ 0 & -\frac12 & 1 & -\frac12\\ -\frac12 & -\frac12 & -\frac12 & 1\end{pmatrix}\). For any integer vector \(\mathbf{u}=(u_1,u_2,u_3,u_4)\) with \(u_i\ge 0\) define
\[\Phi_{\mathbf{u}}(q) = \sum_{i,j,k,l\ge 0} \frac{q^{\frac12\,(i,j,k,l)A(i,j,k,l)^T + \mathbf{u}\cdot(i,j,k,l)}}{(q;q)_i (q;q)_j (q;q)_k (q;q)_l}.\]
Then
\[\Phi_{\mathbf{u}}(q) = 2^{\alpha(\mathbf{u})}\, q^{\beta(\mathbf{u})}\, \frac{J_{2}^{\, \gamma(\mathbf{u})}}{J_{1}^{\, \delta(\mathbf{u})}},\]
where the integer‑valued functions \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\) are given by
\[\alpha(\mathbf{u}) = u_1+u_2+u_3+u_4 - 2,\quad \beta(\mathbf{u}) = -\frac{\lVert\mathbf{u}\rVert_1}{2},\]
\[\gamma(\mathbf{u}) = 6 - \frac{\lVert\mathbf{u}\rVert_1}{2},\quad \delta(\mathbf{u}) = 6 - \frac{\lVert\mathbf{u}\rVert_1}{2}.\]
In particular, for \(\mathbf{u} = (0,0,0,0)\) we recover the first identity of Theorem 1, and for \(\mathbf{u} = (2,2,2,2)\) we recover Theorem 2.

**Why this is falsifiable.** The statement gives an explicit closed‑form product for each \(\Phi_{\mathbf{u}}\). One can compute coefficients of the series expansion of both sides for any concrete \(\mathbf{u}\) (e.g., using SageMath or Mathematica) and check equality up to a high order in \(q\). A single counter‑example disproves the conjecture.

**Domain**: Number Theory (q‑series, modular forms) and Combinatorics.

**Domain bridges**: Connects the theory of Nahm sums (modular q‑hypergeometric series) with the classical theory of theta functions and Euler products.

**Ambition level**: "extension" – it extends the proven four identities to an infinite family.

**Proof strategy**: Use the Bailey‑pair / Bailey‑chain machinery to transform the multi‑sum into a product. The quadratic form matrix \(A\) is unimodular, enabling a change of variables that separates the sum
title: Generalized Rank‑Four Nahm Sum Identity with Quadratic Form Parameter

description: For every positive integer n, there exists a family of n+1 subsets of Fin n whose pairwise symmetric-difference distances are all (n+1)/2 if and only if n = 1 or n ≡ 3 mod 4. Equivalently, the exceptional case lambda = (n+1)/2 in Hegedus's bound is attained exactly in the Hadamard orders.
domain_bridges: binary set systems ↔ signed characteristic vectors

proof_strategy: Show equivalence with the classical Hadamard conjecture. Given such a family, convert each subset to its signed characteristic vector in {±1}^n; pairwise distance (n+1)/2 gives pairwise inner product -1, and appending an all-one coordinate yields n+1 mutually orthogonal {±1}-rows, i.e. a Hadamard matrix of order n+1. Conversely, from a normalized Hadamard matrix of order n+1, delete the all-one column and convert signs back to subsets. The necessity n=1 or n≡3 mod 4 follows from the standard Hadamard determinant/parity obstruction; the sufficiency is exactly the Hadamard conjecture.
title: Hadamard-tightness conjecture for the exceptional binary Hegedus bound

description: Let K be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p > 0, let m > 0, and let s_p(m) be the sum of the base-p digits of m. Prove the weighting obstruction theorem in Lean: if the unattacked squares of Q are covered by rational weights on rows, columns, and diagonals with total weight strictly less than n - |Q|, then Q is non-completable. Then construct, for all sufficiently large n, an explicit parametric partial configuration Q_n of at most floor(n/5) non-attacking queens together with a rational line-weighting certificate covering all squares not attacked by Q_n and having total weight < n - |Q_n|. The remaining proof obligations should be finite interval-membership and affine rational inequality checks, discharged by normalization and linarith.
title: Asymptotic one-fifth upper bound for the n-queens completion threshold

catalog_references: Hermite polynomial real-rootedness and largest-zero monotonicity
description: For n ≥ 2 define X_n(v) = ∑_{k=0}^{⌊n/2⌋} (-1)^k n! / ((n - 2k)! k!) v^k and its reciprocal polynomial Y_n(q) = q^{⌊n/2⌋} X_n(1/q). Conjecture: every root of Y_n is real, positive, and simple, and if λ_n is the largest real root of Y_n, then λ_n < λ_{n+1} for all n ≥ 2. Equivalently, for the orchard denominator D_l(v)=∏_{j=2}^l X_j(v), the exponential growth constant determined by the smallest positive zero of D_l is always λ_l, the largest reciprocal root of the final factor X_l.
domain_bridges: phylogenetic network enumeration to matching polynomials
orchard-network asymptotics to extremal zeros of orthogonal polynomials
complete graph matchings to reciprocal spectral growth constants
proof_strategy: Identify X_n with a rescaled matching polynomial of K_n, equivalently with a specialization of the Hermite polynomial. Use the Heilmann--Lieb real-rootedness theorem or the standard Hermite-polynomial zero theorem to prove that Y_n has only positive simple roots. Then use the strict interlacing of consecutive Hermite zeros to show that the largest reciprocal root λ_n is strictly increasing in n. Finally, observe that the roots of D_l are the union of the roots of the X_j factors, so monotonicity implies that the dominant reciprocal root of D_l is λ_l.
title: Dominant Orchard Denominator Root Comes from the Last Complete-Graph Matching Factor

description: In the h=1 specialization of additive strong blocking sets, i.e. ordinary strong blocking sets in PG(2,2), a finite set S of projective points is strong blocking if and only if it contains at least 6 of the 7 points. Equivalently, the shortest nondegenerate minimal binary linear code of dimension 3 has length 6 under the projective-system correspondence.
domain_bridges: minimal linear codes ↔ strong blocking sets
h=1 additive codes ↔ ordinary linear codes
proof_strategy: Represent points of PG(2,2) as 1-dimensional submodules of V = (ZMod 2)^3 and lines as 2-dimensional submodules. In the Fano plane every line has exactly 3 points and any two distinct points determine a unique line. A set S is strong blocking exactly when every line contains at least two points of S. If S is strong blocking, its complement cannot contain two points, since those two points would determine a line meeting S in only one point; hence |S| ≥ 6. Conversely, if |S| ≥ 6, every line misses at most one point, so it contains at least two points of S and therefore its intersection with S spans the line.
title: Fano-plane threshold for additive strong blocking sets in the h=1 case

description: We propose a conjecture characterizing the conditions under which the Lin-Lu-Yau Ricci curvature of an edge in a connected locally finite graph is non-negative. The conjecture posits that if the size of the symmetric difference of the neighborhoods of two adjacent vertices exceeds their common neighborhood size plus their degrees, the curvature vanishes or is non-negative. This bridges the gap between combinatorial graph metrics and curvature theory, enabling exact computation via graph structure analysis.
proof_strategy: Construct an optimal transport plan between neighborhoods using Hall's Marriage Theorem, then derive curvature bounds via integral geometry and discrete measure theory.
title: Non-negative Lin-Lu-Yau Ricci Curvature on Graphs with Common Neighborhoods

description: Conjecture that for all integers k ≥ 3 and n ≥ 1, the minimal N = g_k(n) satisfies g_k(n) ≥ ⌈((k-1)/(k-2))^n⌉.
proof_strategy: combinatorial counting argument using ternary grid bandwidth
title: Exponential Lower Bound for g_k(n) Conjecture

description: For every odd prime 𝑝 the class of biased graphs that admit a 𝑍ₚ‑gain labelling is minor‑closed and its only excluded minors are the balanced‑cycle–free graph (𝑝+1)K₂, the balanced triangle ±K₃ and the unbalanced 4‑cycle –K₄. In other words, a biased graph 𝔾 is 𝑍ₚ‑gainable iff it contains none of these three minors.
proof_strategy: Use the theory of partial groups developed in the paper to show that if a biased graph contains a minor isomorphic to (p+1)K₂ it cannot be 𝑍ₚ‑gainable. Conversely, show that any 𝑍ₚ‑gainable graph is forced to avoid the three excluded minors by reduction to the cases 𝑝=2 and 𝑝=3 and by an induction on 𝑝 using the fact that any 𝑍ₚ‑gainable graph is also 𝑍₂‑ and 𝑍₃‑gainable. The key step is to prove that every 𝑍ₚ‑gainable biased graph simultaneously satisfies the 𝑍₂‑ and 𝑍₃‑excluded minor conditions, hence satisfies the 𝑝‑excluded minor condition.
title: Excluded minors for bias graphs gainable over cyclic groups 𝑍ₚ

description: The upper bound S_1^φ(x) ≪ x exp{-(1/2 - o(1))√(log x log_2 x)} is tight, i.e., there exists a constant C > 0 such that S_1^φ(x) ≥ C x exp{-(1/2 + o(1))√(log x log_2 x)} for all sufficiently large x.
proof_strategy: Construct explicit examples of n with φ(n)=φ(n+1) achieving the lower bound, or refine the error term analysis in the existing proof
title: Tightness of the unit-shift bound for Euler's totient function

description: We conjecture that the set of positive integers that are divisible by the number of summands in their Zeckendorf decomposition has asymptotic density 0.  Equivalently, for any real ε>0 there are only finitely many Zeckendorf‑Niven numbers n< N with n/N > ε, and the ratio of the counting function to N tends to 0 as N→∞.
domain_bridges: Density of special number sets (Niven, perfect, amicable, etc.)
proof_strategy: The conjecture can be attacked by estimating the growth of the Zeckendorf summand function s_Z(n). The Zeckendorf decomposition of n can be encoded as a word over {0,1} that avoids consecutive 1s. Counting the number of such words of length L gives the number of integers with at most L Fibonacci summands. One can upper–bound s_Z(n) by a logarithmic function of n and then use a probabilistic model (e.g. a Markov chain on the Fibonacci word) to show that the probability that s_Z(n) divides n decays super‑polynomially. An analytic approach would involve Dirichlet series generating functions for the indicator of Zeckendorf‑Niven numbers and bounding its abscissa of convergence. Either route yields an upper bound for the counting function of the form O(N / log^c N) for some c>0, which implies density 0.
title: Zero Asymptotic Density of Zeckendorf‑Niven Numbers

description: For any tree T on n vertices and any complete tripartite graph K_{m_1,m_2,m_3} with 1 ≤ m_1 ≤ m_2 ≤ m_3, the Ramsey number R(T, K_{m_1,m_2,m_3}) equals 2(R(T, K_{m_1,m_2}) - 1) + m_1 for all sufficiently large n. This conjecture specifically tests whether the general bound in the paper becomes an exact equality for the k=3 case.
proof_strategy: Construct explicit red-blue colorings of K_N for N = 2(R(T, K_{m_1,m_2}) - 1) + m_1 - 1 to show they avoid both a red T and blue K_{m_1,m_2,m_3}, thereby proving the lower bound matches the upper bound from the main theorem.
title: Exact Ramsey Numbers for Trees vs Tripartite Graphs

catalog_references: Zhi-Wei Sun's catalog of universal sums of polygonal-type quadratic polynomials
Mathlib formalization targets for Nat-valued quadratic polynomial universality
description: For every nonnegative integer n, there exist natural numbers x, y, z such that n = x*(x+1)/2 + y*(3*y+1)/2 + z*(7*z+1)/2. This is the direct nonagonal analogue of the paper's triangular-pentagonal-heptagonal theorem, replacing z*(5*z+1)/2 by z*(7*z+1)/2.
domain_bridges: polygonal numbers to constrained representations by diagonal ternary quadratic forms
elementary Nat arithmetic to integral quadratic forms with congruence side conditions
computer-assisted finite descent certificates to Lean 4 formalization
proof_strategy: Use the same square-completion reduction as in the paper. The identities 8*T(x)+1=(2*x+1)^2, 24*P(y)+1=(6*y+1)^2, and 56*N(z)+1=(14*z+1)^2 transform the conjecture into: every m = 168*n + 31 is represented by Q(u,v,w)=21*u^2 + 7*v^2 + 3*w^2 with u odd, v ≡ 1 mod 6, and w ≡ 1 mod 14. A proof should first establish a primitive local-global seed for Q on the congruence class 31 mod 168, then construct rational similarities of Q giving a terminating descent to the required congruence class, with any residual finite cone discharged by exact rational/integer certificates analogous to those in the paper.
title: Triangular + second pentagonal + second nonagonal universality

description: If a quadratic polynomial $f = x^2 + c$ over $\mathbb{Q}(i)$ has an irreducible second iterate $f^2$ in $\mathbb{Q}(i)[x]$, then all subsequent iterates $f^n$ remain irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}(i)[x]$ for every $n \geq 1$.
proof_strategy: Proceed by induction on $n$, leveraging the irreducibility of $f^2$ and a new function measuring 'complexity' in $\mathbb{Q}(i)$ due to the absence of linear ordering. The base case $n=2$ is given. For the inductive step, analyze the factorization of $f^{n+1} = f^n \circ f$ using the Galois action on preimages and the tree structure of iterations, adapting techniques from \cite{evstb} to handle the two-dimensional nature of $\mathbb{Q}(i)$.
title: Irreducibility of Iterates for Quadratic Polynomials over $\mathbb{Q}(i)$

description: Conjecture that for every integer r ≥ 20, the Erdős–Lovász cover number function satisfies g(r) ≥ ⌊61r/20⌋ − 4. This strengthens the asymptotic bound g(r) ≥ (61/20 − o(1))r by providing an explicit additive constant, making the statement falsifiable for each specific r.
proof_strategy: Refine the proof of Theorem 1.2(ii) by tracking the exact loss when applying Kahn's small-codegree edge-colouring theorem and the degree‑peeling process, aiming to convert the o(1) term into a uniform additive bound of 4.
title: Conjectured additive refinement of the 61/20 lower bound for g(r)

description: For integers d ≥ 4 and s satisfying ⌈(d+2)/2⌉ ≤ s ≤ d−1, let n be sufficiently large (e.g., n ≥ 2(d+1)). If 𝔽 ⊆ ( [n] choose (d+1) ) is a (d+1)-uniform family such that every F ∈ 𝔽 has a missing trace of size exactly s (i.e., there exists B ⊂ F with |B| = s and for all F' ∈ 𝔽, F ∩ F' ≠ B), then |𝔽| ≤ binom(n−1, d) + binom(n−2(d+1−s)−2, 2s−d−2), and this bound is tight.
proof_strategy: Use shifting/compression to transform an extremal family into a left‑compressed form while preserving the missing‑trace condition. Analyze the possible traces on a fixed (d+1)-set and apply Kleitman’s theorem on intersecting families to bound the number of sets containing a given subset. Perform an induction on n, considering whether a particular element appears in all sets or not. Show that any family attaining the bound must be isomorphic to the explicit construction: take all (d+1)-sets containing a fixed d‑set, together with all (d+1)-sets that avoid a fixed (2(d+1−s)+2)-set and contain a specific (2s−d−2)-subset of its complement.
title: Optimality of the constructed family for the uniform witness conjecture in the upper range

description: All binary Type I self-dual codes of length 26 with minimum distance 6 are equivalent under permutation of coordinates.

proof_strategy: algebraic construction
title: Dimension Equality Conjecture

description: For any prime power q and integers n ≥ k ≥ 1, s ≥ 1 with n ≥ (s+1)k, let m_q(n,k,s) be the maximum size of a family of k-dimensional subspaces of 𝔽_q^n containing no s+1 members with a direct sum. The conjecture states that m_q(n,k,s) equals the maximum of two explicit constructions: all k-subspaces contained in a fixed ((s+1)k-1)-dimensional subspace, or all k-subspaces intersecting a fixed s-dimensional subspace nontrivially. This is the q-analogue of the Erdős Matching Conjecture (proven for k=2, n=(s+1)k, and large n, but open in general).
proof_strategy: The paper combines Lovász's minimax theorem for matroid matchings, a high-dimensional Hoffman bound for uniform hypergraphs, and packing-design arguments in vector spaces. For Lean formalization, one would first develop the theory of Gaussian binomial coefficients, subspace lattices, and direct sums in finite vector spaces. The known cases (k=2, n=(s+1)k, large n) could be formalized incrementally, leveraging matroid libraries and linear algebra over finite fields.
title: Vector-Space Erdős Matching Conjecture

description: For every integer k ≥ 9, the diagonal k-uniform Ramsey number r_k(k+1,k+1) is strictly larger than the 3-color shift number at parameter floor(2k/3)-3; equivalently, r_k(k+1,k+1) > s_3(⌊2k/3⌋-3). This strengthens the paper's bound r_k(k+1,k+1) > s_3(⌊k/2⌋-2) by replacing the coefficient 1/2 with 2/3, while retaining an absolute additive loss.
domain_bridges: Finite k-uniform hypergraphs represented as Finset α predicates of cardinality k
Ramsey numbers represented as least N satisfying a finite coloring property
Shift numbers represented as least N forcing a forbidden monochromatic shifted configuration under every 3-coloring
Tower-type asymptotic lower bounds reduced to explicit inequalities between Nat-valued extremal functions
proof_strategy: Generalize the construction in the paper from the floor(k/2)-2 shift parameter to a three-block or two-scale block encoding. The existing proof converts a 3-coloring witnessing s_3(t) > N into a red/blue coloring of k-subsets with no monochromatic (k+1)-set, where t is roughly k/2. The conjectural improvement would partition the k positions into three interacting zones and encode the local shift obstruction using majority/stability rules so that every candidate monochromatic (k+1)-set yields a forbidden shifted pattern of length floor(2k/3)-3. A Lean formalization would avoid asymptotics: define the finite colorings, the obstruction predicate, and prove that the transformed coloring contains no red or blue clique of size k+1.
title: Two-thirds shift-number lower bound for diagonal hypergraph Ramsey numbers

q-Pochhammer symbols and Gaussian binomial coefficients
Lean/mathlib formal power series and integer partitions
description: Let R,S,k,c be positive integers with 1 ≤ S and 2S ≤ R. Define A_{R,S}(q) = 1 / ((q^S;q^R)_∞ (q^{R-S};q^R)_∞ (q^R;q^R)_∞) and T_{R,S,k}(q) = ∑_{j=-k+1}^{k} (-1)^j q^{R*j*(j-1)/2 + S*j}. Conjecture: for every n ≥ 1, the coefficient of q^n in (-1)^(k-1) * (T_{R,S,k}(q) * A_{R,S}(q)^c - A_{R,S}(q)^(c-1)) is a nonnegative integer. Equivalently, the known Wang--Yee positivity for c=1 persists after convolution with the generating function for (c-1)-colored partitions into parts congruent to 0, S, or R-S modulo R.
domain_bridges: q-series coefficient positivity to colored partition enumeration
bilateral truncated theta sums to formal power series identities
minimal-excludant partition statistics to computable coefficient predicates in Lean
proof_strategy: First formalize the c=1 Wang--Yee identity as an equality of formal power series over ℤ, where (-1)^(k-1) * (T_{R,S,k} * A_{R,S} - 1) is represented by an explicit multiple sum with manifestly nonnegative coefficients. Then observe that A_{R,S}^{c-1} has nonnegative integer coefficients because it is the generating function for (c-1)-colored partitions into allowed residue classes. The conjectured series factors as A_{R,S}^{c-1} * ((-1)^(k-1) * (T_{R,S,k} * A_{R,S} - 1)), so coefficientwise nonnegativity follows from closure of nonnegative integer sequences under Cauchy product.
title: Colored positivity for the bilateral truncated Jacobi triple product after removing the constant term

description: Conjecture: For any integration problem satisfying the assumptions of Theorem 1 (tensor‑product structure, existence of a one‑dimensional worst‑case function h and associated spline functions s_y with A,B>1), the information complexity N_{it}^+(ε,d) grows at least exponentially with the dimension d. Formally, there exists a constant C>1 (depending only on A and B) such that for every d∈ℕ and every ε∈(0,1/2] we have N_{it}^+(ε,d) ≥ C^d. The conjecture is falsifiable: a single counterexample (d,ε) violating the inequality would refute it.
proof_strategy: Leverage the tensor‑product construction of Theorem 1: define the d‑dimensional worst‑case function h_d = ∏_{i=1}^d h(x_i) and the spline products s_y = ∏_{i=1}^d s_{y_i}(x_i). Using the properties A = inf_y I(h)/I(s_y) > 1 and B = inf_y ||h||_1/||s_y||_1 > 1, show that any non‑negative linear rule must incur an error at least (min(A,B))^d times the initial error, which yields the exponential lower bound on the information complexity.
title: Exponential lower bound for non‑negative QMC integration in high dimensions

description: Conjecture: For any field F of characteristic zero, the natural map from the weight‑3 component PolyL₃(F) of the Goncharov Lie coalgebra to the indecomposable quotient of the third‑filtered algebraic K‑theory group K₅^{(3)}(F)⊗ℚ is an isomorphism of ℚ‑vector spaces, intertwining the Lie cobracket with the boundary map in Goncharov’s polylogarithmic complex of weight 3.
proof_strategy:
1. Use the Steinberg module presentation of PolyL_*(F) to identify PolyL₃(F) as the ℚ‑vector space generated by the symbols Li₃(a) and Li_{2,1}(a,b) subject to the weight‑3 functional equations of the trilogarithm.
2. Construct a regulator map r: PolyL₃(F) → K₅^{(3)}(F)⊗ℚ via the Beilinson regulator on motivic cohomology H³_𝓜(F, ℚ(3)) and the identification of K₅^{(3)}(F)⊗ℚ with a quotient of this motivic cohomology.
3. Show r is injective by comparing weight filtrations and using the fact that the kernel would give a non‑trivial relation among polylogarithms contradicting Zagier’s conjecture (proved for number fields by Goncharov–Levin).
4. Prove surjectivity by computing dimensions: Borel’s theorem gives rank K₅^{(3)}(F)⊗ℚ = r₂(F) (the number of complex places), while the weight‑3 polylogarithmic complex has the same dimension via the known basis of Bloch‑Suslin relations; the equality of dimensions follows from the Borel regulator calculation.
5. Verify that r respects the Lie cobra
title: Isomorphism between the weight‑3 Goncharov Lie coalgebra and the indecomposable part of K₅^{(3)}(F)⊗ℚ

description: Conjecture: For any finite simple bipartite graph G with partite sets A and B, let Δ_A = max_{a∈A} deg_G(a) and Δ_B = max_{b∈B} deg_G(b). If Δ_A·Δ_B ≥ 1000 then the strong chromatic index satisfies χ'_s(G) ≤ ⌊(5/3)·Δ_A·Δ_B⌋. This would improve the current bound of 1.676·Δ_A·Δ_B for sufficiently large product and is sharp up to constant factor.
proof_strategy: Use a random edge‑coloring with (5/3)·Δ_A·Δ_B colors, then apply the Lovász local lemma to eliminate conflicts. Refine the dependency analysis by exploiting the bipartite structure to bound the number of edges at distance ≤2 from a given edge by (5/3)·Δ_A·Δ_B - 1, and use a discharging argument to handle the case when Δ_A·Δ_B is just above the threshold.
title: Improved asymptotic bound for the strong chromatic index of bipartite graphs

description: Let D_n be the average stack-sorting depth over all permutations in S_n under West's stack-sorting map. The conjecture is that the unprimed averages satisfy the same type of finite monotonicity suggested by the paper's primed lower-bound sequence: for every n ≥ 1, D_n/(n+1) ≤ D_{n+1}/(n+2). This is a concrete finite inequality at each n and can be falsified by exact enumeration of stack-sorting depths.
domain_bridges: Permutation algorithms formalized as functions on Equiv.Perm (Fin n)
Finite combinatorial averages as rational sums over Fintype
Asymptotic convergence heuristics reduced to finite monotonicity inequalities
proof_strategy: Define West's stack-sorting map on Equiv.Perm (Fin n), define depth as the least iterate reaching the identity permutation, and define D_n as the rational average over all permutations. A possible proof route is to construct a coupling or injection from permutations of size n, with suitable weights accounting for the denominator n+1, into permutations of size n+1 such that expected stack-sorting depth does not decrease after the shifted normalization. The paper's stack-sorting diagram/tableau framework may suggest a size-extension operation preserving or increasing depth in aggregate.
title: Shift-normalized monotonicity of the average stack-sorting depth

description:
For each non‑negative integer k, define
\[
P_{2k}=\prod_{n=2}^{\infty} \exp\Bigl(\frac{1}{n^{2k-1}}\Bigr)\Bigl(1-\frac{1}{n^{2}}\Bigr)^{n^{2k}}\,.
\]
The paper shows that the logarithm of P_{2k} is a finite tail of the Riemann zeta series.  We conjecture an explicit closed‑form expression involving only powers of \(\pi\), rational numbers, harmonic numbers \(H_{2k}\), and odd zeta values \(\zeta(2j+1)\).  This statement is precise, falsifiable and can be formalised in Lean 4 using the existing libraries for real analysis, the gamma function and the Riemann zeta function.
proof_strategy:
Rewrite log P_{2k} as a finite linear combination of the divergent series \(\sum_{n\ge2} n^{-s}\) with s≤1, then apply the minimal exponential counterterm to cancel the pole at s=1.  Using the Euler–Maclaurin formula one obtains
\[
\log P_{2k}=\frac{1}{2}\log\pi -\sum_{j=1}^{k}\binom{2k}{2j-1}\frac{B_{2j}}{2j}\,H_{2k-2j+1}\; +\;\sum_{j=1}^{k}\binom{2k}{2j}\frac{\zeta(2j+1)}{2j+1}\,.
\]
Exponentiating gives the conjectured closed form.  The proof in Lean would proceed by:
1. Defining the product and its logarithm via `tsum` and `log`.
2. Proving the cancellation of the non‑summable terms using `has_sum` for the tail of the zeta series.
3. Formalising the Euler–Maclaurin expansion for the harmonic numbers and Bernoulli numbers (already in Mathlib).
4. Showing the resulting series equals the right‑hand side by `ring` and `linarith` tactics.
5. Finally, using `real.exp_log` to obtain the product identity.
All intermediate lemmas (e.g., `log_one_sub_one_div_nat_sq`, `zeta_neg_one_mul_pow_tw
title: Closed form for even‑indexed regularised Wallis products

catalog_references: Brown--Erdos--Sos conjecture for sparse local configurations
description: For every fixed r >= 3 and k >= 3, every linear r-uniform hypergraph H on n vertices with no collection of k edges spanning at most (r - 2)k + 3 vertices has o(n^2) edges. Equivalently: for every rational epsilon > 0 there is N such that for all n >= N, if H is linear and r-uniform on Fin n and every k-edge subfamily spans more than (r - 2)k + 3 vertices, then |E(H)| <= epsilon n^2. This would replace the paper's positive constant-density forcing threshold by the conjectural Brown--Erdos--Sos vanishing threshold in the linear setting.
domain_bridges: Represent a finite r-uniform hypergraph on n vertices as Finset (Finset (Fin n)).
Express linearity by pairwise edge intersections having cardinality at most 1.
Express a forbidden ((r-2)k+3,k)-configuration by quantifying over k-cardinality Finsets of edges and bounding the cardinality of their Finset.biUnion.
Encode the asymptotic o(n^2) statement using rational epsilon-N quantifiers, avoiding real analysis if desired.
proof_strategy: A plausible route is to formalize the local averaging inequality from the paper as a reusable finite lemma, then combine it with iterative density increment or hypergraph removal-type arguments specialized to linear r-uniform systems. For r=3,k=3 this should connect to the Ruzsa--Szemeredi theorem; for general k one would seek a Lean-formalizable induction on k tracking the number of pairwise edge intersections inside small edge subfamilies. The conjecture is falsifiable by any explicit infinite-density family of linear r-uniform hypergraphs avoiding k edges on at most (r-2)k+3 vertices.
title: Linear Brown--Erdos--Sos o(n^2) conjecture at the paper's span threshold
