proof_strategy: Construct explicit $q$-series transforming objects and verify convergence using the Farkas–Hintikka system.
title: Analytic Verification of Modular Rank-Four Nearest-Point Identities

description: Every nonnegative integer n can be expressed as T(x) + P₁(y) + H₁(z), where T(x) = x(x+1)/2 is the x-th triangular number, P₁(y) = y(3y-1)/2 is the y-th first pentagonal number, and H₁(z) = z(5z-3)/2 is the z-th first heptagonal number, for nonnegative integers x, y, z.
proof_strategy: Adapt the proof techniques from the original paper, potentially involving transformations to a quadratic form and checking congruence conditions, but with modified coefficients for the first pentagonal and heptagonal numbers.
title: Every Nonnegative Integer Is a Sum of a Triangular, First Pentagonal, and First Heptagonal Number

description: All non-trivial zeros of the scattering determinant φ(s) associated to congruence characters of congruence subgroups of SL₂(ℤ) lie on the critical line Re(s) = 1/2. This conjecture, if true, would imply that the prime geodesic theorem for congruence subgroups holds with exponent 1/2 + ε, improving upon the proven exponent 25/36 + ε. The conjecture is falsifiable by exhibiting any zero ρ with |Re(ρ) - 1/2| > δ for some explicit δ > 0.
proof_strategy: Establish the conjecture by proving that the scattering determinant φ(s) satisfies a functional equation relating φ(s) and φ(1-s), and then applying techniques from the theory of automorphic L-functions to show all non-trivial zeros lie on the critical line. Counterexamples would involve computing the zeros numerically to sufficient precision and verifying their real parts differ from 1/2.
title: Scattering Determinant Critical Line Conjecture

catalog_references: Liu's work on finite height representations
description: We conjecture that if a p-adic Galois representation becomes semistable after passing to some finite extension, then it must already have been of finite E-height. This would provide a characterization of finite height representations in terms of their behavior under finite extensions.
proof_strategy: Assume that V_L is semistable for some finite extension L/K. Use the classification of semistable representations via (phi, Gamma)-modules or Breuil-Kisin modules to show that V must be finite height. This involves relating the structure of V_L to V and leveraging the compatibility under base change.
title: A Converse to Finite Height Implying Semistability for p-adic Galois Representations

description: Under the Exponential Time Hypothesis, there exists no deterministic algorithm solving Global Label Min-Cut on n-vertex graphs with p labels in time (np)^{o(log n / log log n)}. More precisely, any deterministic reduction from sparse 3-SAT with N variables to balanced Multicolored Clique with k color classes over q vertices, where k = Θ(sqrt(N/log N)) and log q = Θ(k log k), yields a GLMC instance with p = kq labels and n = O(k²q² log(q+1)^k) vertices satisfying log n = Θ(k log k) and consequently (log n)/(log log n) = Θ(k). This precise parameter relationship is necessary and sufficient for the lower bound to hold.
proof_strategy: Formalize the deterministic reduction construction from sparse 3-SAT to GLMC in Lean, proving the exact parameter relationships: (1) Show that sparse 3-SAT instances with N variables can be reduced to balanced MCC instances with parameters k and q satisfying the specified Θ-relations; (2) Prove that the partition lattice-based construction yields GLMC instances with exactly p = kq labels and n = O(k²q² log(q+1)^k) vertices; (3) Demonstrate that these parameter choices force log n = Θ(k log k) and (log n)/(log log n) = Θ(k); (4) Establish the correctness of the pointed partition disjunctive composition for preserving the disconnectivity property; (5) Prove that violating the time bound would yield a 2^{o(N)}-time algorithm for sparse 3-SAT, contradicting ETH.
title: ETH-based Reduction from Sparse 3-SAT to Global Label Min-Cut with Optimal Parameter Scaling

description: For every dimension d and every positive integer n, any point p in the standard d-simplex in Euclidean space R^(d+1) is within Euclidean distance sqrt(d+1)/(2n) of some barycentric grid point with denominator n, i.e. of some vector k/n where k_i are natural numbers summing to n. This is a deterministic finite-dimensional approximate Carathéodory statement for the vertex set of the regular simplex, strengthening the usual O(1/sqrt(n)) empirical bound to an O(1/n) covering bound in this special geometry.
domain_bridges: Approximate Carathéodory theory ↔ deterministic rounding of probability vectors
Euclidean simplex covering estimates ↔ mesh contraction estimates for Delaunay refinement
Finite-dimensional convex geometry ↔ Lean formalization of EuclideanSpace over Fin index types
proof_strategy: Scale the barycentric coordinates by n to obtain a nonnegative real vector q with integer total sum n. Let a_i = floor(q_i) and let f_i = q_i - a_i. Since the sum of the f_i is an integer r, choose exactly r indices with largest fractional parts and round those coordinates up, rounding all others down. This gives natural numbers k_i summing to n. The Euclidean error is n^{-1} times the L2 rounding error. It remains to prove the finite rounding inequality: for any fractional vector f_i in [0,1] with integer sum, the minimum over such balanced floor/ceiling roundings of sum_i (q_i-k_i)^2 is at most (d+1)/4. This follows by choosing the r largest f_i and bounding each optimal rounding contribution by the extremal value of the associated separable quadratic under the integer-sum constraint.
title: Uniform barycentric grid covering radius of the standard Euclidean simplex

description: Conjecture that every outerplanar graph admits a conflict‑free coloring with at most three colors. This extends the known four‑color conflict‑free bound for planar graphs and would yield a tight bound for the outerplanar subclass.
proof_strategy: Use induction on the number of vertices and the fact that outerplanar graphs are 2‑degenerate. Remove a vertex of degree ≤2, apply the induction hypothesis to obtain a 3‑color conflict‑free coloring of the remaining graph, then extend the coloring to the removed vertex by recoloring at most a bounded number of neighbors. A discharging argument guarantees that the recoloring step never requires a fourth color.
title: Conflict-Free Coloring of Outerplanar Graphs with Three Colors

description: Conjecture that for every integer n ≥ 2, any collection of mutually orthogonal Italian squares of order n contains at most n‑1 squares, and this bound is attained exactly when n is a prime power.
proof_strategy: Establish an upper bound via double counting of symbol occurrences and use finite field constructions to exhibit n‑1 orthogonal squares when n is a prime power; then formalize the combinatorial arguments in Lean using existing libraries for finite fields and finite sets.
title: Maximum size of pairwise orthogonal Italian squares is n‑1 for prime powers

description: Let X be a K3 surface over a finite field 𝔽_q of characteristic ≠ p. Let k_n = 𝔽_{q^{p^n}} and let Br(X_{k_n})[p^∞] denote the p‑primary part of the Brauer group. Write Γ = Gal(k_∞/k) ≅ ℤ_p and Λ = ℤ_p[[Γ]]. Let M = varprojlim_n Br(X_{k_n})[p^∞]^∨ be the Pontryagin dual, a compact Λ‑module. Conjecture: M is a finitely generated torsion Λ‑module and its characteristic power series f_M(T) ∈ Λ equals, up to a unit in Λ, the p‑adic L‑function L_p(T, X) defined from the Frobenius eigenvalues on H^2_et(X_{̅𝔽_q}, ℚ_p(1)).
proof_strategy: Use the Artin–Tate conjecture (known for K3 surfaces) to identify the p‑primary Brauer group with a subquotient of étale cohomology. Prove a Mazur‑style control theorem for the tower Br(X_{k_n})[p^∞] to show that M is a finitely generated torsion Λ‑module. Construct a p‑adic L‑function via the Frobenius action on H^2_et and the theory of overconvergent modular symbols (or via Perrin‑Riou's big exponential map). Finally, compare the characteristic ideal of M with the p‑adic L‑function using an Euler system built from norm‑compatible classes in the Brauer groups of finite level (e.g., using Kummer classes of rational points on associated elliptic fibrations) to obtain divisibility in both directions, hence equality up to a unit.
title: Iwasawa Main Conjecture for Brauer groups of K3 surfaces over finite fields

catalog_references: Infinite products in formal power series
description: For integers b >= 2 and m >= 2, let T_{b,m}(n) be the coefficient of x^n in the formal power series product \prod_{i=0}^{\infty} (1 - x^{b^i})^m. Equivalently, T_{b,m}(n) is the coefficient of x^n in the finite polynomial product \prod_{i=0}^{n} (1 - x^{b^i})^m. The conjecture is that the integer sequence n \mapsto T_{b,m}(n) is unbounded in absolute value: for every B, there exists n such that |T_{b,m}(n)| > B. The paper proves the case b = 2; this conjecture asserts the same phenomenon for every base b >= 2.
domain_bridges: Combinatorics on words via digit-sum and base-b expansions
Algebraic formal power series via coefficient extraction from polynomial truncations
p-adic methods via valuations of recursively defined coefficient sequences
Analytic number theory via growth and unboundedness of coefficient sequences
proof_strategy: Define T_{b,m}(n) by finite truncation, since factors with b^i > n cannot affect the coefficient of x^n. The functional equation F_{b,m}(x) = (1 - x)^m F_{b,m}(x^b) gives a finite recurrence expressing T_{b,m}(bn + r) in terms of nearby earlier coefficients. For b > m, one can already obtain explicit exponentially large values by taking n with many base-b digits equal to 1, where no carrying occurs. The difficult range b <= m should be attacked by adapting the paper's algebraic and p-adic method: encode the coefficient recurrence by a finite family of integer matrices indexed by residues modulo b, then prove that some explicitly constructible product has spectral or p-adic growth greater than 1, forcing unboundedness.
title: Generalized Gawron–Miska–Ulas unboundedness for arbitrary integer bases

description: Conjecture: For every even integer n ≥ 4, there exists a maximal standard social decision frame whose incoherence index (the length of the shortest perfectly balanced sequence of majority or tie sets) equals n. This would strengthen the known result that incoherence indices are unbounded by showing that every sufficiently large even number is actually attained.
proof_strategy: Use an algebraic construction based on orthogonal vectors in ℚ^d to encode voting blocs. For a given even n=2k+2, build a family of half-sized subsets corresponding to vectors with pairwise zero dot product, then extend to a maximal frame by adding complementary choices for all remaining subsets of size n/2. Verify that any perfectly balanced sequence of majority/tie sets must have length at least n, and exhibit a sequence of length exactly n, establishing the incoherence index.
title: Realization of all even incoherence indices ≥4 by maximal standard frames

description: We conjecture a Rogers-Ramanujan type identity for a sum over four variables with denominators involving (q^4; q^4)_n, expressed as a product involving J_4^3 and J_1^3. This extends the pattern observed in Theorem~2 of the referenced paper to a higher modulus.
proof_strategy: Apply the lift-dual operation to modular rank three Nahm sums adapted for modulus 4, then use the method of false infinite product series and modular equations as in the referenced paper.
title: Conjecture on Modular Rank Four Nahm Sums with Modulus 4

description: For the polynomial R_g(t) defined in the main theorem, when expressed as R_g(t) = Σ_{j=0}^{g-1} a_j·t^j, each coefficient a_j ∈ ℚ has a specific closed-form expression involving generalized Catalan numbers and Bernoulli numbers. Specifically, a_j = ((-1)^j · B_{2j} · C_{g,j})/(2j)! · 2^{4j-g} where C_{g,j} is the j-th generalized Catalan coefficient arising from the Laurent expansion of csc^(2g-2)(z), and this formula yields R_g(t) with rational coefficients that satisfy the integrality condition: 2^g · R_g(p^2) ∈ ℤ for all primes p.
proof_strategy: 1) Formalize the Laurent expansion of csc^(2g-2)(z) and extract coefficients C_{g,j} = [z^{-2j}]csc^(2g-2)(z). 2) Prove that these coefficients satisfy the generalized Catalan number recurrence relation, making them computable integers. 3) Establish the closed-form expression for a_j using Bernoulli number theory and the explicit csc expansion. 4) Verify the integrality condition by showing 2^g · R_g(t) ∈ ℤ[t] through Bernoulli number divisibility properties. 5) Implement algorithmic computation of R_g(t) for small g values to verify against known cases (g=2,3).
title: Explicit Rational Coefficients of Generalized Verschiebung Degree Polynomial

catalog_references: Mazur, J. (1972). "Rational points of elliptic curves". Inventiones Mathematicae.
description: Conjecture that for any K3 surface X over a number field K, the p-primary part of the Brauer group Sel_B(X/K_∞) is a finitely generated torsion Λ-module over the Iwasawa algebra Λ = ℤ_p[[Γ]] where Γ ≅ ℤ_p.
proof_strategy: Apply Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence to the Galois extension K_∞/K, identify the p‑primary Brauer Selmer group with a cohomology group of the Iwasawa algebra, prove finiteness of cohomology in the tower using boundedness results, and deduce torsion via degree arguments.
title: Finitely generated torsion conjecture for the p-primary Brauer group of K3 surfaces in ℤ_p-cyclotomic extensions

description: For any integer m ≥2, the coefficients t_m(2^k) of the generalized Prouhet-Thue-Morse function F_m(x) grow exponentially in k. Specifically, there exist constants C >0 and r >1 such that for all sufficiently large k, |t_m(2^k)| ≥ C*r^k.
proof_strategy: Use induction on k combined with the functional equation to establish a recursive lower bound, leveraging the p-adic analytic methods from the original paper.
title: Exponential Growth of Coefficients at Powers of Two for Generalized Prouhet-Thue-Morse Series

description: For the family of radical number fields K_n(p) = Q(ζ_{p-1}, \sqrt[p]{p}) where p is an odd prime and n = p-1, the minimal index satisfies Ind_min(K_n(p)) > log(log(discriminant(K_n(p))))^{1/3} for all sufficiently large p. This provides an explicit quantitative version of the main theorem about arbitrarily large minimal indices.
proof_strategy: Use the Chebotarev density theorem to control the splitting behavior of primes in the radical extensions, combine with explicit discriminant formulas for the constructed fields, and apply lower bounds for L-functions to derive the logarithmic growth rate of the minimal index relative to the discriminant.
title: Explicit lower bound for minimal index in radical extensions

description: For any two words u and v over an alphabet α and any repetition-free word z over a disjoint alphabet β, append z as a common suffix using the tagged alphabet α ⊕ β. Then every common t-deletion descendant of map inl u ++ map inr z and map inl v ++ map inr z has a unique split into a common i-deletion descendant of u and v and a (t-i)-deletion descendant of z. Consequently the intersection size is exactly the binomial convolution ∑_{i=0}^t |D_i(u) ∩ D_i(v)| * choose(|z|, t-i). This would formalize the seed-lifting mechanism behind the paper's asymptotic attainability claims and gives an exact finite-N polynomial identity over a separated extension alphabet.
proof_strategy: Prove a unique decomposition lemma for subsequences of tagged concatenations: any subsequence of (u.map Sum.inl ++ z.map Sum.inr) splits uniquely as a Sum.inl-prefix coming from a subsequence of u followed by a Sum.inr-suffix coming from a subsequence of z. Apply this simultaneously to the two centers. If the total number of deletions is t and i deletions occur in the α-part, then t-i deletions occur in the β-part. The tagged alphabets make cross-boundary alignments impossible, and Nodup z implies |D_k(z)| = choose z.length k. Summing over i gives the claimed exact convolution.
title: Exact separator-suffix convolution for deletion-ball intersections

description: For every integers r ≥ 3 and k ≥ 3 there exist arbitrarily large linear r‑uniform hypergraphs on n vertices with edge count just below the bound given in Theorem 1 that contain no ((r‑2)k+3, k)‑configuration. In other words, the density threshold in Theorem 1 is sharp up to lower‑order terms.
proof_strategy: Construct explicit families of linear r‑uniform hypergraphs (e.g. using finite projective planes, affine geometries, or suitable random constructions) whose edge count meets the bound in Theorem 1 minus an arbitrarily small ε. Prove combinatorially that these hypergraphs avoid any ((r‑2)k+3, k)‑configuration by analysing intersection patterns of edges and counting arguments. The construction should show that any attempt to exceed this edge count would force the existence of the forbidden configuration, thereby proving the bound in Theorem 1 is tight.
title: Optimality of the Density Threshold for Linear r‑Uniform Hypergraphs

description: Conjecture that there exists a deterministic algorithm solving the Global Label Min-Cut (GLMC) problem on any undirected graph with n vertices and p labels in time O((np)^{C·log n / log log n}) for some absolute constant C.
proof_strategy: The conjectured upper bound can be approached by extending the partition‑lattice dynamic programming techniques used for hypergraph min‑cut.  One would encode the connectivity of the union of label graphs as lattice elements and propagate partial solutions using fast zeta transforms on the lattice.  By carefully arranging the recursion depth to be O(log n / log log n) and applying a logarithmic‑depth divide‑and‑conquer on the label set, the total number of DP states can be bounded by (np)^{O(log n / log log n)}.  A full formal proof would involve defining the lattice, proving its size bound, and showing that the DP recurrence respects the GLMC objective.  The crux is to avoid an exponential blow‑up in the number of subsets of labels by exploiting the lattice’s Möbius inversion to compute union‑connectivity in quasi‑linear time per layer.
title: Polynomial-Logarithmic Time Algorithm for Global Label Min-Cut

description: Conjecture that each Delaunay refinement with minicenter Steiner points reduces the maximum simplex diameter by a constant factor λ > 1, leading to exponential contraction after k iterations: max{σ ∈ Del(X_k)}.diameter ≤ (1/λ)^k · max{σ ∈ Del(X_0)}.diameter
proof_strategy: Formalize covering estimates via pivotal sampling and the dimension-dependent Carathéodory theorem to bound diameter decay per refinement step
title: Exponentialdiameter contraction under Delaunay minicenter refinement

description: For every ε > 0, there exists a constant c_ε > 0 such that the number of ordered pairs S(x) = #{(a,b) ∈ ℕ² : a + b ≤ x, σ(a) + σ(b) = σ(a+b)} satisfies S(x) > c_ε x (log x)^(2+ε) for all sufficiently large x. This is a specific instance of the main theorem where the growth rate exceeds x (log x)^2.
proof_strategy: Adapt the construction in the paper to establish a quantitative lower bound for R=2+ε, leveraging the two-height core theorem and coprime multiplier amplification. Formalize the asymptotic estimate in Lean using bounds on prime distribution in arithmetic progressions.
title: Specific Growth Rate Conjecture for Erdős Problem 1061

description: We conjecture that for any prime p>11, the superspecial K3 surface X over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p does not admit any non‑trivial extension of a maximal symplectic group. Precisely, if G≤ Aut(X) is a finite group whose symplectic subgroup G_s is maximal (as classified by Ohashi‑Schütt) then G = G_s, i.e. the non‑symplectic index [G:G_s] equals 1.
domain_bridges: Finite group actions on K3 surfaces
Symplectic automorphism groups in positive characteristic
Formal verification of arithmetic geometry statements
proof_strategy: Combine the classification of maximal symplectic groups (Ohashi‑Schütt) with the lattice‑theoretic constraints on non‑symplectic automorphisms of superspecial K3 surfaces (trace formulas, Artin invariant 1). Show that any non‑trivial extension would give a non‑symplectic element whose fixed locus forces a contradiction with the known list of possible finite subgroups of Aut(X). The tame case theorem (Section TameCase) rules out tame extensions, and the wild case is handled by examining the p‑torsion in the Néron‑Severi lattice.
title: No non‑trivial extensions of maximal symplectic groups on the superspecial K3 surface

catalog_references: Mathlib: Nat.choose, Finset.sum, finite multisets as partitions
description: For every integer k >= 2 and n >= 0, let A_k(n) be the sum over all ordinary partitions λ of n of binom(mex(λ) + k - 2, k - 1), where mex(λ) is the smallest positive integer not appearing as a part of λ. The conjecture is that A_k(n) equals the finite triangular convolution sum over j >= 0 with T_j = j(j+1)/2 <= n of binom(j + k - 2, k - 2) p(n - T_j), where p is the ordinary partition function. For k = 2 this specializes to the classical σmex triangular-sum form underlying the Andrews-Newman identity σmex(n) = D_2(n).
domain_bridges: mex statistics on ordinary partitions to triangular-number shifted partition convolutions
k-color mex-weighted partition functions to binomial coefficient weights
q-series generating functions to finite combinatorial bijections
proof_strategy: Use the hockey-stick identity binom(m+k-2,k-1) = sum_{j=0}^{m-1} binom(j+k-2,k-2). After expanding the mex weight, count triples consisting of a partition λ of n and an index j with j < mex(λ). The condition j < mex(λ) is equivalent to saying that λ contains every part 1,2,...,j at least once. Removing one copy of each of these parts gives a bijection with ordinary partitions of n - T_j, where T_j = j(j+1)/2. Summing the remaining binomial weight over all admissible j gives the stated formula.
title: Mex-binomial weights equal a triangular partition convolution

description: For every natural number k there exists a maximal standard social decision frame whose shortest coherence violation has length exactly 2k+2, showing that the incoherence index of such frames is not bounded by any uniform finite constant.
domain_bridges: social choice theory ↔ finite additive measures
combinatorial geometry ↔ rational vector space orthogonality
proof_strategy: Construct, for each k, a maximal standard frame using symmetric half-sized voting blocs arranged in orthogonal rational vector subspaces, guaranteeing that any coherence violation must involve at least 2k+2 sets.
title: Unbounded Incoherence Index in Maximal Standard Social Decision Frames

description: For all integers r ≥ 3, k ≥ 3, and n ≥ (r-2)(k-2)+1, there exists a linear r-uniform hypergraph H on n vertices with |E(H)| = [(k-2)/(r²((r-2)(k-2)+1))n² + n/r] - 1, which does not contain k edges spanning at most (r-2)k+3 vertices. This conjectures that the bound in the main theorem is tight.
proof_strategy: Construct a family of hypergraphs achieving the threshold edge count minus one while avoiding the forbidden configuration, or prove non-existence via contradiction. This requires detailed combinatorial analysis of linear hypergraph structures and their edge distributions.
title: Tightness of the density threshold in the main theorem for linear hypergraphs

description: It is impossible to replace the coherence criterion for strict majority representability by any bounded finite fragment in finite social decision frames. For every k ≥ 1, there exists a maximal standard frame whose shortest coherence violation has length 2k+2, proving no uniform finite bound exists on incoherence indices.
proof_strategy: Construct explicit maximal frames with increasing incoherence indices via orthogonal half-spaces in rational vector spaces, then show all shorter obstructions are excluded
title: Non-Finite-Axiomatization of Measurable Majorities via the Incoherence Index

description: For every nonnegative integer n, there exist natural numbers x, y, z such that n = T(x) + P(y) + H(z) and max(x, y, z) ≤ ⌊√(2n)⌋, where T(x)=x(x+1)/2, P(y)=y(3y+1)/2, H(z)=z(5z+1)/2.
proof_strategy: Use the circle method to show that the singular series is positive and the singular integral gives a main term of order n^{1/2}. Then apply a sieve to extract a representation with variables bounded by √(2n). The bound follows from size estimates: if any variable exceeds √(2n) then its corresponding term exceeds n, forcing the others to be zero, which can be checked directly.
title: Bounded variables representation for triangular-pentagonal-heptagonal sums

catalog_references: A Simple Counting Argument for Dense Linear Hypergraphs (arXiv:2408.06542)
Santos and Tyomkyn, On the Brown-Erdős-Sós problem for linear hypergraphs (arXiv:2408.06542)
description: The paper proves that any linear 3-uniform hypergraph on n vertices with linear density at least 4/9 + o(1) contains a (7,4)-configuration (i.e., 4 edges spanning at most 7 vertices). It is conjectured that this bound is asymptotically tight: for every ε > 0, there exist arbitrarily large linear 3-uniform hypergraphs with linear density at least 4/9 - ε that avoid (7,4)-configurations. This would mean the constant 4/9 cannot be improved in general.
proof_strategy: Use the probabilistic method (e.g., random linear hypergraph constructions) or algebraic constructions (e.g., finite geometry) to exhibit linear 3-uniform hypergraphs with density approaching 4/9 from below that contain no (7,4)-configurations. Alternatively, adapt known constructions for linear hypergraphs avoiding dense configurations, such as those derived from projective planes or product constructions.
title: Asymptotic Tightness of the 4/9 Density Threshold for (7,4)-Configurations in Linear Triple Systems

description: Every planar graph admits a conflict-free coloring with four colors. This is equivalent to the Four Color Theorem and provides an upper bound on the conflict-free chromatic number for planar graphs.
proof_strategy: Leverage the Four Color Theorem and structural decomposition techniques (Gallai-Edmonds variant) to construct a conflict-free 4-coloring for any planar graph. The proof requires formalizing the equivalence between conflict-free colorings and proper colorings in planar graphs.
title: Conflict-Free Chromatic Number of Planar Graphs is Bounded by Four

description: For every k≥1, we construct a maximal standard frame where the shortest coherence violation sequence has precisely length 2k+2. This disproves the existence of a universal finite bound on coherence violations across all standard frames, resolving Moss and Pedersen's Conjecture 5.7 via a geometric construction in rational vector spaces.
proof_strategy: Constructs an infinite family of frames via geometric methods, bounding minimal coherence violation lengths to demonstrate non-uniform coherence complexity across frame sizes.
title: The incoherence index of social decision frames cannot be bounded uniformly across all frame sizes

description: Let Q(u, v, w) = 15u^2 + 5v^2 + 3w^2. For any integer m such that m ≡ 23 (mod 120), there exist integers u, v, w such that Q(u, v, w) = m, where u is odd, v ≡ 1 (mod 6), and w ≡ 1 (mod 10).
proof_strategy: The proof would require formalizing the genus-theoretic properties of the quadratic form Q, specifically showing that the genus of Q contains only two classes and using the Hasse-Minkowski theorem to establish local representation, then applying the descent method (as described in the paper) to ensure the specific congruence constraints on u, v, and w are satisfied.
title: Universality of Ternary Quadratic Forms for Specific Congruence Classes

description: This conjecture formalizes the result from the paper, asserting that for any congruence subgroup Γ of SL₂(ℤ) and any non-trivial congruence character χ, the error term in the prime geodesic theorem satisfies |π_Γ(X; χ) - MainTerm| ≤ C X^{25/36 + ε} for any ε > 0, where C is a constant depending on Γ, χ, and ε. Here, π_Γ(X; χ) counts primitive conjugacy classes in Γ with trace > 2 and norm ≤ X, weighted by χ, and MainTerm represents the expected asymptotic contribution from the principal part of the explicit formula.
domain_bridges: Reduction of geodesic counting to spectral theory via the explicit formula
Connection between Maass form eigenvalues and error term exponents
Trace formula techniques in arithmetic dynamics
proof_strategy: Adapt the explicit formula approach from the paper, bounding contributions from: (1) poles of the scattering determinant, (2) cuspidal Maass forms via spectral theory, and (3) possible residual spectrum. Use the meromorphic continuation of the Dirichlet series D(s) and estimate integrals over vertical lines in the critical strip, leveraging the assumption that all non-trivial zeros satisfy Re(ρ) < 25/36 + ε.
title: Exponent bound in the Chebotarev geodesic theorem for SL₂(ℤ) congruence subgroups

description: This conjecture posits that under certain algebraic and geometric constraints, the semistability condition manifests in a new context involving analytic prismal $F$-crystals, thereby providing a bridge between classical height theory and modern adelic methods.
proof_strategy: Use the analytic framework of algebraic prismatic $F$-crystals combined with refined purity criteria to extend Du-Liu-Moon-Shimizu's result locally and globally.
title: Semistability of finite height Galois representations relative to analytic prismitals

description: We conjecture that for Reed-Muller code conversion in the merge regime, when the write cost meets the lower bound derived from generalized Hamming weights (as shown in the paper), the read cost for both initial blocks also achieves the corresponding lower bound under the same parameter conditions. Specifically, for Reed-Muller codes with parameters $(m, r)$ converted to $(m', r')$ in the Plotkin decomposition framework, if the write cost is tight, then the read cost bound must also be tight for both initial blocks. This would resolve the gap noted in the paper where one block's read cost analysis is sharp but the other remains unaccounted for.
proof_strategy: Leverage the Plotkin decomposition structure for Reed-Muller codes to construct explicit conversion algorithms that simultaneously optimize both read and write costs. Analyze the generalized Hamming weight hierarchy to establish a bijective correspondence between the bounds and achievable costs, focusing on parameter regimes where nontrivial weight jumps occur.
title: Read Cost Tightness for Reed-Muller Code Conversion in the Merge Regime

description: For a non‑negative homogeneous convex function \(p\) and a non‑negative homogeneous convex function \(q\) on a finite‑dimensional real Banach space \(X\), consider the ratio function \(f = p/q\) (defined on \(\{x \mid q(x)>0\}\)). The conjecture asserts that the sublevel sets of \(f\) and of its polarity dual \(f^\circ\) are homeomorphic after an explicit linear transformation given by the polarity map. Consequently, their reduced homology groups are isomorphic in all degrees, establishing a precise topological duality that underlies the critical‑point Morse equivalence proved in the paper.
proof_strategy: 1. Formalize the polarity map \(\mathcal P : X \to X^*\) as a linear isomorphism induced by the dual norm. 2. Show that for any \(c>0\), the sublevel set \(\{x\mid p(x)/q(x) \le c\}\) is the image under \(\mathcal P^{-1}\) of the sublevel set of the dual ratio \(\{\phi\mid p^\circ(\phi)/q^\circ(\phi) \le c\}\). 3. Use the fact that \(\mathcal P\) is a homeomorphism to deduce a homeomorphism of sublevel sets. 4. Invoke the existing Lean theorem `homeomorph.induced_homology_eq` to obtain isomorphism of reduced homology groups. 5. Assemble the result into a statement about Morse critical groups being preserved under polarity duality.
title: Duality of Sublevel Set Homotopy Types for RC Functions on Finite‑Dimensional Banach Spaces

description: In any finite game satisfying the path independence condition (PI), any two exact potentials differ by a constant. This follows because the unilateral move graph is connected and the potential differences are path-independent.
proof_strategy: Fix a reference profile s₀. For any two exact potentials P and Q, show that P(s) - Q(s) = P(s₀) - Q(s₀) for all s by considering a path of unilateral moves from s₀ to s and using the exact potential property. The path independence condition ensures the difference is well-defined.
title: Uniqueness of Exact Potential up to Additive Constant

description: Analyzes contraction bounds in spherical Delaunay refinement using an exact Carathéodory-type result.
proof_strategy: dimensional analysis and covering theorems
title: Sharp approximate Carathéodory theorem and application to iterated Delaunay refinement

description: For any positive integer k, if G is a signed graph embedded on the projective plane where all faces have length k and are positive, then the circular chromatic number of G is either at most 2 or at least 2k/(k-2). In other words, the interval (2, 2k/(k-2)) is excluded from the possible values of the circular chromatic number.
proof_strategy: Adapt the winding number framework from the paper to characterize continuous extensions of circular colorings for signed graphs, establishing topological obstructions that enforce the chromatic gap.
title: Circular Chromatic Number Gap for Signed Graphs with Positive Faces

catalog_references: Deb26:On families of integral power series
description: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p. For a one-dimensional formal group F over K of arbitrary height h, we conjecture that if the multiplication-by-n endomorphisms [n]_F have coefficients in O_K for all integers n and the Weierstrass degree of [p]_F is p^h, then F itself has coefficients in O_K. This extends the height-one case proven in the paper to higher heights, suggesting a general equivalence between integrality of endomorphisms and the formal group under height constraints.
domain_bridges: p-adic Hodge theory and formal group integrality
commuting power series families and reconstruction
proof_strategy: Extend the p-adic Hodge-theoretic methods used in the height-one case to higher heights, analyzing the structure of [p]_F and its iterates to bound the denominators of F's coefficients. Investigate whether the stability conditions from Lubin's dynamical systems framework generalize to enforce integrality in higher heights.
title: Integrality of Higher Height Formal Groups via Endomorphism Conditions

description: Conjecture that for the superspecial K3 surface in characteristic p>11, any maximal symplectic subgroup Gs (as classified by Ohashi–Schütt) cannot be properly extended by a non‑symplectic finite group; i.e., the non‑symplectic index [G:Gs] must be 1 for every faithful action.
proof_strategy: Combine the classification of finite symplectic groups on superspecial K3 surfaces (Ohashi–Schütt) with the known constraints on the Néron‑Severi lattice of a supersingular K3. Show that any non‑symplectic element would induce a pseudo‑reflection on the lattice of order dividing p, contradicting the maximality of Gs. Use character theory and the fact that the presence of a non‑trivial non‑symplectic element forces a decomposition of the Picard group that cannot coexist with the unique maximal symplectic subgroup structure.
title: Nontrivial extensions of maximal symplectic groups on superspecial K3 surfaces do not exist

description:
For every integer A ≥ 2, the sum over all partitions λ of n of the smallest multiple of A that does not occur as a part of λ equals the number of A‑color partitions of n into distinct parts.  Formally, letting mexA0(A,λ) denote the least non‑negative integer m such that m≡0 (mod A) and m∉λ, and letting D_A^dist(n) denote the number of partitions of n whose parts are distinct and each part is coloured with one of A colours, we conjecture that
\[\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}\mathrm{mexA0}(A,\lambda)=D_A^dist(n).\]  This reduces to the known identity σ_mex(n)=D_2(n) for A=2.
proof_strategy: Develop a bijection between partitions λ of n with a given mexA0 value m and A‑colorings of distinct partitions of n whose smallest missing multiple of A is m.  Alternatively, derive a generating‑function identity: ∑_{n≥0} (∑_{λ⊢n} mexA0(A,λ)) q^n = ∏_{k≥1}(1+q^k)^A, and verify coefficient equality by expansion.
title: Generalization of the mex‑sum identity to A‑color partitions

description: We conjecture that the finite family 𝔉₄ of graphs listed in the paper (the minimal obstructions for star‑4‑colorability of split graphs) is *complete*: a split graph G admits a star‑4‑coloring if and only if G contains no induced subgraph isomorphic to a member of 𝔉₄. Moreover, each graph in 𝔉₄ is minimal with respect to this property. This statement is precise, falsifiable by a counterexample split graph, and can be formalised in Lean 4 using the graph library, induced subgraph predicates, and star‑coloring definitions.
proof_strategy: Formalise split graphs as simple graphs whose vertex set can be partitioned into a clique C and an independent set I. Define star‑k‑coloring (proper coloring with no bicolored P₄). Encode the finite list 𝔉₄ of forbidden induced subgraphs (as explicit edge lists). Prove two directions: (→) Show that each H ∈ 𝔉₄ does not admit a star‑4‑coloring (by exhaustive case analysis on color assignments, already done in the paper). Hence any star‑4‑colorable split graph cannot contain H as an induced subgraph. (←) Use the certifying linear‑time algorithm from the paper: given a split graph G with no induced H∈𝔉₄, construct a star‑4‑coloring by iteratively coloring the clique C with at most 4 colors while respecting the constraints imposed by the independent set I. Formalise the algorithm as a constructive function in Lean and prove its correctness by induction on the number of vertices, using the structural properties of split graphs (e.g., ordering of clique vertices by neighborhoods). Finally, p
title: Exact Forbidden Subgraph Characterization for Star‑4‑Colorable Split Graphs

description: Assuming the Generalised Riemann Hypothesis and simplicity of zeros, for any primitive Dirichlet character χ modulo q>1, the sums over non‑trivial zeros ρ=1/2+iγ with 0<γ≤T of |L'(ρ,χ)|^{-2} and |L(2ρ,χ^2)/L'(ρ,χ)|^2 are asymptotic to (3/π^3)T and (1/(2π))T respectively, as T→∞.
proof_strategy: Use explicit formulae relating sums over zeros to integrals of logarithmic derivatives, approximate functional equations, and mollifiers to isolate the main term; then apply a smooth weight and optimise the contour to match the conjectured constant, following the strategy of Milinovich–Ng and Sinha adapted to the uniform setting.
title: Asymptotic formula for discrete second moments of Dirichlet L-functions under GRH

description: For any fixed integer width w ≥ 2, the maximum number of strict alternating cycles in a poset of size n and width w is Θ(n^{2w}) as n → ∞. The paper establishes an upper bound of O(n^{2w}) (Corollary 1 and Lemma 1); this conjecture asserts that this bound is asymptotically tight, i.e., there exists a constant c_w > 0 such that for all sufficiently large n, some poset of size n and width w has at least c_w n^{2w} strict alternating cycles.
proof_strategy: Construct explicit families of posets of width w and size n (e.g., by taking w disjoint chains of nearly equal length and adding suitable cross relations) that yield many incomparable pairs and strict alternating cycles. Alternatively, use a probabilistic method to show the existence of posets with at least Ω(n^{2w}) strict alternating cycles. The construction should ensure that the number of strict alternating cycles grows as a polynomial of degree 2w in n.
title: Tight asymptotic lower bound for the maximum number of strict alternating cycles in posets of fixed width

description: For an orientation D of a tree whose underlying undirected tree has diameter exactly four, D is converse invariant (i.e., f_T(D)=f_T(¬D) for every tournament T) if and only if the multilinear polynomial P_D, defined as the signed sum over subgraphs of the underlying graph of D, has zero coefficient for each monomial corresponding to a non‑self‑converse sub‑tree of diameter four that is not obtainable by bridge‑mirroring from a path.
proof_strategy: Use the polynomial method introduced in the paper: compute the coefficient of each monomial in P_D as a signed count of embeddings of certain subgraphs. For diameter‑four trees, the only possible monomials arise from sub‑trees of diameter at most four. Enumerate all non‑self‑converse orientations of such sub‑trees (a finite list). Show that converse invariance forces each of these coefficients to vanish, which yields a set of linear constraints on the orientation of D. Solve these constraints to obtain exactly the orientations described in the classification theorem (self‑converse or obtained by bridge‑mirroring from a path, plus the sporadic examples found in the paper). Conversely, verify that each orientation satisfying the constraints indeed makes all coefficients zero, hence D is converse invariant.
title: Converse invariant orientations of trees of diameter four are characterized by vanishing of certain coefficients in the digraph polynomial

catalog_references: Bonamy et al. (2023) on infinite H-induced-saturated graphs
description: For every finite simple graph H that is not complete, there exists a finite simple graph G with at least one edge such that G contains no induced subgraph isomorphic to H, but deleting any edge of G creates an induced copy of H. This is the central conjecture of the paper, verified for all graphs on ≤6 vertices and proven for several infinite families including complete bipartite graphs with unequal parts, triangle-free graphs with one cycle, and line graphs of trees.
proof_strategy: The paper establishes the conjecture for multiple families using explicit constructions and structural arguments. A general proof might combine: (1) Reduction to prime graphs under some decomposition, (2) Probabilistic method for dense graphs, (3) Explicit constructions for sparse graphs leveraging the asymmetry (only edge deletion matters), (4) Induction on graph parameters using the verified base cases up to 6 vertices.
title: Existence of H-deletion-saturated graphs for all non-complete H

description: This conjecture asserts that a finitely generated abelian group $A$ defines a canonical threshold for $k$-flow-connectedness based on the existence of certain minor structures in cubic graphs, aiming to bridge the combinatorial rigidity described in Esperet et al. with algorithmic verification in Lean 4.
proof_strategy: Constructive existence via minor elimination and inductive flow decomposition
title: A compact characterization of $A$-flow-connectedness in terms of graph minor theory

description: For a non‑exceptional polynomial f with disconnected Julia set, if α_1,…,α_n are algebraic numbers in the Böttcher domain D_R that are linearly independent over ℚ, then the tuple (Ψ_f(α_1),…,Ψ_f(α_n)) is algebraically independent over the algebraic numbers; equivalently there is no non‑zero polynomial P∈ℚ[X_1,…,X_n] such that P(Ψ_f(α_1),…,Ψ_f(α_n))=0.
proof_strategy: Adapt the classical Lindemann–Weierstrass proof using properties of the Böttcher coordinate, linear independence over ℚ, and transcendence measures; possibly invoke Mahler’s method or properties of rational functions.
title: Ψ_f-Lindemann–Weierstrass Conjecture for Algebraic Independence of Böttcher Coordinates

description: Formulates a concise formalism in Lean 4 to verify an instance of Hegedçs' eigenvalue condition using Gram matrix eigenvalues and algebraic constraints, making the bound falsifiable through explicit construction.
proof_strategy: Leverage the lemma on norm equality and linear independence to tighten dimension bounds via spectral arguments.
title: Proof of Hegedçs bound via spectral constraints in combinatorial families

description: Conjecture that the regulator integral R_N of the element Ξ_N ∈ K₄^{(3)}(X_N) satisfies R_N = (3/2) ζ(3) N² − (π²/6) N log N + O(N) as N → ∞. This refines the asymptotic result proved in the paper by specifying the coefficient of the N log N term.
proof_strategy: Use the explicit hypergeometric expression for the regulator derived in the paper, apply known asymptotics of the hypergeometric function {}_3F₂ and of Zagier's trilogarithm sums, and extract the subleading term via Mellin–Barnes integral techniques or saddle‑point analysis.
title: Next-to-leading asymptotic of regulator integrals for K₄ elements on Fermat curves

catalog_references: Bloom, Sawin, Schildkraut, Zhelezov (2023). Disproving the sum‑product conjecture over ℝ.
Bloom, Sawin, Schildkraut, Zhelezov (2024). Both AA and (A+1)(A+1) can be small.
description: We conjecture that there exists a universal constant c > 0 such that for any finite set S ⊆ ℝ (or ℚ) one can find arbitrarily large finite sets A ⊆ ℝ with max_{λ ∈ S} |(A+λ)(A+λ)| ≪ |A|^{2-c}. In other words, the exponent 2-c can be taken independent of the size or the particular elements of S, strengthening the existing result which only guarantees a c that may depend on S.
domain_bridges: Number theory (totally real fields and discriminant bounds)
proof_strategy: Adapt the expander‑graph construction of Bloom–Sawin–Schildkraut–Zhelezov to a uniform setting. Use a sequence of totally real number fields K with exceptionally small discriminant (as guaranteed by Theorem 2.2) to encode a common additive structure for all shifts λ ∈ S. For each N choose a field K of degree d ≈ log N and form a set A ⊆ ℚ as a union of boxes B⁺(R) and B⁎(Y) with carefully balanced parameters R,Y. The box lemmas give precise control on |A+A| and |AA|. By making the discriminant small enough one can force the product set (A+λ)(A+λ) to stay of size O(N^{2-c}) uniformly for every λ ∈ S. The exponent c comes from the quantitative bound Δ_K ≤ C^d and can be chosen independently of S by taking d large enough. The argument thus yields a single constant c that works for all finite S, achieving the uniform bound.
title: Uniform shift exponent for product sets

description: The conjecture asserts that H_α converges to zero as network size increases for sufficiently large structures.
proof_strategy: induction over network size
title: Convergence to Zero

catalog_references: Esterov-Gusev classification of mixed volume one tuples
description: Conjecture that a tuple of lattice polytopes has mixed volume one if and only if it is unimodularly equivalent to one of the classified configurations and its tropical intersection forms a reduced point whose fan structure corresponds to a uniform matroid Bergman fan. Specifically: MV(P₁,...,Pₙ)=1 ⟺ ∃ unimodular φ such that (φ(P₁),...,φ(Pₙ)) satisfies Esterov-Gusev classification criteria, implying Σ_{P₁}∩_{st}...∩_{st}Σ_{Pₙ}={(0,1)} with Bergman fan structure of U_{n+1,n+1}.
proof_strategy: Establish necessity by showing mixed volume one implies unimodular equivalence to classified forms via volume considerations; prove sufficiency by verifying tropical intersection multiplicities match reduced point condition. Connect to Fink's work through matroid subdivision dual to mixed volume computations. Use the three verified cases (unmixed sequences, hypersurface cycles, 2-cycles) as foundational tools for induction on dimension and polytope complexity.
title: Unimodular Equivalence Classification for Mixed Volume One Tuples

description: For any self‑repelling polymer model on \(\mathbb Z^2\) satisfying the standard assumptions of the paper (finite range, repulsive interaction, and a constant vertical force of strength \(h>0\)), the variational problem defining the macroscopic shape has a unique minimizer. Moreover, the minimizer depends continuously on the endpoint data and on the force strength.
proof_strategy: Show that the functional \(\mathcal F[\gamma]=\int_0^1 L(\gamma(t),\dot\gamma(t))\,dt\) is strictly convex on the admissible set of absolutely continuous curves with prescribed endpoints. The Lagrangian \(L\) is the Legendre transform of the limiting free‑energy rate function, which is known to be convex and smooth. Strict convexity follows from uniform positivity of the second derivative of \(L\) in the velocity variable, a consequence of the repulsive interaction and the constant force field. Apply the direct method of the calculus of variations to obtain existence, then invoke strict convexity to deduce uniqueness. Continuity of the minimizer with respect to parameters follows from the implicit function theorem for minimizers of strictly convex functionals.
title: Uniqueness of the macroscopic shape minimizer for self‑repelling polymers in a constant force field

catalog_references: Perfect state transfer equivalence between G and G/π
description: Let G be a connected graph with equitable partition π₁ yielding quotient graph G/π₁, and suppose G/π₁ admits an equitable partition π₂ with quotient ((G/π₁)/π₂). Then perfect state transfer occurs on G if and only if it occurs on (G/π₁)/π₂. This extends the single-step quotient result to chains of quotient constructions.
proof_strategy: Proceed by composing the characteristic matrices Q₁ (for π₁) and Q₂ (for π₂) to form a composite equitable partition on G. Leverage the already-proven equivalence: PST on G ⟺ PST on G/π₁, then apply the same equivalence to G/π₁ ≺ (G/π₁)/π₂. The composition Q₂∘Q₁ yields a valid equitable partition of G with quotient isomorphic to (G/π₁)/π₂. The result follows by transitivity of the established PST-preserving correspondence.
title: PST Preservation Through Iterative Quotient Graphs

description: Conjecture that there exist infinitely many subset-minimal minor-closed graph classes whose limiting density is exactly 3/2. This is the boundary case beyond which the paper's finiteness result no longer applies.
proof_strategy: Construct an infinite family of minor-minimal classes with density 3/2 by generalizing known constructions, or prove that any finite bound leads to a contradiction via density properties.
title: Infinitude of Minimal Minor-Closed Classes with Density Exactly 3/2

description: For every number of leaves ℓ ≥ 2, the column generating function F_ℓ(v) for orchard networks is a rational function whose denominator equals the product D_ℓ(v)=∏_{j=2}^ℓ X_j(v), where X_j(v)=∑_{k=0}^{⌊j/2⌋} (-1)^k (j!)/((j-2k)! k!) v^k is the matching polynomial of the complete graph K_j. Moreover, D_ℓ(v) is monic and its roots are all simple and positive real.
proof_strategy: Formalize phylogenetic network definitions and the recursive decomposition used in the paper to derive the functional equation for F_ℓ(v). Show that the recursion yields a linear recurrence with polynomial coefficients whose characteristic polynomial is exactly D_ℓ(v). Use Lean's polynomial library to prove by induction on ℓ that F_ℓ(v) = N_ℓ(v)/D_ℓ(v) for some polynomial N_ℓ(v). Then apply known results about matching polynomials of complete graphs (available in Mathlib) to prove D_ℓ(v) is monic with simple positive real roots, completing the conjecture.
title: Rationality of the Orchard Network Column Generating Function

description: For integers R ≥ 1, S with 1 ≤ S ≤ R/2, and k ≥ 1, the coefficient of qⁿ in the bilateral truncated Jacobi triple product identity [...] is equal to the number of partitions of n where the minimal excludant is k, and the number of parts greater than k minus the number of parts less than k equals S.
proof_strategy: Combinatorial proof by constructing a bijection between the coefficients' contributing terms and the partitions described, leveraging the generating function expressions from Wang and Yee's work and the partition interpretation techniques from Andrews and Merca.
title: A Partition-Theoretic Interpretation of the Bilateral Truncated Jacobi Triple Product Coefficients via Minimal Excludant

description: The limit of the average stack-sorting depth scaled by n converges to the rational number 3/4.
proof_strategy: numerical_experiment_and_analytic_upper_lower_bounds
title: Exact asymptotic value of the average stack-sorting depth

description: Conjecture: For every integer n ≥ 2, a biased graph is gainable over the cyclic group Z_n if and only if it contains none of the minors ( (n+1)K2, ∅ ), ±K3, or -K4.
proof_strategy: Prove the equivalence by induction on the size of the graph, using the theory of partial groups to reduce to Z_2 and Z_3 cases and applying known excluded minor classifications for those groups.
title: Excluded minors for Z_n-gainable biased graphs

description: For any dimension d ≥ 2 and any positive integer N, the number of spanning trees of the d-dimensional grid graph with free boundaries (Cartesian product of d path graphs) having exactly N vertices is maximized when the side lengths are as equal as possible (i.e., differ by at most 1). Moreover, any maximizer must have this balanced shape.
proof_strategy: Extend the heat-trace Schur-concavity argument from perfect-power volumes to arbitrary N by showing that the logarithm of the spanning tree count is a symmetric Schur-concave function of the logarithmic side lengths. Use discrete majorization and smoothing techniques to prove that any imbalance in side lengths can be locally adjusted to increase the spanning tree count, thereby establishing that the unique maximizers (up to permutation) are the balanced tuples.
title: Balanced Side Lengths Maximize Spanning Trees in Free Boundary Product Grids

description: The paper proves that for any fixed k ≥ 2 and any ε > 0, almost all n satisfy g_k(n) ≥ (3(k-1)/log 12 - ε) log n, where g_k(n) is the maximum excess a_1+⋯+a_k - n with a_1!⋯a_k! ∣ n!. It also gives the pointwise upper bound g_k(n) ≤ (k-1) log_2 n + log_2 log n + O_k(1). The constant 3/log 12 ≈ 1.207 is strictly smaller than the binary leading coefficient 1/log 2 ≈ 1.443. This conjecture asserts that the density-one lower bound cannot be improved, i.e., 3(k-1)/log 12 is the exact almost-everywhere constant.
proof_strategy: Construct a positive-density set of integers n where the mixed 2-3 representation used in the lower bound is essentially optimal, by showing that the phase separation for S-unit progressions cannot be improved beyond the current uniform digit-sum normal-order theorem. Alternatively, develop a large-sieve argument to prove that the exceptional set for any larger constant has positive lower density.
title: Optimality of the Density-One Constant for Erdős Problem 400

description: This paper investigates the algebraic origins of overlap units in SIC-POVMs by linking them to square roots of Stark units in the context of ray class fields. It proposes a framework to systematically decode these units through arithmetic progression properties.
domain_bridges: linear algebra over finite fields + analytic number theory
proof_strategy: Inductive construction of ray class fields and modular constraints
title: Constructive characterization of overlap units in SIC-POVMs via ray class fields

description: We conjecture that the girth of an optimal small-set expander G with parameters (s, α) is uniquely determined by s and α, and this property yields optimal code distances for the corresponding binary linear codes B(G). This would enable rigorous translation of combinatorial expander bounds to coding-theoretic parameters.
proof_strategy: Use transversality principles to link girth constraints with extremal set expansions, then apply derandomization to embed codeword structures.
title: Girth-Determined Optimality of Small-Set Expanders for Post-Quantum Key Exchange Codes

description: This paper investigates the triviality of Boolean degree one functions on the Grassmann scheme $J_q(n,k)$ under specific constraints involving $k$ and $n$, aiming to characterize when such functions must vanish.
domain_bridges: The existence of counterexamples hinges on deep properties of $q$-binomial coefficients and duality in Grassmann algebras.
proof_strategy: Construct a degree-one Boolean function explicitly and verify its behavior under duality and constraint conditions.
title: Boolean degree one functions on the Grassmann scheme

description: Conjecture: There exists a constant C > 0 such that for all n ≥ 1, the number a_n of Pólya trees with n nodes satisfies a_n ≤ C * ρ^{-n} * n^{-3/2}, where ρ ≈ 0.338321 is the radius of convergence of the generating function A(z) defined by A(z) = z exp(A(z)) Φ(z) with Φ(z) = exp(∑_{i≥2} A(z^i)/i).
proof_strategy: Use singularity analysis: show that A(z) has a square-root singularity at z=ρ, apply Flajolet and Odlyzko's transfer theorem to obtain the asymptotic a_n ∼ c_A n^{-3/2} ρ^{-n}. From the asymptotic, deduce an explicit upper bound with some constant C, which can be made effective by bounding the error terms in the singular expansion.
title: Improved upper bound for Pólya tree coefficients

description: For every edge density β ∈ [0,1] the minimum possible asymptotic density of semi‑induced copies of S_{2,1} in an n‑vertex graph G with edge density β is given by the one‑parameter three‑class complement‑split construction: let t ∈ [0,1] be the unique solution of β = t(1 − t/2); then the minimum semi‑induced density equals p_min(β) = t²(1−t).
proof_strategy: Apply a transfer argument to reduce the extremal problem to optimizing over degree distributions. Use Lagrange multipliers to show that an optimal distribution is supported on at most three points. Realize these three points by a three‑class complement‑split graphon (two clique parts and an independent set part with adjustable internal density). Solve the moment equations linking the graphon parameters to β and to the semi‑induced count, yielding the explicit formula p_min(β)=t²(1−t) where t satisfies β=t(1−t/2).
title: Exact lower semi-inducibility profile for the red‑blue star S_{2,1}

description: The conjecture asserts that the minimal vertex cut separating two vertex sets A and B has size bounded logarithmically by a parameter related to the problem's complexity, ensuring falsifiability through counterexamples.
proof_strategy: induction based on parameter constraints
title: Logarithmic Disjoint Path Bounds

description: Conjecture: Let K be an imaginary quadratic field with class number 1 and let N ≥ 1 be an odd integer. Let S_K = Herm_2(O_K) be the rank‑four lattice of 2×2 Hermitian matrices over O_K equipped with the quadratic form 2 det. For the very general S_K(2N)-polarized K3 surface X_{K,2N}, the natural representation Aut(X_{K,2N}) → O(NS(X_{K,2N})) identifies Aut(X_{K,2N}) with the projective level subgroup Bi_K(2N) of the Bianchi group Γ_K = PSL_2(O_K). In particular, Aut(X_{K,2N}) ≅ Bi_K(2N) as abstract groups.
proof_strategy: Use the global Torelli theorem for K3 surfaces to embed Aut(X_{K,2N}) into the group of Hodge isometries of the Néron‑Severi lattice NS(X_{K,2N}) ≅ S_K(2N). Show that any such isometry preserves the natural level‑2N structure coming from the polarization, hence lies in the orthogonal group O(S_K(2N); 2N). By strong approximation for the spinor genus of S_K and the hypothesis that the class number of O_K is 1, the subgroup of O(S_K(2N); 2N) acting trivially on the discriminant group coincides with the projective level subgroup Bi_K(2N). The converse inclusion follows from constructing explicit geometric automorphisms (e.g., genus‑one fibration translations and covering involutions) that generate Bi_K(2N).
title: Automorphism groups of Picard-rank-four K3 surfaces polarized by Hermitian lattices over class number one imaginary quadratic fields equal projective level subgroups of Bianchi groups

description: For a connected digraph $G$, stability of the pair $(G, K_2)$ is equivalent to the absence of nontrivial automorphisms of $G$ that preserve the arc structure under vertex swapping. We conjecture that no finite arc-transitive circulant digraphs with more than two vertices are nontrivially unstable.
proof_strategy: Use arc-transitivity properties and eigenvalue analysis of circulant digraphs to show that any nontrivial endomorphism would require eigenvalues not preserved under automorphism group action, contradicting arc-transitivity.
title: Nonexistence of nontrivially unstable finite arc-transitive circulant digraphs

description: This paper presents a refined characterization of the externally supported independence number and its computational implications in trees, offering sharp bounds and algorithmic insights.
proof_strategy: formalization and verification using Lean 4
title: Externally Supported Independence Number for Trees

description: The paper proves that every binary delta-matroid has the property that all five nontrivial partial-twuality polynomials (for • ∈ {*, ×, *×, ×*, *×*}) are interpolating (each is either even, odd, or both even- and odd-interpolating). It also shows the binary assumption is essential by providing counterexamples. This conjecture proposes the exact converse: if a delta-matroid has this universal interpolation property for all five operators simultaneously, then it must be binary. This would characterize binary delta-matroids purely in terms of the interpolation behavior of their partial-twuality polynomials.
proof_strategy: 1. Formalize delta-matroids, binary delta-matroids, and the five twuality operations in Lean. 2. Define partial-• polynomials and the notions of even/odd/interpolating polynomials. 3. Prove the forward direction (binary ⇒ universal interpolation) by translating the paper's proof. 4. For the converse, assume a non-binary delta-matroid D has universal interpolation. Use the fact that non-binary delta-matroids contain a minor isomorphic to one of the excluded minors for binary delta-matroids (e.g., U_{2,4} or its delta-matroid analogues). 5. Compute the partial-twuality polynomials for these excluded minors and show at least one operator fails interpolation. 6. Use minor-closure properties of the interpolation property to derive a contradiction.
title: Characterization of Delta-Matroids with Universal Partial-Twuality Interpolation

description: The Turán density of the 4-uniform tight cycle of length 6 minus one edge, denoted C_6^{4-}, equals 3/8, and this value is achieved by the complete odd-bipartite 4-graph with parts of sizes ⌊n/2⌋ and ⌈n/2⌉ in each bipartite class. This conjecture provides the exact density for the smallest non-trivial case (k=1) of tight cycles minus one edge, which connects to but may differ from the 1/2 density established for longer tight cycles C_{4k+2}^{4} with k≥2.
proof_strategy: 1) Establish upper bound via flag algebra computations or entropy compression arguments showing no C_6^{4-} free 4-graph can have density exceeding 3/8. 2) Construct the complete odd-bipartite 4-graph achieving 3/8 density. 3) Prove stability: any C_6^{4-} free 4-graph with density approaching 3/8 must be close to the complete odd-bipartite construction. 4) Use removal lemma techniques to handle the local structure of potential extremal configurations.
title: Exact Turán Density of the 4-Uniform Tight 6-Cycle Minus One Edge

description: The conjecture posits that series expansions derived for higher-order trinomial equations maintain structural consistency when substituting variables like $D$ and $1/D$, validated via algebraic identities analogous to Kummer's results.
proof_strategy: Direct Verification via Coefficient Matching
title: Convergence of Hypergeometric Series Under Algebraic Transformations

description: We conjecture that for ternary matrices with fixed row and column sums, the lazy swap chain (defined analogously by swapping 2x2 submatrices preserving margins) has a spectral gap of at least Ω(1/(m²n²)), matching the binary case's inverse-polynomial bound.
proof_strategy: Adapt the reduction to three rows and Johnson harmonic sector decomposition to ternary case, verify margin preservation under swaps
title: SpectralGap for Lazy Swap Chains on Ternary Matrices

description: For every positive integer \( s \), there exists a graph with exactly \( s \) irreducible FAT colorings. This is shown explicitly for prime \( s \) using a cycle of length \( 2s + 1 \) with a single pendant vertex, where only the trivial and full-colorings are irreducible, and generalizations extend this to composite \( s \).
proof_strategy: Construct a graph where only the trivial 2-coloring (non-adjacent vertices) and full-coloring are FAT, leveraging parity and degree constraints to block all intermediate partitions.
title: Bounded Irreducible FAT Colorings via Modified Even Cycles

description: For every fixed graph H without isolated vertices, any graphon W achieving the supremum in the sparse threshold conjecture is a three-step threshold graphon, and the constant C_T(H) is the unique maximizer of the associated variational problem.
proof_strategy: Assume a graphon W achieves the supremum. Use the finite-kernel framework to decompose W into interacting scales. Apply the finite state decomposition to show that any deviation from three-step threshold structure would violate the optimality condition, forcing W to be a three-step threshold graphon. Then, prove uniqueness by analyzing the Hessian of the variational problem for C_T(H) to show strict concavity, ensuring a unique maximizer.
title: Uniqueness of Extremal Graphons in Sparse Threshold Problems

catalog_references: On k-limited domination: complexity and Cartesian products (arXiv preprint)
description: For every connected finite simple graph G of order n with maximum degree Δ and every integer k satisfying 1 ≤ k < Δ, the k‑limited domination number γ_k^L(G) equals the lower bound ⌈ n/(k+1) ⌉.
proof_strategy: Attempt a constructive proof by exhibiting a k‑limited dominating set of size ⌈n/(k+1)⌉ using a greedy covering argument, or disprove by locating a graph where any k‑limited dominating set must be larger, thereby providing a counterexample.
title: Conjecture: The k‑limited domination number meets its lower bound for all connected graphs

description: Conjecture: For every tree T, the minimum size of an initial set that forces all vertices to exceed the transmission threshold (the transmission zero forcing number) is exactly the domination number of T, i.e., the size of a smallest dominating set.
proof_strategy: Use induction on the number of vertices of a tree, leveraging leaf properties and the fact that a dominating set must contain a neighbor of each leaf; show that the forcing process can be simulated by a dominating set and vice‑versa, thereby establishing equality.
title: Transmission Zero Forcing Number Equals Domination Number on Trees

description:
For any integer matrix \(M = \begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}\) with non‑zero determinant and \(\gcd(a,b,c,d)=1\), the set of ratios of Lagrange constants
\[\mathcal{V}(M) := \{ k(Mx)/k(x) : x \in \mathrm{Bad}\}\]
coincides with the closed interval \([|\det M|^{-1},\,|\det M|]\). In other words, every value between the extremal bounds given by Lagarias–Shallit is attained by some badly approximable number, and no values outside the interval occur.
proof_strategy: Use the Smith normal form of \(M\) to reduce to diagonal matrices \(\operatorname{diag}(d,1)\) with \(d=\det M\). For a diagonal matrix the transformation is \(x \mapsto d x\) or \(x \mapsto x/d\). Show that for any \(r\) in the interval there exists a badly approximable \(x\) with prescribed limsup of partial quotients such that \(k(d x)=r\,k(x)\). This is achieved by constructing continued fractions with blocks of large partial quotients whose frequencies encode the desired ratio, employing the known formula \(k(x)=\limsup ([a_n; a_{n+1},\dots]+[0;a_{n-1},\dots,a_1])\). Finally lift the result back to the original \(M\) using the unimodular matrices from the Smith decomposition, which preserve \(k(x)\) up to the determinant factor. The argument is fully formalizable in Lean using existing libraries for continued fractions, matrix normal forms, and Diophantine approximation.
title: Exact Ratio Spectrum of Lagrange Constants under Integer Linear Fractional Transformations

catalog_references: Farnsworth, J. (2022). Lower bounds for Hales‑Jewett numbers.
van der Waerden, D. (1927). Beweis einer baudetschen Vermutung.
Hindman, N. & Tressler, J. (2020). The Hales‑Jewett number ℕJ(3,2)=4.
Lavrov, A. (2023). Improved upper bounds for Hales‑Jewett numbers.
description: We conjecture that the Hales‑Jewett number ℕJ(3,4) is at least 20. This extends the coordinate‑symmetric coloring method used to obtain the improved bounds ℕJ(3,3)≥2 2 and ℕJ(4,2)≥2 14. The expectation is that there exists a 4‑coloring of the cube [3]^{20} depending only on the letter‑count vector (i.e. invariant under permutations of coordinates) that contains no monochromatic combinatorial line. If true, this would raise the current lower bound for ℕJ(3,4) (presently only the van der Waerden bound) and demonstrate that the symmetric approach scales to larger parameters.
proof_strategy: We will formalize the definitions of ℕJ(t,r), combinatorial lines, coordinate‑symmetric colorings, and the line‑free condition in Lean 4. The finite reduction lemma is encoded as a system of constraints on the coloring function f: ℕ^{t} → ℤ/r (where f maps a count vector to a color). An external SAT solver finds a candidate function f for n=20; the solution is then presented as an explicit table of fewer than 600 entries. A mechanically checked verification in Lean confirms that no corner tuple on the discrete simplex is monochromatic, thereby establishing the existence of a line‑free symmetric coloring. The lower bound ℕJ(3,4)≥2 20 follows directly from this coloring.
title: Conjecture: HJ(3,4) ≥ 20 via symmetric colorings

description: Let n be a positive integer. Define an affine permutation σ: ℕ/nℕ → ℕ/nℕ by σ(i) = ai + b (mod n). The conjecture states that for n coprime to 2 and 3, the permutation σ is panmagic if and only if a is a unit in ℕ/nℕ and both a and a-1 are units such that the mapping i → ai+b and i → (a-1)i+b satisfy specific modular constraints related to the panmagic property (specifically, that the coefficients of the linear forms for diagonals do not vanish modulo n). Specifically, we propose to formalize the theorem that for prime n > 3, the set of panmagic affine permutations forms a structure related to the cosets of the dihedral group within the affine group Aff(ℕ/nℕ).
proof_strategy: The strategy involves defining the permutation matrix of an affine map in Lean, implementing the panmagic property as a predicate on the sum of entries over broken diagonals, and using the properties of modular arithmetic to show that the panmagic condition is equivalent to certain coefficients being invertible in ℕ/nℕ. The proof would rely on the theory of finite rings and the characterization of latin squares.
title: Algebraic Characterization of Panmagic Affine Permutations over Z_n

description: The conjecture asserts that the determinant of the L' vertices in the five-vertex model must vanish unless specific boundary conditions on weights are met, which can be verified computationally.
title: Determinantal Consistency

catalog_references: Inverse power series in formal power series ring
description: Propose that for any Sprugnoli array $(g(x), f_1(x), f_2(x))$ in the first family, there exists a unique inverse array $(g^{-1}(x), f_1^{-1}(x), f_2^{-1}(x))$ whose coefficients are closed-form expressions involving only summation symbols, binomial coefficients, and arithmetic operations, as described in the paper's Section 3. This inverse must satisfy the condition that the matrix product of the original and inverse arrays yields the identity matrix.
proof_strategy: Verify via induction on matrix dimensions, leveraging the weighted composition law from the Sprugnoli group's fundamental theorem. Construct inverse coefficients recursively using the paper's closed-form expressions and verify the identity matrix condition through modular arithmetic constraints.
title: Existence of Inverse Sprugnoli Arrays with Closed-Form Coefficients

description: For any ordinary algebraic differential equation $\mathfrak{P}$ of order $k$, the set $S(\mathfrak{P},0)$ of $t$-adic orders of formal Hahn solutions at $t_0=0$ is exactly equal to the set of $t$-adic orders of Hahn elementary $k$-solutions of its tropicalization $P = \mathrm{trop}(\mathfrak{P})$, i.e., $S(\mathfrak{P},0) = \mathrm{ord}_t(Sol_{\mathbb{B}[\![t^{\mathbb{R}]\!,k}(P))$. This conjecture strengthens the containment relation proved in the paper to an equality, requiring that every solution order arises purely from the tropical elementary solutions.
proof_strategy: Establish a bijective correspondence between the support of solution germs and the combinatorial structure of tropical elementary solutions by leveraging valuation-theoretic properties of Hahn series and the functoriality of tropicalization under differential operations.
title: Equality of Solution Orders and Tropical Elementary Solutions

catalog_references: Musiker, Schiffler, and Williams (2011) - Positivity for cluster algebras of surface type
Çanakçı and Schiffler (2020) - Snake graphs and q-continued fractions
description: For a band graph $\mathcal{G}$ associated with a closed curve $\ell$ on a surface $\mathcal{S}$, the $q$-weighted dimer partition function $\mathcal{Z}_{G,m}(q)$—defined as the sum over the set of 'good higher dimer covers'—is a palindromic polynomial. Specifically, there exists an integer $N$ such that $q^N \mathcal{Z}_{G,m}(q^{-1}) = \mathcal{Z}_{G,m}(q)$, where the symmetry is induced by the distributive lattice structure of the face-flip operation on higher dimer covers.
proof_strategy: First, formalize the definition of 'good higher dimer covers' as a subset of matchings on a band graph. Second, implement the 'face flip' operation as a partial order, proving the resulting structure is a distributive lattice. Third, apply the property that the rank generating function of a distributive lattice is palindromic if the lattice is self-dual, mapping the dimer partition function to this rank generating function via a $q$-weighting shift.
title: Palindromicity of the $q$-weighted partition function for higher dimer covers on band graphs

description: We conjecture that every connected, cubic (3-regular), edge-transitive graph that contains a Hamiltonian cycle has a Hamiltonian compression factor κ(Γ) ≥ 2. This would follow if every such graph admits a Hamiltonian cycle invariant under a non-trivial automorphism acting as a rotation. A counterexample would be an edge-transitive cubic Hamiltonian graph with κ(Γ) = 1, which would falsify the conjecture.
proof_strategy: Possibly by leveraging the edge-transitivity to construct a rotational automorphism of a Hamiltonian cycle, or by contradiction assuming κ(Γ)=1 and deriving a structural impossibility inherent to edge-transitive cubic graphs.
title: Every Hamiltonian Edge-Transitive Cubic Graph Has Hamiltonian Compression Factor at Least 2

description:
We conjecture that for any integer n ≥ 3 and any fixed parity pattern ε ∈ {+1,‑1}^r (e.g. ε = (‑1,…,‑1) giving the t‑values), the following weighted sum holds:

⏎
∑※_{k_1+⋆+⋆+k_r=n, k_r≥2} ∟_{i=2}^r (i+1)^{k_i} ⋆ M(k;ε) = (n+1) ⋆ M(n;ε),
⏎

where M(k;ε) denotes the finite multiple mixed value defined in the paper. This generalizes the Guo‑Xie weighted sum for ordinary MZVs to the three level‑two families t, T, and S, and suggests a unified weighted sum principle for all finite mixed values.
domain_bridges: Hopf algebras of multiple zeta values
proof_strategy:
1. Formalise the iterated integral representation of finite multiple mixed values M(k;ε) using Lean’s algebraic structures for commutative rings and formal series.
2. Derive a weighted sum identity for the associated multiple polylogarithms by reducing to the known Guo‑Xie weighted sum for ordinary MZVs via parity projections.
3. Use induction on the total weight n together with the shuffle relations to collapse the double sum to a single term (n+1)M(n;ε).
4. Encode the combinatorial data (admissible indices, parity patterns) as dependent types in Lean, and implement the weighted product ∟_{i=2}^r (i+1)^{k_i} as a rational exponentiation.
5. Produce a machine‑checked proof (or a proof outline) of the theorem, establishing the conjecture as a formal lemma that can be used for further investigations of level‑two finite multiple values.
title: Weighted sum formula for finite multiple mixed values: a conjectural extension of Guo‑Xie formulas to level‑two families

description: Conjecture: For every positive integer d there exist non-derogatory integer matrices M,N such that they are similar over Q_p for all primes p, yet any number field L over which they become similar satisfies [L:ℚ] > d.
proof_strategy: Construct explicit families of companion matrices of cyclotomic polynomials; use class field theory to show unbounded index of the splitting field of the characteristic polynomial; formalize the construction and the lower bound on extension degree in Lean's mathlib.
title: No uniform bound on extension degree for similarity of integral matrices over number fields

proof_strategy: Elementary decomposition via group theory
title: Elementary Decomposition Bound

catalog_references: Landau's Theorem on tournament score sequences
Bebeacua et al. (2005) on xrays of permutations
description: Formalize and prove the conjecture that the set of increasing characteristic sequences of permutations on Z_n (binary xrays) is exactly the set of score sequences of tournaments on n vertices, effectively showing that the numerical conditions characterizing characteristic sequences of permutations are equivalent to Landau's Theorem for tournament score sequences.
proof_strategy: The proof should involve mapping the necessary and sufficient conditions of Landau's Theorem (sum of the first k elements of a score sequence is at least k(k-1)/2) to the specific constraints on the characteristic set C(phi) = {i + phi(i) : i in Z_n}. The strategy would be to construct a bijection between the set of increasing characteristic sequences and the set of score sequences by demonstrating that the constraints on the sums of the smallest k elements of the characteristic sequence are identical to those in Landau's theorem.
title: Correspondence between Characteristic Sequences and Tournament Score Sequences

description: This paper proposes a novel framework to classify three-lines and cubic/cubic-quartic arrangements via combinatorial invariants derived from intersection theory, Dyck word patterns, and rooted tree decompositions. The conjecture predicts a unique topological invariant (the so-called 'curve obstruction index') that distinguishes realizable configurations across degrees, under certain algebraic constraints.
proof_strategy: Algorithmic exploration combined with symbolic manipulation in Lean 4
title: Combinatorial classification of arrangements of curves using topological and combinatorial invariants
