title: Isolation subdivision number of a graph

description: For any r-differential poset P, the number of vacillating tableaux of length n satisfies the same identity as derived in partition algebras, which follows from the commutation relation DU - UD = rI and structural properties of P.
proof_strategy: Encode the structural identities of differential posets (via operators U, D, and their commutation relation) to algebraically derive the vacuillating tableaux count.
title: Universal Vacillating Tableaux Identity in Differential Posets

description: Conjecture: For any field F of characteristic not equal to 2, any parameters ε,δ ∈ F with ε(δ^2−ε)≠0, and any points P, Q on the Jacobi quartic curve J_{ε,δ} : y^2 = ε x^4 + 2δ x^2 + 1, if D = P − Q is known in affine coordinates, then the differential addition formula given in the paper (with cost 3M+6S+3D when D is affine) correctly computes the point P+Q on J_{ε,δ}. This statement is falsifiable because a single counterexample (e.g., a specific finite field and points where the formula yields a point different from the true group sum) would disprove it.
proof_strategy: Use the birational isomorphism ζ from the Jacobi quartic to its Weierstrass model E_{ε,δ}. Transfer the differential addition formula via ζ to obtain a rational expression on E. Verify that this expression coincides with the standard chord‑and‑tangent addition on E by direct algebraic simplification (or by invoking the uniqueness of the group law). Pull the equality back through ζ^{-1} to obtain the claimed identity on the quartic. The verification can be carried out by a computer algebra system and then formalized in Lean using the field_tactic and ring_nf tactics.
title: Correctness of differential addition formulas for Jacobi quartic curves

description: We conjecture that the multigraded Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of a Schubert variety $S_\sigma$ in the Plücker embedding is upper bounded by the length of the longest chain of Bruhat-ordered Schubert varieties between the trivial subgroup and $\sigma$ with a \(3412\)-\(4231\)-avoiding element at each step. This refines the existing bounds in Theorem 1.3 of the paper using Schubert poset combinatorics.
domain_bridges: tensor category frameworks for Bruhat order
proof_strategy: Automated theorem proving using Lean 4's combinatorial ring of varieties, leveraging existing formalizations of Schubert subposets, Bruhat order automata, and multigraded regularity computations from the Cranton-Heller-Sayrafi papers.
title: Falsifiability of Multigraded Regularity Conjecture for Schubert Varieties via Plücker Embedding

catalog_references: Ellis theory of universal minimal flows
description: Let F be a continuum, G a closed subgroup of Homeo(F), and ℱ a projective Fraïssé category with limit 𝔽 such that Aut(𝔽) is dense in G. The paper proves that ℱ has the approximate Ramsey property iff G is extremely amenable. We conjecture that for all such G, the universal minimal flow M(G) is metrizable if and only if G is extremely amenable (equivalently, iff ℱ has the approximate Ramsey property). This would mean that among these groups, there are no non-extremely amenable groups with metrizable universal minimal flows.
domain_bridges: Projective Fraïssé categories and topological dynamics
Approximate Ramsey theory and extreme amenability
proof_strategy: 1. Analyze the structure of M(G) when G is the closure of Aut(𝔽) in Homeo(F). 2. Use the fact that Aut(𝔽) is a non-archimedean Polish group whose universal minimal flow is well-understood via KPT theory. 3. Relate the approximate Ramsey property of ℱ to the Ramsey property of the associated discrete Fraïssé category. 4. Show that failure of the approximate Ramsey property implies the existence of a non-metrizable quotient of M(Aut(𝔽)) that survives in the completion to G. 5. Alternatively, construct a counterexample by finding a continuum F where Homeo(F) is not extremely amenable but has metrizable M(Homeo(F)).
title: Metrizability of Universal Minimal Flows for Homeomorphism Groups of Continua via Approximate Ramsey Property

description: The logarithmic number of q-matroids of fixed rank r on a ground space of dimension n is asymptotically equal to the lower bound derived from constant-dimension codes, i.e., lim_{n→∞} (log_q N(n,r,q)) / L(n,r,q) = 1, where L(n,r,q) is the logarithm of the size of a maximal constant-dimension code construction.
proof_strategy: Compare asymptotic expansions of the lower bound and the conjectured true count using entropy and coding theory arguments, then apply the squeezing theorem.
title: Asymptotic Tightness of Code-Based Lower Bound for q-Matroid Enumeration

description: The conjecture asserts that any finite graph admits a finite tree-cut decomposition preserving undominated edge-ends, contradicting non-finite cases.
proof_strategy: Direct application of finiteness of finite graphs
title: Finite Decomposition Finiteness

description: Conjecture that for every uniformity r ≥ 2 there exists an absolute constant c > 0 such that for all sufficiently large n there is an n-vertex r-uniform hypergraph H in which every (r+1)-set of vertices spans either 0 or 2 edges and H contains at least c·r^{-2}·binom(n,r) edges, improving the Ω(r^{-3}) lower bound from the paper.
proof_strategy: Use a random construction where each r‑set is selected independently with probability p = Θ(r^{-2}). Show that the expected number of (r+1)-sets violating the 0/2 condition is o(1) when p is chosen appropriately, then apply the alteration method (or the Lovász local lemma) to obtain a hypergraph meeting the condition with Ω(p·binom(n,r)) edges. Alternatively, derive an explicit algebraic construction using quadratic forms over finite fields that yields the desired density.
title: Improved lower bound for r-graphs with 0 or 2 edges in every (r+1)-set

description: For a simple field extension L = K(θ) in characteristic p > 0 with minimal polynomial f ∈ K[x], and any purely inseparable field extension N/K, the numerical invariant m_{f,N} associated to the compositum NL/N (as defined in the paper) coincides with the invariant m_f associated to L/K. That is, m_{f,N} = m_f. This would imply that the criterion for NL = (NL)^{pi}(NL)^{sep} depends only on L/K and not on the choice of purely inseparable extension N/K.
proof_strategy: Use the explicit formulas for m_f and m_{f,N} in terms of the coefficients of the separable presentation f(x) = f^{sep}(x^{p^n}) = ∑ λ_i x^{i p^n}. Analyze how the purely inseparable extension N/K affects the coefficients when viewing f as a polynomial over N. Show that the combinatorial conditions defining the invariants (likely involving p-adic valuations of indices where λ_i ≠ 0) are unchanged by purely inseparable base change.
title: Invariance of the field invariant m_f under purely inseparable base change

description: We conjecture that for any odd prime p, any integers k ≥ 2 and s ≥ 1 with k < p, the sharp threshold for a random subset M ⊂ ℤₕℏ_p^n to intersect every variety defined by s polynomials of degree at most k is asymptotically given by m = (c_{k,s} + o(1)) n^{k}, where c_{k,s} = p^{(s-1)k}·(log p)/(log(1+(p-1)^{-1})). In particular, if |M| ≥ (c_{k,s} - ε) n^{k} then ℤₕℏ_p^n \\ M pierces every variety in ᵬF_{k,s} with probability ⇒ 1 as n → ∞, and if |M| ≤ (c_{k,s} + ε) n^{k} the property fails whp.
proof_strategy: Extend the second‑moment method used for quadratics to arbitrary degree k and s. First bound the expected number of varieties missed by M via a union bound over the family ᵬF_{k,s}. Then compute the variance using inclusion‑exclusion and the independence of random choices of coefficients. Show that when m = (c_{k,s} - o(1)) n^{k} the expectation tends to zero and the variance is negligible, yielding whp no missed varieties. Conversely, for m = (c_{k,s} + o(1)) n^{k} construct a dependent pair of varieties that are likely both missed, establishing sharpness. This mirrors the proof for k=2, s=1 and generalises the argument to higher degree.
title: Generalized random piercing threshold for families of low‑degree varieties over finite fields

description: For every finite simple graph Γ and every integer s ≥ 1, if Γ contains an s‑clique then there exists a pair (k,λ) arising from that clique such that the generalised CAP polynomial CA_Γ(x,s,k,λ) is non‑negative for all integer values of x. Equivalently, the impossibility of finding an integer x making CA_Γ negative certifies the existence of an s‑clique.
proof_strategy: algorithmic_verification
title: Conjecture on CAP Detectability of Cliques via Non‑negativity

description: Establishes that restricted Rota-Baxter Lie algebras endowed with a weight-1 graph subalgebra structure satisfy the post-Lie bracket defined through an explicit splitting mechanism involving the Rota-Baxter operator, enabling inductive construction of post-Lie structures from Rota-Baxter algebras.
proof_strategy: Constructive induction using Rota-Baxter operator properties and splitting lemma from §3.2
title: Restricted Rota-Baxter Lie algebras of arbitrary weight give rise to restricted post-Lie algebras via splitting property

description:
For any finite partial cube G, the following are equivalent:
1. G is a minimal forbidden pc‑minor for the class of daisy cubes (that is, G is a partial cube that contains a non‑peripheral Θ‑class and every proper pc‑minor of G is a daisy cube).
2. There exist integers r ≥ 2 and s ≥ 1 such that G is isomorphic to the graph obtained from the Cartesian product P₃ⁿ□Qₛ by deleting the two vertices that are opposite in the P₃ⁿ factor and lie in the same Qₛ copy.  In other words, G ≅ (P₃ⁿ□Qₛ) \ {u, v} with u and v the two antipodal corners of the P₃ⁿ factor.

In particular, the infinite family { (P₃ⁿ□Qₛ) \ {u, v} | r ≥ 2, s ≥ 1 } is precisely the set of all minimal forbidden pc‑minors for daisy cubes.
domain_bridges: Partial cubes ↔ isometric subgraphs of hypercubes
Daisy cubes ↔ down‑sets in Boolean lattices
proof_strategy: The proof will proceed by induction on the isometric dimension of a minimal forbidden partial cube G containing a non‑peripheral Θ‑class. First, we show that any such G must have a Θ‑class whose associated convex halfspace is a proper subset of the vertex set and whose peripheral halfspace is a single vertex—this vertex is an ‘extremal’ corner in the hypercube representation. Next, we prove that removing this corner yields a subgraph that is still a partial cube but has one fewer Θ‑class. Repeating this operation at each step forces G to decompose as a Cartesian product of P₃‑factors and a Qₛ‑factor, with the removed corners precisely the two distinct antipodal vertices in the P₃ⁿ component. A structural lemma about minimal non‑peripheral Θ‑classes in partial cubes is required, which can be formalized using the convexity and evenness conditions of Θ‑classes. The final step is to verify that any graph outside this family contains a proper pc‑minor that also fails the peripheral Θ‑class
title: Complete Characterization of Minimal Forbidden Partial‑Cube Minors for Daisy Cubes

description: Conjecture that for all sufficiently large n and all real x with 0 ≤ x ≤ n^{1/3}, the tail probability ratio satisfies |log(P(Y_n > x)/Φ(x))| ≤ C (x^3 + (1+x) log n)/√n, where Y_n = (log q_n - n)/√n and Φ is the standard normal cdf.
proof_strategy: Extend the existing martingale decomposition to control the logarithm of q_n uniformly for larger x up to n^{1/3}, using concentration inequalities and refined bounds on the martingale increments.
title: Uniform Cramér-type moderate deviation bound for Engel digit logarithms up to n^{1/3}

description: The ratio γ(G)/ρ_L(G) is bounded by a universal constant for all graphs. Based on the observed bounds of 3, 4, and 5 for interval graphs, permutation graphs, and asteroidal-triple-free graphs respectively, we conjecture that γ(G)/ρ_L(G) ≤ 6 for all finite simple graphs G, and this bound is tight.
proof_strategy: Prove the conjecture by establishing upper bounds on γ/ρ_L through careful analysis of neighborhood structures and maximal packings. Use induction on graph order and structural decomposition techniques. To show tightness, construct an infinite family of graphs achieving ratio arbitrarily close to 6.
title: Universal Upper Bound on Domination to Lower Packing Ratio

description: For every connected weighted graph G and nonempty vertex set S, the quantity max_{u: 1^T u = 1} u^T R[S] u equals the maximum of u^T R[S] u attained uniquely by a vector u whose entries are proportional to the diagonal of the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse of the reduced Laplacian K = L^S, i.e., u_i = q_i / (∑_j q_j) where q = diag(K^+). This refines the variational characterization of the normalized factor det R[S]/cof R[S].
proof_strategy: Construct a counterexample using a weighted star graph where the maximizer is not proportional to diag(K^+), thereby falsifying the conjecture.
title: Conjecture: Maximizer of u^T R[S] u is proportional to diag(K^+)

description: We conjecture that for a vertex‑transitive graph G and a fixed vertex v0, the finitary upho poset P(G,v0) of walks starting at v0 is multiplicable (i.e., admits an LCIF monoid structure whose left‑divisibility order recovers the poset order) if and only if the automorphism group Aut(G) contains a regular subgroup. This condition is equivalent to G being a Cayley graph. The conjecture refines the Fu‑Peng‑Zhang conjecture and captures the phenomenon exhibited by the Petersen graph (non‑Cayley → non‑multiplicable) and its line graph (Cayley → multiplicable).
proof_strategy: 1. Assuming multiplicability, extract from the LCIF monoid structure a left action of Aut(G) on the set of walks that is transitive and free, yielding a regular subgroup. 2. Assuming a regular subgroup H ≤ Aut(G), define a monoid structure on P(G,v0) by concatenation of walks, identity = empty walk, and left division using the regular action to guarantee uniqueness, left‑cancellativity, and invertible‑free property. Formalize all definitions in Lean (graphs, walks, posets, monoids) and prove the equivalence.
title: Multiplicability of Upho Posets from Vertex-Transitive Graphs

description: Conjecture that there exists an absolute constant c>0 such that for all sufficiently large N, any Sidon set A⊆{1,…,N²} satisfies |A| ≤ N·exp(−c·log N / log log N).
proof_strategy: entropy_method_and_modular_splitting
title: Super‑polylogarithmic bound for Sidon sets in [N²]

description: For any finite set S acted on by the cyclic group G = Z/nZ, the number of G-orbits of size exactly m equals the Möbius-weighted sum over divisors d of n with m|d of μ(d/m)/φ(d) times the number of H-orbits in S, where H is the subgroup of index d. Moreover, this relation uniquely determines the multiset of orbit sizes of G on S.
proof_strategy: Provide a counterexample for a non-cyclic group or show that the formula fails when the action is not faithful, thereby falsifying the conjecture.
title: Conjecture on Möbius-weighted orbit counts for cyclic subgroups

description: We conjecture that for every sink‑free digraph D on n vertices there exists a quasi‑kernel Q such that the closed out‑neighbourhood N_D^+(Q) has size at least 2n/3. This strengthens the 2n/3 bound proved for break digraphs in the paper arXiv:2308.07843 and would imply the small quasi‑kernel conjecture when combined with the trivial bound |Q| ≤ n/2.
proof_strategy: Develop a hereditary framework that isolates the weighted half‑neighbourhood property. Using induction on n and a decomposition of a sink‑free digraph into a break‑digraph core (to which the 2n/3 bound is already known) and a remainder with few sinks, transfer the bound to the general case. Formalise in Lean 4 by defining oriented graphs, independent sets, quasi‑kernels, closed out‑neighbourhoods, and the property, then carry out an inductive construction of the required Q.
title: Weighted Half‑Neighbourhood for All Sink‑Free Digraphs

description: Every connected 1-binding graph G whose spectral radius exceeds 2k+1 contains a spanning subgraph F that is an odd-even factor with respect to some even-cardinality vertex set W, satisfying d_F(u)∈{1,3,…,k} for all u∈W and d_F(v)∈{0,2,…,k+1} for all v∈V(G)∖W.
proof_strategy: Use eigenvalue interlacing and degree sequence constraints to show that the absence of such a factor would force the spectral radius to be ≤ 2k+1, contradicting the hypothesis.
title: Odd-even factor existence in 1-binding graphs under a spectral radius bound

description: For a field k and a torus T whose character lattice over k_s is M with Galois splitting field E/k having Gal(E/k) ≅ S_{n+1}×S_2 acting as specified, any Brauer presentation of H^1(k,T) can only involve the quadratic subextension K = E^{S_{n+1}×{1}} and the degree (n+1) subextension L = E^{S_n×S_2} as source fields; no other intermediate fields of E/k occur as source fields.
proof_strategy: Explicit computation of restriction and corestriction maps in the Brauer group using cohomological Mackey functors, together with Galois cohomology of the group S_{n+1}×S_2 to identify possible intermediate fields.
title: Conjecture on source fields in Brauer presentations of generalized del Pezzo torus torsors

description: For a connected graph G of even order n and an even integer b ≥ 2, if the distance spectral radius μ(G) satisfies μ(G) ≤ (n-2)/b, then G contains an H_b-factor (a spanning subgraph where each vertex degree is either an odd number at most b-1 or exactly b).
proof_strategy: Combine the Lu-Wang sufficient condition based on the number of odd components of G−S with an upper bound on the number of odd components in terms of the distance spectral radius via the Rayleigh quotient and eigenvalue interlacing for the distance matrix. Show that μ(G) ≤ (n-2)/b forces the odd-component condition to hold for every vertex subset S, thereby guaranteeing an H_b-factor.
title: Distance spectral radius threshold for H_b-factors

catalog_references: Conjugacy Class Averages and Sidorenko's Conjecture
description: We conjecture that for any finite group G, any real‑valued function f : G → ℝ, and any bipartite graph H, the homomorphism density of H in the Cayley kernel defined by f satisfies the Sidorenko inequality t(H, G_f) ≥ t(K₂, G_f)^{e(H)}. This extends the paper’s result for 1‑subdivision graphs to all bipartite graphs and would imply that every bipartite graph is strong Sidorenko via conjugacy averaging.
proof_strategy: One could attempt to prove the conjecture by expressing the homomorphism density as a multilinear form and applying the Fourier transform on G. The inequality reduces to a convexity argument on the spectral measure of the Cayley kernel. The case of 1‑subdivision graphs is already proved; extending to arbitrary bipartite graphs would require a general eigenvalue bound for the adjacency operator of the kernel, analogous to known eigenvalue conditions for strong Sidorenko graphs.
title: Sidorenko inequality for Cayley kernels with arbitrary real‑valued functions

description: Let Semiprime be the set of semiprimes (products of two distinct primes). For each N ≥ 2, define the semiprime subset-sum set SS(N) as the set of all finite subset sums ∑_{i=1}^k 1/s_i where s_1 < s_2 < ... < s_k are semiprimes ≤ N (including the empty sum 0). Let gap(SS(N)) denote the maximum gap between consecutive elements of SS(N) when sorted in increasing order. Then lim_{N→∞} gap(SS(N)) = 0. This is the key remaining conjecture for the ω=2 regime below the threshold for rational representability, as stated in the paper.
proof_strategy: The conjecture concerns the density of subset sums of reciprocals of semiprimes. A formalization in Lean 4 would involve: (1) defining semiprimes as numbers with exactly two distinct prime factors, (2) defining the subset-sum set SS(N) inductively, (3) proving that as N increases, new semiprimes add sufficient granularity to reduce the maximum gap. The approach would leverage the unboundedness of semiprimes and their distribution properties, potentially using sieve methods to show that for any ε > 0, there exists N₀(ε) such that for all N ≥ N₀, the gap is less than ε. The paper suggests this can be reduced to elementary bounds combined with Olson's addition theorem for the asymptotic regime.
title: Gap-free floor of semiprime subset-sum set tends to zero

catalog_references: arXiv:2405.12345 (hypothetical paper on extended Eulerian numbers)
description: The extended Eulerian numbers A(n,k,s) = ∑_{j=0}^k (-1)^j C(n+1,j) (k+1-j-s)^n satisfy the recurrence A(n,k,s) = (k+1-s) A(n-1,k,s) + (n-k+s) A(n-1,k-1,s) for n ≥ 1, with boundary conditions A(0,0,s)=1 and A(n,k,s)=0 for k<0 or k>n. This generalizes the classical Eulerian recurrence (s=0).
proof_strategy: Manipulate the sum definition by splitting (k+1-j-s)^n = (k+1-j-s)(k+1-j-s)^{n-1} and reindexing sums, analogous to the classical proof for Eulerian numbers using the Worpitzky identity or generating functions.
title: Recurrence relation for extended Eulerian numbers

description: Conjecture that the sum of all odd parts in all partitions of 5n+1 without repeated odd parts is divisible by 5, i.e., SODO(5n+1) ≡ 0 (mod 5) for all n ∈ ℕ.
proof_strategy: Derive the generating function for SODO(n) using theta function identities, reduce it modulo 5, and show that the coefficients for exponents congruent to 1 mod 5 vanish.
title: Congruence for the sum of odd parts in partitions without repeated odd parts modulo 5

description: For any connected graph G with no isolated vertices, the Laplacian spectral radius μ(G) is bounded above by the maximum over all vertices i of the expression d_i + m_i + sqrt(d_i m_i), where d_i is the degree of vertex i and m_i is the average degree of its neighbors.
proof_strategy: Apply the Collatz-Wielandt comparison theorem to construct a non-negative eigenvector and use the arithmetic mean-geometric mean inequality to validate the bound. Verify via induction on graph structure for small cases and leverage known results for classical bounds.
title: Laplacian Spectral Radius Upper Bound via Vertex-Average Neighbor Degree Combination

description: We conjecture that for every integer d ≥ 1 there exists an inclusion‑minimal convex body K ⊂ ℝ^d whose integer translates cover ℝ^d and such that K is a polytope with exactly 2d facets. This would show that the lower bound "at least 2d facets" proved in the paper is sharp in all dimensions.
proof_strategy: Construct, for each d, an explicit polytope K_d (for example the centrally symmetric cross‑polytope scaled appropriately) and verify three properties in Lean: (1) K_d is convex and compact; (2) K_d + ℤ^d = Set.univ (i.e., the integer translates cover ℝ^d); (3) K_d is inclusion‑minimal with this covering property, meaning that any proper sub‑convex subset fails to cover ℝ^d via integer translates. The first two properties follow from elementary geometry of the cross‑polytope and a lattice‑covering argument. Minimality can be proved by showing that removing any facet creates a gap in the covering, which can be expressed as the existence of a point in ℝ^d whose distance (in the norm induced by K_d) to the integer lattice exceeds 1/2. The facet count is then computed directly from the definition of K_d, yielding exactly 2d facets. All steps are amenable to formalisation using existing lemmas about convex polytopes, Minkowski sums, and covering radii in mathlib.
title: Existence of Minimal Covering Polytopes with Exactly 2d Facets in Every Dimension

catalog_references: Finite field trace and norm maps
description: For the polynomial f(x) = x^q + bx^2 + cx + d over F_{q^2}, we conjecture that f is a permutation polynomial if and only if specific explicit conditions on the coefficients hold: when q is odd, f permutes F_{q^2} iff b, c, d satisfy g(b,c,d) ≠ 0 where g is an explicit polynomial expression derived from Weil sum evaluation; when q is even, f permutes F_{q^2} iff h(b,c,d) ≠ 0 with h being another explicit expression. The precise forms of g and h relate to the discriminant of the associated Weil sum and can be computed via the number of solutions to the equation f(x) = f(y) for x ≠ y.
proof_strategy: Use the Weil sum characterization: f permutes F_{q^2} iff the equation y(f(x)-f(z)) = 0 has exactly one solution for each y ∈ F_{q^2}, which translates to computing the Weil sum S = sum_{x,z∈F_{q^2}} χ(y(f(x)-f(z))) and showing it equals q^2 precisely when the conjectured coefficient conditions hold. The proof involves expanding the character sum, completing the square in the exponent, and applying Gauss sum evaluations.
title: Complete Characterization of Permutation Polynomials x^q + bx^2 + cx + d over F_{q^2}

description: The paper leaves open a single distribution‑equivalence question for two specific length‑2 mesh patterns, say p and q. It is further conjectured that the same equidistribution holds when the permutations are restricted to involutions. We formulate the precise conjecture that for every n≥0 and every k≥0 the number of n‑involutions containing exactly k occurrences of p equals the number containing exactly k occurrences of q. This statement is concrete, falsifiable by computing the bivariate generating functions for involutions, and can be formalized in Lean by defining mesh patterns, involutions, and the occurrence statistic.
proof_strategy: Define the two mesh patterns p and q (the ones appearing in the unresolved distribution‑equivalence question) as structures on permutations. Prove that the map constructed in the paper (the involution on the whole symmetric group) restricts to a bijection on the set of involutions, preserving the number of occurrences of each pattern. This can be done by verifying that the involution sends an involution to an involution (i.e., it commutes with the inverse operation) and that it does not change the pattern‑occurrence count. In Lean, one would: (1) formalise permutations as bijections on fin n, (2) define involutions as permutations equal to their inverse, (3) encode mesh patterns and the occurrence count, (4) implement the bijection from the paper, and (5) prove the two preservation lemmas. Consequently the bivariate generating functions for p and q over involutions coincide, establishing the conjecture.
title: Equidistribution of the unresolved length‑2 mesh patterns on involutions

catalog_references: Secondary terms for first moments of Selmer groups
description: The error terms for cyclic prime twist family moments grow slower than expected due to non-algebraic dependencies, conflicting with conjectural predictions.
proof_strategy: direct computation
title: Error Term Convergence Bound

description: This paper investigates the computational complexity of computing the block tensor rank of sum-rank metric codes, with implications for efficient decoding in high-dimensional data settings.
proof_strategy: Formalize a concrete reconstruction theorem and apply reductions from known tensor decomposition problems.
title: Block Tensor Rank of Sum-Rank Metric Codes

description: The coefficient of q^{16} in the series vanishes modulo 16.
proof_strategy: Modular verification through direct computation
title: Modulo 16 Coefficient Zero

description: The conjecture asserts that for the transfer operator $L$ defined on the Banach space $\mathcal B_R$ of analytic functions on the disk $D$ with real boundary values and bounded derivative, when restricted to the real subspace $\mathcal B_{R,\mathbb R}$ and equipped with the cone of functions having non‑negative derivative on $[0,1]$, the second largest eigenvalue $\lambda_2$ in modulus satisfies $|\lambda_2|\le 0.9$. Moreover, there exists an eigenfunction $\phi$ associated to $\lambda_2$ that can be chosen to satisfy $\phi'(x)\ge 0$ for all $x\in[0,1]$. This statement is falsifiable: a single counterexample where $|\lambda_2|>0.9$ or where no such non‑negative‑derivative eigenfunction exists would disprove it.
proof_strategy: Combine spectral theory of transfer operators with numerical verification using interval arithmetic or validated eigenvalue computations to bound the norm of $L$ on the cone, possibly leveraging known bounds on the Gauss–Kuzmin–Wirsing constant and Ruelle–Perron–Frobenius theory.
title: Conjecture on a universal spectral gap for the Gauss transfer operator on real-analytic functions

description: Formalize the sharp lower bound for the cardinality of the product set of subsets of spheres in a free group. Specifically, for a free group F_m with standard generating set S, if U is a subset of the sphere of radius n (S_n) and V is a subset of the sphere of radius k (S_k), then |UV| ≥ (2/3 + 1/(3 * 4^min(n,k))) * |U| * |V|.
proof_strategy: The proof would likely proceed by induction on the radii n and k, using the tree structure of the Cayley graph of the free group. One must account for the cancellation in the word metric and use the fact that in a tree, the product of two elements from spheres of radii n and k has a well-defined distance based on the length of their common prefix (the Gromov product).
title: Product Growth Bound in Free Groups

description: For the infinite family of complete graphs K_{2n+1}, the rational homology group H_2(conf_3(K_{2n+1}), Q) contains the irreducible S_3-representation indexed by the partition (2,1) with multiplicity exactly n for all n>=1. This multiplicity can be computed combinatorially and is stable under inclusion of K_{2n+1} into K_{2m+1} for m>n.
proof_strategy: Combine functoriality of homology with symmetric group representation theory, use generating functions to predict multiplicities, and verify initial cases computationally; a proof would require showing that the multiplicity function satisfies a linear recurrence that matches the conjectured closed form.
title: Conjecture on stable multiplicities of S_3 representations in H_2 of configuration spaces of complete graphs

description: For a finite field 𝔽_q with q>2, if the point set of the projective space PG(m-1, q) can be partitioned into (n-1)-dimensional subspaces (i.e., an (n-1)-spread exists), then n divides m. This follows from counting points in each subspace and using the divisibility properties of q^a-1.
proof_strategy: Count the number of points in PG(m-1, q) and in an (n-1)-dimensional subspace over 𝔽_q. If the subspaces partition the point set, then (q^m-1)/(q-1) = t·(q^n-1)/(q-1) for some integer t, implying (q^m-1) = t·(q^n-1). Using the known lemma that (q^a-1) | (q^b-1) iff a | b, we deduce n | m.
title: Divisibility condition for spreads in finite projective spaces

description: Conjecture that for any two WQH-type graphs G and G' that are cospectral, equality of the multisets of common neighbour counts between the parts C1 and C2 implies that G and G' are isomorphic.
proof_strategy: Develop a Lean 4 invariant based on the multiset Λ_{C1, C2} of common neighbour counts, and show that its equality forces a graph isomorphism via degree‑preserving bijections and spectral compatibility.
title: Common-neighbour multiset invariant for WQH-switching isomorphism

description: We conjecture that the partial order on ASM(n) induced by the corner sum function (i.e., B ≤ A iff the corner sum of B is pointwise less than or equal to that of A) makes ASM(n) into a lattice, i.e., every pair of ASMs has a greatest lower bound and a least upper bound with respect to this order.
proof_strategy: Use the bijection between ASMs and monotone triangles (or Gelfand-Tsetlin patterns). Show that the weak order on ASMs corresponds to the product order on monotone triangles, which is known to be a lattice because it is a sublattice of a product of chains. Transfer the lattice structure back to ASMs via the bijection.
title: Weak order on alternating sign matrices forms a lattice

description: Conjecture: For every integer C ≥ 0, there exists an integer N such that for all odd integers n > N, the maximum codimension h_2(n) of a cyclically covering subspace of F_2^n exceeds C. This is equivalent to the statement that h_2(n) → ∞ as n → ∞ through odd integers.
proof_strategy: Use the equivalence between h_2(n)=0 and the non-existence of full-weight codewords in binary cyclic codes of length n. Show that for sufficiently large odd n, there exist binary cyclic codes with full-weight codewords, implying h_2(n) cannot be zero. Then, by considering codes with higher minimum distance or using the Discrete Fourier Transform to analyze the vanishing of certain sums, establish that h_2(n) grows without bound. This may involve analytic number theory to show that for large odd n, the number of cyclotomic cosets or the size of certain sets forces h_2(n) to be large.
title: Unboundedness of h_2(n) for odd n

description: For the complete r-uniform hypergraph on n vertices with all edges having the same target bound L_e^+ = L_e^- = L, the exponential criterion from the biased Alon-Krivelevich-Spencer-Szabó theorem admits a closed-form threshold: Balancer can force |D_e| ≤ L for all edges if and only if L > max{r, (p+q)√(rn ln(2))}. This conjecture proposes that the universal constant in the biased discrepancy bound for complete uniform hypergraphs equals 1, matching the classical Chernoff inequality structure.
proof_strategy: Apply the biased exponential criterion to the complete r-uniform hypergraph, simplify using symmetry (all edges have equal size r), and prove both sufficiency and necessity via potential function analysis combining martingale concentration inequalities with explicit strategy constructions for the threshold case.
title: Threshold formula for biased discrepancy game on complete uniform hypergraphs

description: For any finite coloring of R^2, there exists a color class that realizes all pairs (a,b) in R^2 as (c_1(A_v), c_2(A_v)) for some 2-simplex v. This tests whether the impossibility result for c_1 alone can be overcome when combined with c_2.
proof_strategy: Use the directional expansion framework from the paper combined with a parametric family of triangles achieving prescribed (trace, determinant) pairs, and analyze whether the ergodic construction can be adapted to control both coefficients simultaneously.
title: Simultaneous Realization of Trace and Determinant in Finite Colorings

description: Proposes an algorithmic method for computing joins in the weak order of the Coxeter group of type B, with a focus on extending Dyer's geometric conjecture.
proof_strategy: Formalize and analyze the recursive structure of signed permutations in the Coxeter group of type B using formal verification techniques.
title: Computing Joins in the Weak Order of Type B Coxeter Groups

catalog_references: Chapter 6 of the thesis (construction of size n^2/4 + 1)
description: Conjecture that for every even integer n ≥ 6, the maximum cardinality lcs(n) of a critical set in any Latin square of order n equals n^2/4 + 1.
proof_strategy: Prove an upper bound of n^2/4 + 1 for lcs(n) when n is even using combinatorial arguments on intercalates and trade structures, and exhibit a construction achieving this bound, thereby establishing equality.
title: The exact value of the largest critical set size for even orders

description: For RESOCA 115, if p and p+3 are twin periods (i.e., both are periods and p+3 is also a period), then the next pair of twin periods is given by p' = 2p + 3 if p is even, or p' = 2p +6 if p is odd, leading to p' and p'+3 as the next twin periods.
proof_strategy: Induction on the twin period pairs, leveraging properties of the background sequence and the merge construction to establish the recurrence relation for subsequent twin periods.
title: Twin Periods of RESOCA 115 Follow a Recurrence Relation

description: For the h-spacing sum D_{2,h}(Q) defined as the sum of squared distances between Farey fractions that are h positions apart in F_Q, there exists a constant C_h such that the normalized quantity C_h(Q) = D_{2,h}(Q) · Q²/log(Q) is bounded above by C_h < 3 for all Q ≥ 2 and all h ≥ 1, where the bound C_h depends explicitly on h.
proof_strategy: Extend the effective estimation techniques from the consecutive case (h=1) to arbitrary h, using the BCZ-map framework and uniform bounds for Kloosterman sums to handle the longer chains of consecutive Farey fractions. The defect term c_I for subintervals can be controlled via explicit estimates.
title: Generalized Mundici-Type Bounds for h-Spacing Farey Sums

description: For any graph G and any partition selection 𝔓, the degree of the affine flow polynomial φ_G^(𝔓, t) equals the cyclomatic number of G, defined as |E(G)| - |V(G)| + k(G), where k(G) is the number of connected components of G.
proof_strategy: Use induction on the number of edges, leveraging the deletion-contraction recurrence for affine flow polynomials. Base cases (trees, edgeless graphs) can be verified directly. For the inductive step, analyze how deletion/contraction affects the cyclomatic number and the polynomial's degree.
title: Degree of Affine Flow Polynomials Equals Cyclomatic Number

description: This conjecture proposes a recursive decomposition of the q-Whittaker and Macdonald operators using rank recursion, connecting their combinatorial structure to polynomial interpolation and q-deformed binomial distributions. The recursion serves as a foundational tool for analyzing their combinatorial and spectral properties in representation theory.
proof_strategy: Formalize the recurrence using polynomial interpolation properties of q-binomial coefficients, verify via coefficient matching in Lean 4, and connect to q-Hahn identities through case analysis on operator support.
title: Recursive Structure of q-Whittaker and Macdonald Operators via Rank Recursion

description:
For any finite Coxeter group of type A (i.e. the symmetric group S_n) and any parabolic subgroup W_J, the family of normalized parabolic Kazhdan–Lusztig R‑polynomials \(\widetilde R_{x,y}^{J}(q)\) (with \(x,y\in W/W_J\)) satisfies

1. \(\widetilde R_{x,y}^{J}(q) \in \mathbb{Q}_{\ge 0}[q]\) (all coefficients are non‑negative rational numbers), and
2. Evaluating at \(q=1\) gives a stochastic matrix: for each fixed \(x\), \(\sum_{y}\widetilde R_{x,y}^{J}(1)=1\).

Consequently the kernel \(K(x,y)=\widetilde R_{x,y}^{J}(1)\) defines a Markov transition kernel which intertwines the censored stochastic six‑vertex dynamics with its blocking (stationary) measure. This conjecture isolates the algebraic core of the censoring inequality proved in the paper and is falsifiable by explicit computation in small symmetric groups.
proof_strategy: Use the recursive definition of parabolic KL R‑polynomials via the Hecke algebra relations and the known positivity of ordinary KL‑polynomials. Show that the normalisation factor (the sum over y) equals the value of the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis element at q=1, which is 1 for the identity coset. Then induct on the length of coset representatives, exploiting the parabolic recurrence to preserve non‑negativity and the stochastic sum property. Formalise the recursion in Lean using the existing `Mathlib` development of Coxeter groups and Hecke algebras, and verify the base cases by computer‑checked calculation for small n.
title: Positivity and Normalisation of Parabolic Kazhdan–Lusztig R‑Polynomials as Intertwining Kernels

description: This conjecture asserts that when t exceeds half the matrix dimension, the maximal size of a (t-1)-intersection-free family in GL(n,q) is bounded above by the size of a t-umvirate, which is q^{n(n-t)}. The paper indicates a regime change at t > n/2 but leaves this specific quantitative bound unproven.
proof_strategy: Combining algebraic geometry techniques with quantitative hypercontractivity bounds to analyze rank structures in matrix differences
title: Thm: For t > n/2, (t-1)-intersection-free families in GL(n,q) have size strictly less than t-umvirates

description: Conjecture: Up to permutation of the four colors, the only integral geometric 4‑colorings of the full Moser lattice \(L_{Moser}\) are the two colorings described by the parity formulas \(\pi_{\gamma_1}(v)=1+(a+b+d\bmod 2)+2\cdot(a+c+d\bmod 2)\) and the second coloring obtained from \(\pi_{\gamma_1}\) by swapping colors (e.g., interchanging colors 2 and 3). Equivalently, any integral geometric 4‑coloring of \(L_{Moser}\) arises from a sublattice of index 4 (the kernel of the coloring), and the only sublattices of index 4 are those generated in the basis \(\{1,\omega_1,\omega_3,\omega_1\omega_3\}\) by the vectors \((2,0,0,0), (0,2,0,0), (0,0,2,0), (0,0,0,2)\) together with the diagonal \((1,1,1,1)\). This yields exactly two inequivalent colorings. The conjecture is falsifiable: if another integral geometric 4‑coloring exists, the Lean formalisation will refute it.
proof_strategy: 1. Formalise the definition of an integral geometric coloring in Lean (distance‑preserving condition). 2. Define the Moser lattice \(L_{Moser}\) as the \(\mathbb Z\)-module generated by \(1,\omega_1,\omega_3,\omega_1\omega_3\) with the given algebraic relations. 3. Implement a search over all sublattices of index 4 (finitely many up to automorphisms). 4. For each sublattice compute the induced coloring via the coset decomposition and verify the geometric condition using the explicit distance formula in the lattice. 5. Show that only the two described colorings satisfy the condition, up to permutation of the four colors. 6. Use Lean tactics (`simp`, `ring`, `decide`, `cases`) to automate parity checks and distance congruences.
title: Classification of integral geometric 4‑colorings of the Moser lattice

description: This conjecture posits that the asymptotic density of the Deleted Hypergraphs $F_{r,s,t}$ satisfying certain structural thresholds exhibits a precise growth rate dictated by a linear combination of logarithmic and inverse power laws. It bridges discrete geometry, extremal combinatorics, and the theoretical foundations of Lean mathematics.
proof_strategy: Constructive asymptotic analysis with subparameterized counting
title: Hypergraph Turán-type problem with logarithmic density gaps

description: The bigraded Hilbert series of the GL_n(F_q)-superspace coinvariant ring SR equals the product formula: ∏_{i=1}^n ((1-t^i)/(1-t))^2 · ∏_{j=1}^{n-1} ((1-z^{q^j})/(1-z)) where the first product accounts for the commutative grading of invariant polynomials and the second for the exterior grading structure arising from the differential forms action.
proof_strategy: Verify the conjecture by computing the Hilbert series explicitly for small values of n (n=1,2,3) and q (q=2,3) using character theory of GL_n(F_q) and the known degrees of basic invariants, then prove the general case by induction on n using the structure of the superspace algebra Ω as an induced module for the Borel subgroup of upper triangular matrices in GL_n(F_q).
title: Bigraded Hilbert series formula for GL_n(F_q) superspace coinvariants

description: Conjecture: For a factorial association scheme over a field F of characteristic zero, each block algebra of the Terwilliger F-algebra corresponding to a primitive idempotent of the Bose-Mesner algebra is a full matrix algebra over F. Consequently, the Terwilliger algebra is semisimple and its Jacobson radical is zero.
proof_strategy: Apply the double centralizer theorem: the Terwilliger algebra is the centralizer of the adjacency (Bose-Mesner) algebra in the endomorphism algebra of the permutation module. Over a field of characteristic zero the Bose-Mesner algebra is semisimple, so its centralizer decomposes as a direct sum of full matrix algebras whose sizes are the multiplicities of the irreducible Bose-Mesner modules. For factorial schemes these multiplicities are determined by the factorial valencies, yielding explicit matrix dimensions. Since a direct sum of matrix algebras has zero Jacobson radical, the Terwilliger algebra is semisimple.
title: Semisimplicity and Matrix Structure of Block Algebras in Terwilliger Algebras of Factorial Association Schemes

catalog_references: Bondy & Murty (1976). Graph Theory with Applications.
description: We conjecture that for any fan graph F_n (n ≥ 2) and any wheel graph W_n (n ≥ 4), the all‑negative signature uniquely maximizes the frustration index when the underlying cycle (for wheels) or the path length (for fans) is odd. When the length is even, there are exactly two signatures achieving the same maximal frustration index: the all‑negative signature and the signature obtained by switching the apex vertex (or equivalently, flipping the signs of all edges incident to the hub).
proof_strategy: Using the switching invariance of the frustration index, reduce the problem to maximizing the number of consistent edges. For fan and wheel graphs the structure forces the all‑negative signature to be optimal by parity arguments on the unique cycle. Any other signature can be transformed via switching to a signature with a strictly smaller maximum consistent cut, thus yielding a smaller frustration index. The parity of the cycle determines whether the all‑negative signature is the only maximizer or shares the maximum with its switched counterpart.
title: Parity-based uniqueness of the all‑negative signature for fan and wheel graphs

description: For s=3 q-ary Hamming balls of equal radius t centered at points c¹, c², c³ in ℤ_q^n with minimum pairwise distance d, and for all q≥2, q≠6 and sufficiently large n, the maximum intersection size equals V_q(n,t-d/2+1) when d is even, and V_q(n,t-(d-1)/2) when d is odd, provided d ≤ 2t. This conjecture extends the claimed necessary and sufficient conditions in the paper to an explicit closed-form expression for the maximum intersection cardinality.
proof_strategy: Verify the conjectured formula by: (1) proving it matches known small cases through exhaustive computation, (2) establishing the structural necessary conditions from the paper's exact formula imply this form, (3) showing sufficiency by constructing center point configurations achieving this bound, and (4) using asymptotic analysis for large n to confirm the conjecture holds in the limit. The proof would require careful case analysis on the weight distribution and support overlaps of the center points.
title: Conjectured Formula for Maximum Intersection Size of Three q-ary Hamming Balls

description: We conjecture that every definable bipartite graph in a 1‑semi‑equational theory satisfies the strong Erdős–Hajnal property with a uniform constant depending only on the formula and the theory. In particular, for any partitioned formula φ(x,y) in a 1‑semi‑equational theory T there exists β>0 such that for all finite sets X,Y and all probability measures μ on X, ν on Y, there are subsets X0⊆X,Y0⊆Y with μ(X0),ν(Y0)≥β and either X0×Y0⊆Eφ or X0×Y0∩Eφ=∅.
proof_strategy: The conjecture would follow by proving that 1‑semi‑equational formulas admit a uniform weak‑normal decomposition analogous to the one‑based case, and then applying the structural arguments used for one‑based theories. A key step is to show that any finite set of parameters can be refined into finitely many “equivalence classes’’ on which the formula is constant, with the number of classes bounded uniformly. This would yield a uniform bound β on the size of a homogeneous subgraph.
title: Strong Erdős–Hajnal for 1‑Semi‑Equational Theories

description: Prove that for a finite, connected, simple, unweighted graph G with Bakry-Émery curvature bounded below by K > 0, if the (Δ-1)-th eigenvalue of the non-normalized Laplacian satisfies λ_{Δ-1} = K, where Δ is the maximum degree of G, then G is isomorphic to the Δ-dimensional hypercube graph H_Δ.
proof_strategy: 1. Formalize the Bakry-Émery curvature operator (Γ₂) for unweighted graphs. 2. Implement the non-normalized Laplacian and its spectrum. 3. Define the spectral embedding into ℝ^{Δ} using the first eigenspace. 4. Use the condition λ_{Δ-1} = K to show that the local curvature matrices at each vertex are constrained to be those of a hypercube. 5. Prove that this local structure forces a global isomorphism to H_Δ via induction on the dimension or by reconstructing the Cartesian product structure.
title: Spectral Rigidity of Hypercubes via Bakry-Émery Curvature

description: For every partition λ ⊢ n+1 and every removable corner c ∈ D(λ), the tangent weights of the torus action on Hilb^{n,n+1}(𝔸²) at the fixed point (I_λ, I_{λ\c}) are given by the multiset { α(b) : b ∈ D(λ) } ∪ { β(b) : b ∈ Add(λ\c) }, where α(b) = (a(b)+1, -ℓ(b)) for b ≠ c with a(b), ℓ(b) the arm and leg lengths in λ, α(c) = (0,0) (excluded), and β(b) = (a'(b), -ℓ'(b)-1) with a'(b), ℓ'(b) the arm and leg lengths in λ\c, modified by the shortening rule: if b shares its row with c then a'(b) := a'(b)-1, if b shares its column with c then ℓ'(b) := ℓ'(b)-1. This formula, verified by Macaulay2 for |λ| ≤ 16, is conjectured to hold for all n ≥ 1.
proof_strategy: Extend the computational verification by proving the monomial syzygy description of the compatibility kernel is uniform in n. Use the arrow basis of Hom(I,R/I) to show the kernel conditions impose exactly the shortening rule on arm-leg weights. Formalize the bijection between kernel basis elements and boxes in D(λ) ∪ Add(λ\c) with the stated weights.
title: Universal Tangent Weight Formula for Nested Hilbert Scheme Fixed Points

description: For every noncrossing matching σ corresponding to a two-row standard Young tableau, the polynomial ideal I_σ defined in the paper is a radical ideal. This conjecture asserts that these ideals not only define the irreducible components of two-row Springer fibers set-theoretically but also as reduced subvarieties.
proof_strategy: Verify radicality by constructing a primary decomposition with minimal primes, or show the ideal is Cohen-Macaulay with a linear resolution. Compare with known radicality results for related ideals in matrix Schubert varieties.
title: Radicality of ideals defining two-row Springer fiber components

description: The hyperfunction associated with the Riemann zeta-function on the critical line, when normalized by a factor involving log log T, has moment generating functions identical to those derived from the characteristic polynomial of a random matrix from the circular unitary ensemble, matching the Keating-Snaith conjecture's predictions for all κ ∈ ℂ² with Re(κ₁+κ₂) > -1.
proof_strategy: Formalize hyperfunction definitions in Lean 4, establish moment equality via transfer of statistical properties between zeta-function and CUE matrices, leverage existing proofs of Keating-Snaith for exponential functions.
title: Equivalence of Hyperfunction Moments Between Riemann Zeta and Circular Unitary Ensemble

description: The conjecture that the D-chromatic index of G satisfies χ'_D(G) ≤ (1/2)Δ² + 1/2 Δ, formalizable as a precise mathematical statement.
proof_strategy: Direct verification via inductive bounds on Δ
title: Optimal D-Coloring Bounding

catalog_references: Erdős (1942) elementary proof for log p(n)
description: The paper establishes log pp(n) ~ 2π√(n/(3 log n)) for partitions into primes using an elementary three-step method (recursive formula, exponential sum bound, elementary sum evaluation). This conjecture posits that the same method adapts to partitions into prime powers (including primes themselves and higher powers p^k for k ≥ 2). Let pp_pow(n) denote the number of partitions of n into prime powers. Conjecture: log pp_pow(n) ~ 2π√(n/(3 log n)). This is falsifiable because the constant factor could differ if prime powers contribute significantly to the asymptotics, and the elementary method might fail to control the additional terms from higher prime powers.
domain_bridges: Analytic number theory (prime number theorem for prime powers)
proof_strategy: Follow the paper's three-step recipe: (R1) Derive a recursive inequality for pp_pow(n) analogous to Erdős's recurrence, accounting for all prime powers. (R2) Bound pp_pow(n) by a double sum over prime powers a and integers k, with weights φ(a)e^{-ψ(a,k)}. (R3) Evaluate the sum by splitting prime powers into primes (dominant) and higher powers (negligible), using Chebyshev-type estimates for the prime power counting function π_k(x) = #{p^k ≤ x}. The key is showing higher prime powers contribute o(√(n/log n)) to the logarithm.
title: Elementary Asymptotics for Partitions into Prime Powers

description: For the planted submatrix model with k planted communities of size n^α each, the sharp threshold for degree-D strong separation between two planted hypotheses occurs precisely when the signal-to-noise ratio crosses the critical value λ_c = 1/(k(k-1)), matching the low-degree recovery threshold. Specifically, for any fixed k ≥ 2 and α ∈ (0,1), strong separation is achievable if and only if D > D_c(λ) = k(k-1)λ for λ > λ_c, where λ measures the signal strength relative to noise.
proof_strategy: Extend the low-degree framework by constructing explicit degree-D polynomial tests that achieve strong separation when D > D_c(λ), using spectral methods combined with moment matching techniques. For the converse, apply the degree-D advantage upper bound via careful tensor analysis of the planted-vs-planted likelihood ratio, tracking the sharp constant through the pruning of non-signal contributions.
title: Sharp Threshold Equivalence for Planted Submatrix Testing

description: This conjecture establishes a residue-class equidistribution of the statistic τ(μ) (number of parts strictly larger than the smallest part) on the family D₃(n), showing it is uniformly distributed modulo 3. Furthermore, it proposes a canonical bijection ιₙ: C₃(n) → D₃⁰(n) (where D₃⁰(n) is the τ≡0 mod 3 subset) constructed via a composition of four transformation maps. The bijection is validated through AI-assisted exploration and Lean formalization.
proof_strategy: Use AI-guided recursive decomposition of partitions in D₃(n), formalize equidistribution via generating functions, and construct ιₙ using Lean-verified recursive bijections between Young tableau-like structures.
title: Residue Class Equidistribution and Bijection Between Cubic Partition Families via AI-Assisted Methods

description: Every temporal clique on n vertices admits a temporal spanner of size at most 3n, improving the 7n upper bound from the referenced paper. This conjecture asserts that the constant factor in the linear spanner size for temporal cliques can be reduced, and that the true extremal constant lies between 2 and 3.
proof_strategy: Improve the greedy edge-selection algorithm from the reference paper by analyzing the structure of temporal cliques more carefully, potentially using amortized analysis or improved charging schemes to reduce the constant factor from 7 to 3. The approach would involve demonstrating that each vertex can be assigned at most 3 edges in the spanner while maintaining temporal connectivity.
title: Tight Linear Bound for Temporal Clique Spanners

description: For every r ≥ 3, k ≥ 3, and n ≥ (r-2)(k-2)+1, there exists a linear r-uniform hypergraph H on n vertices with edge count |E(H)| = ((k-2)/(r²((r-2)(k-2)+1)))n² + n/r - 1 that does not contain a k-edge configuration spanning at most (r-2)k+3 vertices. This would establish the tightness of the threshold in Theorem 1 of the paper.
proof_strategy: Construct an explicit family of hypergraphs achieving the lower bound or use probabilistic methods to demonstrate existence; might involve careful averaging arguments similar to those in the paper.
title: Tightness of the Density Threshold for Configurations in Linear Hypergraphs

description: Every planar graph admits a conflict-free coloring with exactly 4 colors, and this statement is equivalent to the Four Color Theorem over ZFC set theory. More precisely, for any planar graph G, there exists a vertex coloring f: V(G) → {1,2,3,4} such that every vertex v has a neighbor w where color f(w) appears exactly once in the open neighborhood N(v), and the existence of such a 4-coloring for all planar graphs is interderivable with the Four Color Theorem.
proof_strategy: Establish the forward direction by constructing an explicit 4-coloring algorithm using the refined Gallai-Edmonds decomposition, then prove the backward direction by showing that any planar graph requiring 4 colors for conflict-free coloring must contain a subgraph that violates the Four Color Theorem. The equivalence follows from demonstrating that both statements have the same logical strength and can be used to prove each other via constructive transformations.
title: Equivalence Between Four Color Theorem and Conflict-Free Chromatic Number of Planar Graphs

description: Conjecture that a rank four Nahm sum of the form Σ q^Q(i,j,k,l)/((q;q)_i(q;q)_j(q;q)_k(q;q)_l) where Q is a quadratic form in four variables is modular (expressible as an infinite product of q-Pochhammer symbols) if and only if the discriminant of Q's Hessian matrix equals 8, 12, or 16. This would generalize the proven cases in the paper where discriminants compute to these values.
proof_strategy: Compute the Hessian matrix of the quadratic form in each exponent, determine its discriminant, verify it matches one of the allowed values {8,12,16}, then apply the Bailey lemma or Bailey pair machinery to establish the sum-to-product identity. For the converse, use modularity constraints to show that other discriminants cannot yield modular forms.
title: Characterization of Modular Rank Four Nahm Sums via Discriminant Condition

description: Formalize the statement that for a family of graphs on the same vertex set, the partition of connected components of their union is the join (in the partition lattice) of their individual connected component partitions. This is a key combinatorial lemma used in the ETH-hardness reduction for Global Label Min-Cut.
proof_strategy: Use the fact that two vertices are in the same component of the union iff there is a path using edges from the union, which corresponds to the transitive closure of the union of relations, which is the join of the equivalence relations.
title: Join of Partition Lattices Corresponds to Graph Union Connectivity

description: Let $f \in \mathcal{O}_K[X]$ be a monic irreducible polynomial defining a finite extension of $K$, where $K$ is a finite extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. Suppose the Newton polygon of $f$ with respect to some monic irreducible $\varphi \in \mathcal{O}_K[X]$ satisfies Montes and Nart's index conditions (i.e., the indices of the equation order induced by $f$ are trivial). Then, the decomposition group of any prime $\mathfrak{p}$ of $\mathcal{O}_K$ in the splitting field of $f$ is isomorphic to the subgroup of the Galois group constructed via the Newton polygon method described in the paper. This conjecture formalizes the claim that the algorithmic procedure extends to the weaker index assumptions.
proof_strategy: Formalize the Newton polygon decomposition algorithm in Lean, then prove that under Montes-Nart index conditions, the constructed group matches the decomposition group by verifying compatibility with ramification filtrations and Frobenius actions.
title: Decomposition Group Computation via Newton Polygon Indices

description: Formalizes a precise conjecture about the asymptotic distribution of ordered pairs satisfying the sum-of-divisors identity, leveraging analytic growth estimates and sieve techniques.
proof_strategy: Construct a three-parameter rational solution and apply a sieve to uniformize solutions across divisor classes.
title: Resolution of Erdős Problem 1061 using analytic and combinatorial methods

description: For every integer m ≥ 2 and every integer k ≥ 0, there exists a natural number n such that the 2-adic valuation of t_m(n) is at least k.

description: Given a $q$-ary alphabet $\Sigma_q$ and two sequences $x, y \in \Sigma_q^n$, if their $(s-1)$-deletion balls are disjoint ($D_{s-1}(x) \cap D_{s-1}(y) = \emptyset$), then the size of the intersection of their $t$-deletion balls is bounded by $|D_t(x) \cap D_t(y)| \le \binom{2s}{s}\binom{n-s}{t-s}$ for $t \ge s$.
proof_strategy: The proof requires formalizing the notion of 'runs' in sequences and the 'subsequence' relation ($\preccurlyeq$). One would use a combinatorial counting argument to bound the number of common subsequences based on the fact that if $D_{s-1}(x)$ and $D_{s-1}(y)$ are disjoint, the 'edit distance' or structural difference between $x$ and $y$ is sufficiently large. The Lean proof would likely utilize the `Finset` library for counting and a recursive definition of the subsequence relation, followed by an inductive proof on $n$ and $t$.
title: Upper Bound on Deletion-Ball Intersection under Lower-Order Disjointness

title: Conjecture on quadratic irrational stripe densities in aperiodic Wang tiles

title: Quantitative bound for multi-colored induced join-free partition

description: For any tournament T (complete oriented graph), the P3-direct convexity and P3^s-direct convexity coincide if and only if T contains no transitive directed triangle as an induced subtournament. This conjecture provides a structural characterization linking tournament theory to convex geometry properties.
proof_strategy: Prove both directions: (1) If a tournament has no transitive triangle, then every directed P3 with endpoints in a convex set must have the arc between endpoints, making both convexities equivalent; (2) If a tournament has a transitive triangle (u,v,w) with u→v→w and u→w, construct a set whose convex hulls differ between the two convexity notions.
title: Characterization of When P3-Direct Convexity Equals P3^s-Direct Convexity in Tournaments

description:
For a finite field ϵ_q of order q and integers n ≥ (s+1)k, the maximum number m_q(n,k,s) of k‑dimensional subspaces of an n‑dimensional ϵ_q‑vector space that contain no s+1 mutually independent members (i.e. no s+1 subspaces whose sum is direct) equals the maximum of the two natural constructions: all k‑subspaces inside a fixed ((s+1)k−1)‑dimensional subspace, and all k‑subspaces that meet a fixed s‑dimensional subspace non‑trivially. Explicitly, for n ≥ (s+1)k:

m_q(n,k,s) = max { [((s+1)k−1) choose k]_q , [n choose k]_q – q^{ks} [n−s choose k]_q }.

This conjecture generalises the Erdős–Gallai theorem to vector spaces and is still open for arbitrary k, s and n.
proof_strategy: Use Lovász’s minimax theorem for matroid matchings to relate the extremal size to the fractional matching number in the associated matroid. Apply a high‑dimensional Hoffman bound for uniform hypergraphs over the lattice of subspaces to obtain upper bounds that match the two constructions. Then develop a stability argument that shows any family attaining the upper bound must be structurally close to one of the two extremal families, and finally exploit design‑theoretic counting to rule out all other configurations. The proof would combine linear‑algebraic isoperimetric inequalities, spectral techniques on the Grassmann graph, and matroid intersection theory.
title: Vector‑Space Erdős Matching Conjecture (full case)

title: Non-similarity of Vishik-equivalent semi-singular quadratic forms in characteristic 2

description: Formalize the regularization of the sum of all prime numbers by defining a specific analytic continuation of the prime zeta function P(s) = ∑ p^(-s) into a domain beyond its natural boundary (Re(s) = 0), and prove that the regularized sum (the value of the continuation at s = -1) converges to a specific constant value.
proof_strategy: 1. Define the prime zeta function P(s) as a Dirichlet series. 2. Implement the singular expansion of P(s) near the imaginary axis using the relationship between P(s) and the Riemann zeta function ζ(s) via the Mobius inversion formula: P(s) = ∑_{n=1}^∞ μ(n)/n * log ζ(ns). 3. Use the properties of the logarithm of the Riemann zeta function near its zeros and poles to construct a regularized limit or a specific path-dependent continuation. 4. Evaluate the resulting expression at s = -1.
title: Regularized Sum of Primes via Analytic Continuation Beyond the Natural Boundary

description: Every Veronese circuit achieving the sharp bound dim L = (t+m-2)/m arises from a rational-normal-curve configuration, and conversely, rational-normal-curve configurations achieve this bound if and only if the number of linear forms satisfies t = m·(dim L - 1) + 2. This conjecture asserts that the main dimension bound is not only sharp but fully characterized by rational normal curve constructions.

Coding theory (Schur powers and Kneser-type theorems)

The converse direction follows by explicit computation of rational-normal-curve Veronese images.
title: Classification of extremal Veronese circuits via rational normal curves

description: Conjecture: For an odd prime p, integer ℓ with 1 ≤ ℓ ≤ (p-1)/2, and a symmetric subset S ⊆ Z_p\{0\} with 0 ∉ S, the undirected Cayley graph Cay(Z_p,S) contains a cycle C_{2ℓ+1} as a subgraph if and only if S contains a subset of size 2ℓ+1 whose elements sum to zero in Z_p.
proof_strategy: Use the polynomial method (Combinatorial Nullstellensatz) to show that a zero-sum subset of size 2ℓ+1 yields a solution to the system of equations defining a cycle, and conversely extract a zero-sum subset from a given cycle via its edge differences. The symmetry of S allows reordering of differences to obtain a subset of S. Character sums over Z_p handle the distinctness condition on vertices.
title: Zero-sum characterization of odd cycles in symmetric Cayley graphs over prime cyclic groups

description: We conjecture that the support of any infinite rational series with rational terms has positive density on all sufficiently large dyadic blocks, with the deficit constant depending only on the denominator. This refines and implies a conjecture from the given ArXiv paper on positive densities for rational series, using integral carries and carry geometry.
proof_strategy: Assume density vanishes on a block, then use carry pressure lower bound and upper bound via stopping-time budget to derive contradiction. Uses four local carry estimates: complete-lap mass balance, total-support summation, fixed-pin confinement, and class-one realization.
title: Positive dyadic density of rational series supports via carry recurrence

description: Conjecture that the completion threshold ratio satisfies \(\displaystyle \limsup_{n\to\infty} \frac{qc(n)}{n}=0.216\). Equivalently, there exist infinitely many board sizes n for which qc(n) \geq c n\) for some constant c > 0.216, and no constant larger than 0.216 can serve as a universal lower bound.

title: Tight asymptotic bound for the n‑queens completion threshold

description: Conjecture that for all integers k ≥ 5, the 3-color shift number s₃(k) equals the square of the (k-2)-fold tower of twos evaluated at 2, i.e., s₃(k) = (twr_{k-2}(2))².
proof_strategy: Proceed by induction on k. For the base case k=5, verify s₃(5) = (twr₃(2))² = (2^{2^{2}})² = 64 via explicit construction. For the inductive step, assume the formula holds for k and construct a 3-coloring of (k+1)-subsets that avoids large monochromatic homogeneous sets by taking a product of the coloring for k with a 2-coloring of pairs, then apply the stepping-up lemma for shift numbers to show that s₃(k+1) ≥ (twr_{k-1}(2))². Conversely, use a density increment argument to show that any 3-coloring of (k+1)-subsets of a set of size (twr_{k-1}(2))² must contain a monochromatic homogeneous set of size k+1, establishing the upper bound.
title: Exact value of the 3-color shift number

description: We conjecture that for any prime power q, any extension degree h>1, and any integer k≥2, the maximum cardinality of an additive strong blocking set B in PG(k‑1,q) that does not contain a hyperplane is exactly q^{k‑1}. Moreover, this bound is attained: there always exists a nondegenerate minimal additive code over F_{q^h} of F_q‑dimension k whose associated additive strong blocking set has size |B| = q^{k‑1}. Consequently, the upper bound derived in the literature is tight and the existence of extremal codes follows from explicit constructions using additive codes.
proof_strategy: The proof would proceed in two parts. (1) Upper bound: Using the strong blocking property, one shows that any non‑outer additive strong blocking set B in PG(k‑1,q) can be partitioned into fibres of a map from the complement to B, leading to the inequality |B| ≤ q^{k‑1}. This follows from counting arguments and the fact that each line not meeting B can be used to bound the number of points in B. (2) Existence: Construct an explicit additive code by taking a generator matrix whose columns are the points of a maximal partial spread in PG(k‑1,q) of size q^{k‑1}. Such partial spreads are known to exist for all q and k (e.g., via affine geometry constructions). The code is nondegenerate and minimal because removing any column destroys the strong blocking property. Formalising these constructions in Lean 4 will require definitions of finite fields, vector spaces, subspaces, projective geometry, and the strong blocking condition.
title: Conjecture: Exact extremal size of non‑outer additive strong blocking sets

description:
For any generic cohomological cuspidal automorphic representation \(\pi\) of \(\GL_n\) over a number field, the Betti‑Whittaker period of its contragredient \(\pi^\vee\) is the algebraic reciprocal of the period of \(\pi\) up to an explicit factor depending only on the central character and the archimedean gamma factors.  Formally, there exists an algebraic number \(C(\pi)\in\Qbar\) such that
\[\mathrm{P}_{\betti}(\pi^\vee)=\frac{C(\pi)}{\mathrm{P}_{\betti}(\pi)}.\]
This generalises Chen’s theorem by removing regularity hypotheses and extending to all generic cohomological representations.
proof_strategy: Use the global functional equation for the Rankin–Selberg convolution \(L(s,\pi\times\pi^\vee)\).  Associate to each place a local zeta integral representing the Betti‑Whittaker period and compare the local gamma factors in the functional equation with the local Whittaker integrals.  By the multiplicativity of local factors, the ratio of the global periods equals the product of the archimedean constants, which are algebraic by Deligne’s conjecture on critical values.  The explicit constant \(C(\pi)\) is expressed in terms of the central character and the local epsilon factors at infinity.
title: Period Relation for Betti‑Whittaker Periods of Contragredient Generic Cohomological Representations of GL(n)

description: For any finite group Γ, real-valued function f: Γ → ℝ, and directed cycle Cₙ of length n, the homomorphism density satisfies t(Cₙ, 𝒞_f) ≥ (𝔼_{g∈Γ} f(g))^(2n). This provides a concrete falsifiable statement about the Sidorenko inequality for directed cycles in the two-sided correlation construction.
proof_strategy: Formalize the kernel definition and density calculations in Lean 4, then prove the inequality by establishing the recurrence relation for directed cycle densities and applying Jensen's inequality to the expectation of f. The key is to leverage the correlation structure of 𝒞_f to show that directed cycles satisfy the Sidorenko bound.
title: Sidorenko Inequality for Directed Cycles in Two-Sided Group Correlation Kernels

description: Conjecture: Let G be a finite group. If G is not nilpotent and the deleted co-maximal subgroup graph Γ*(G) contains a cycle, then the girth of Γ*(G) equals 3. Equivalently, Γ*(G) has girth 4 only when G is nilpotent.
proof_strategy: First, use the paper's result that Γ*(G) is either a star or contains a cycle of length 3 or 4. Second, show that if G is not nilpotent then Γ*(G) cannot be a star (by the classification of star groups). Third, construct three subgroups H, K, L such that each pair product equals G but no pair of them is contained in a maximal subgroup that would force a 4‑cycle, yielding a triangle. This construction relies on the existence of a non‑normal maximal subgroup and its core, together with a Sylow subgroup not contained in that maximal subgroup.
title: Girth of the deleted co-maximal subgroup graph is three for non-nilpotent finite groups

description: If the endpoint restriction conjecture for the 3-dimensional paraboloid P₃ over finite fields (where -1 is not a square) holds, then the integer lattice points on the 3-dimensional Euclidean paraboloid form a Λ(3) set, characterized by having additive energy bounded by O(|S|³^(2/3)) for subsets S of size O(1).

description: For a pure r-dimensional simplicial complex K on n vertices satisfying the homological condition H̃_t(lk_K(σ), ℝ) = 0 for all faces σ with |σ| = r-t, if the (r-1)-up signless Laplacian spectral radius q_{r-1}(K) is within ε of the upper bound tn - (t-1)(r+1), then K is within edit distance O(εn) of the extremal join structure Δ_{r+1-t} ⋆ Δ^{t}_{n-r-1+t}, where the edit distance counts vertices whose deletion makes the complexes isomorphic.
proof_strategy: Use variational characterizations of the signless Laplacian spectral radius, analyze the structure of near-extremal eigenvectors via Hodge decomposition on links, apply homological stability lemmas to control local deviations from the extremal structure, and employ combinatorial arguments to bound the global edit distance in terms of spectral gap.

description:
For a finite simple co‑chordal graph G let \(\overline G\) be its chordal complement and let \(\kappa(\overline G)\) denote the size of a smallest vertex separator of \(\overline G\) (i.e., the minimum cardinality of a set whose removal disconnects \(\overline G\)). The conjecture asserts that the projective dimension of the edge ideal \(I(G)\) is given by
\[\operatorname{pdim}\bigl(S/I(G)\bigr) = |V(G)| - \kappa(\overline G) - 1.\]
Equivalently, the largest homological degree appearing in the linear strand formula (1) of the paper coincides exactly with the complement’s minimal separator size. This provides a purely graph‑theoretic invariant that determines the homological invariant \(\operatorname{pdim}\) for the whole class of co‑chordal graphs, extending the partial result proved in the paper for glued clique complexes where \(\kappa(\overline G)=\min\{r_m\}\). The statement is falsifiable: one can compute \(\kappa(\overline G)\) and \(\operatorname{pdim}(S/I(G))\) for any co‑chordal graph (e.g., via Macaulay2) and check equality.
proof_strategy: 1. Formalize finite simple graphs, edge ideals, and chordal/complement notions in Lean using existing graph libraries. 2. Define vertex separators and prove basic properties (existence, minimality). 3. Show that for a co‑chordal graph G, its complement \(\overline G\) is chordal, hence admits a perfect elimination ordering; use this ordering to construct the glued clique complex described in the paper. 4. Prove that the minimal separator size of \(\overline G\) equals the minimum intersection size \(\min_{m}\{r_m\}\) appearing in the glued complex (by analysing the perfect elimination ordering and the way facets are glued). 5. Using the explicit Betti formula (1) from the paper, translate the bound on the maximal homological degree into the expression \(|V(G)|-\min\{r_m\}-1\). 6. Combine steps 4 and 5 to obtain the desired equality \(\operatorname{pdim}(S/I(G)) = |V(G)|-\kappa(\overline G)-1\). 7. Verify base cases (trees, split graphs, threshold graphs) by computation and then lift to
title: Projective Dimension of Edge Ideals of Co‑Chordal Graphs via Minimal Separators

description: Let k be a number field, p a prime, Σ a (possibly empty) set of p‑adic primes of k, and let N∞/k be the unique Σ‑ramified ℤₚ‑extension (assuming it exists). Denote by X_Σ(N∞) = Gal(M_Σ(N∞)/N∞) the Σ‑ramified unramified Iwasawa module, which is a module over the Iwasawa algebra Λ = ℤₚ⟦Gal(N∞/k)⟧ ≅ ℤₚ⟦T⟧. The conjecture asserts that X_Σ(N∞) is a torsion Λ‑module; equivalently, Λ‑rank X_Σ(N∞) = 0. This statement is a precise, falsifiable generalisation of Greenberg’s conjecture to arbitrary Σ‑ramified ℤₚ‑extensions and is amenable to formalisation in Lean‑4 using existing libraries for number fields, Galois groups, profinite groups and Iwasawa algebras.
domain_bridges: AlgebraicNumberTheory ↔ CommutativeAlgebra (torsion modules over power series rings)
proof_strategy: Develop the necessary Lean infrastructure for (i) the construction of the maximal abelian pro‑p extension M_Σ(N∞) unramified outside Σ, (ii) the identification of Gal(N∞/k) with ℤₚ and thus the Iwasawa algebra Λ ≅ ℤₚ⟦T⟧, (iii) the module structure of X_Σ(N∞) over Λ, and (iv) a reduction to known finiteness results: show that the Λ‑rank of X_Σ(N∞) equals the λ‑invariant of the corresponding Iwasawa µ‑invariant, and use the control theorem together with known vanishing of µ‑invariant in the Σ‑ramified setting. The conjecture can be disproved by constructing a concrete Σ‑ramified ℤₚ‑extension (e.g., via explicit class field theory) where the λ‑invariant is shown to be positive, yielding a non‑torsion Λ‑module.
title: Torsionness of Σ‑ramified Iwasawa modules over a ℤₚ‑extension
