catalog_references: Cameron, P., & Puleo, J. (2022). *On the saturation number of joins of graphs*. Discrete Math. 345, 112867.
Erdős, P., Hajnal, A., & Moon, J. (1964). *A problem in graph theory*. Amer. Math. Monthly 71, 939–943.
description:
We conjecture a precise necessary and sufficient condition on a non‑empty graph F (allowing isolated vertices) for which the Cameron–Puleo inequality

\[\operatorname{sat}(n, K_{1}\vee F) = n-1+\operatorname{sat}(n-1, F)\]

holds for all integers \(n > |V(F)|\). The conjecture predicts that equality fails exactly when F contains a component that is a complete graph on at least three vertices together with at least one isolated vertex. In all other cases – i.e. when every non‑trivial component of F is a star or a matching – equality holds. This unifies the known results for \(F=K_{p-1}\cup K_{1}\), \(F=K_{2}\cup qK_{1}\) and \(F=2K_{2}\cup qK_{1}\) and gives a clean combinatorial description of the extremal situation.
proof_strategy: Use induction on n together with structural analysis of minimum saturated graphs for F. One direction (sufficiency) proceeds by constructing the candidate extremal graph K_1 \vee H where H is an n‑1‑vertex F‑saturated graph attaining sat(n‑1,F), and showing it is (K_1\vee F)‑saturated. The converse (necessity) assumes equality holds for infinitely many n and derives constraints on the components of F by examining the degree‑sequence of any extremal (K_1\vee F)‑saturated graph: the unique vertex of the K_1 part must be universal, forcing every non‑isolated component of F to be a star or a matching; otherwise one can exhibit a strictly smaller (K_1\vee F)‑saturated graph, contradicting minimality. The proof can be formalized in Lean by defining saturation, join, and the sat function, then proving the two lemmas “if F satisfies the component condition then equality holds” and “if equality holds then F satisfies the component condition”.
title: Characterization of equality in the Cameron–Puleo bound for joins with an isolated vertex

description: Every symmetric sign pattern P with zero diagonal requires full P-vertices if and only if every maximum matching of the underlying graph G is a perfect matching, extending the tree characterization from the paper to general graphs.
proof_strategy: Prove necessity by constructing matrices in the qualitative class with non-perfect maximum matchings leading to fewer than n P-vertices. Prove sufficiency by showing that when every maximum matching is perfect, the eigenvalue multiplicity condition m_{A(j)}(0) - m_A(0) = 1 holds for all vertices j and all A in the qualitative class, using interlacing theorems and structural graph analysis.
title: Perfect Matching Characterization for Symmetric Sign Patterns Requiring Full P-vertices

description: For any odd prime p and prime ℓ ≠ p, let G^{MB}(ℓ, p) be the finite directed graph whose vertices are equivalence classes of Moret-Bailly families of principally polarized supersingular abelian surfaces over 𝔽̄_p and whose edges are (ℓ, ℓ)-isogenies weighted by w(f) = |RA(v₁)/Stab_{RA(v₁)}(Ker f)|. Let M be the random walk matrix of this graph (i.e., the weighted adjacency matrix normalized by the weighted out-degree at each vertex). Then all eigenvalues λ of M satisfy either λ = 1 (with multiplicity 1) or |λ| ≤ 2√ℓ / (ℓ + 1).
proof_strategy: Use the Jacquet-Langlands correspondence to relate the eigenvalues of M to Hecke eigenvalues on an inner form of GSp₄/ℚ that is compact modulo center. Apply the generalized Ramanujan conjecture for GSp₄ (known in this setting via work of Weissauer, Laumon, etc.) to bound the Satake parameters at ℓ, which translate to the eigenvalue bound via the explicit dictionary between Hecke operators and graph adjacency.
title: Ramanujan Bound for Moret-Bailly Isogeny Graphs

description: Formalize the theorem stating that for a finite connected graph G with n vertices and resistance matrix R, the determinant of R can be expressed as a weighted sum of squared differences of resistances from any fixed vertex k: det R = ((-1)^(n-1) * 2^(n-2) / kappa(G)) * sum_{e=(i,j) in E} (R_{ik} - R_{jk})^2, where kappa(G) is the number of spanning trees.
proof_strategy: The proof involves defining the Laplacian matrix L and utilizing the Matrix Tree Theorem to express kappa(G). The resistance matrix R is then related to the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse of L. The formalization would require implementing the Bapat identity for det R and the combinatorial identity linking spanning forests to resistance differences, then applying the sum over edges using the property that the sum is invariant of the choice of vertex k.
title: Combinatorial Determinant of the Resistance Matrix

description: The paper establishes explicit identities for the odd rank generating functions modulo 5, analogous to Ramanujan's identity ∑ p(5n+4)q^n = 5(q^5;q^5)_∞^5/(q;q)_∞^6. We conjecture that a similar identity exists modulo 7 for odd ranks: there exist integers a, b, c, d, e, f such that the generating function for odd ranks of partitions congruent to 5 modulo 7 can be expressed as a combination of q-Pochhammer symbols (q^7;q^7)_∞ and (q;q)_∞ with rational coefficients, mirroring Ramanujan's identity ∑ p(7n+5)q^n = 7(q^7;q^7)_∞^3/(q;q)_∞^4 + 49q(q^7;q^7)_∞^7/(q;q)_∞^8. This would imply both the equidistribution of odd ranks modulo 7 for partitions of 7n+5 and a congruence for the odd partition function modulo 7.
proof_strategy: Use the transformation formulas for odd rank generating functions developed in the paper to analyze the behavior at the 7th root of unity ζ_7. Compute the Fourier expansion of the completed odd rank generating function as a weak Maass form, isolate the holomorphic part, and match coefficients with a suitable linear combination of eta-quotients. Verify the identity by checking initial coefficients and proving the modular transformation properties.
title: Modulo 7 Analogue of Ramanujan's Identity for Odd Ranks

description: For any graph G with clique number 3, after regularizing G to G' while preserving triangle packings, the complement of G' is conformable if and only if G admits a perfect triangle packing. This conjecture formalizes the bi-conditional relationship between conformable colorings in the complement graph and triangle packings in the original graph, as implied by the reduction in the paper.
proof_strategy: Formalize the regularization process, prove the correspondence between odd cliques in the regularized graph and conformable color classes, and establish the equivalence with perfect triangle packing. Use structural induction on the triangle decomposition and leverage the parity conditions imposed by conformability.
title: Conformability of the Complement Regularized Graph and Perfect Triangle Packings

description: The paper proves the infinite family $\overline{b}_{9l+2}(9m+3) \equiv 0 \pmod{3}$ for all $l,m \geq 0$. Observing that $3 \equiv 3 \pmod{4}$, $9 = 3^2$, $2 = 3-1$, and $3 = 3$, we conjecture this pattern generalizes to all primes $p \equiv 3 \pmod{4}$: for all $l,m \geq 0$, $\overline{b}_{p^2 l + (p-1)}(p^2 m + p) \equiv 0 \pmod{p}$. This is falsifiable by computing $\overline{b}_k(n)$ for small $p$ (e.g., $p=7$ predicts $\overline{b}_{49l+6}(49m+7) \equiv 0 \pmod{7}$).
proof_strategy: The generating function for $\overline{b}_k(n)$ is an infinite product (eta-quotient). For $k = p^2 l + p - 1$, analyze the generating function modulo $p$ using the $U_p$ operator and the fact that $\eta(pz)/\eta(z)$ is a modular form of level $p$. Show that the coefficient of $q^n$ vanishes modulo $p$ unless $n \equiv p \pmod{p^2}$, by proving the form is congruent to a $p$-adic modular form supported on that progression.
title: Generalized Congruence Family for Overcubic Partition k-Tuples Modulo Primes p ≡ 3 (mod 4)

description: We conjecture that the number of extra vertices introduced by DPLAN's orthogonal floor plan (OFP) generation equals the number of separating triangles in the intermediate plane triangulation, and that this number is optimal: no orthogonal floor plan can realize the same door‑adjacency constraints with fewer added vertices.
domain_bridges: Formalizing graph‑based floorplan generation in proof assistants
Planar embeddings and orthogonal polygon generation
proof_strategy: The proof would consist of three parts: (1) establishing a bijection between separating triangles and added vertices in the OFP construction, (2) showing each added vertex is necessary via a lower‑bound argument using Euler's formula and face‑vertex incidences, and (3) proving optimality by demonstrating that any orthogonal floor plan realizing the same adjacency constraints must have at least as many interior vertices as there are separating triangles (e.g., via a counting argument on the dual graph and its treewidth). Induction on the number of separating triangles together with known results on planar triangulations and orthogonal duals would be employed.
title: Minimal Added Vertices in DPLAN's Orthogonal Floor Plan Mode

description:
For a circulant graph $C_{p^k}(R)$ with $p$ prime and $k\ge 1$, consider its Type‑2 isomorphism graph $\mathcal G_{2}(C_{p^k}(R))$ whose vertices are all circulants Type‑2‑isomorphic to $C_{p^k}(R)$ (with respect to any divisor $m>1$ of $p^k$) and whose edges join two vertices when they are related by a single Type‑2 transformation. The conjecture states that the graph diameter of $\mathcal G_{2}(C_{p^k}(R))$ is exactly $k$, i.e. the exponent of the cyclic group $\mathbb Z_{p^k}$.

Formally: let $\mathcal V$ be the set of all $C_{p^k}(S)$ that are Type‑2‑isomorphic to $C_{p^k}(R)$. Define a directed edge $C_{p^k}(S) \to C_{p^k}(T)$ whenever there exists a divisor $m\mid p^k$, $m>1$, and a unit $x\in\mathbb Z_{p^k}^*$ such that $T = xS$ after the reflexive reduction modulo $p^k$ and $\gcd(p^k, x)=m$. Let $\mathcal G_{2}$ be the underlying undirected graph. Then the conjecture is:

$$\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal G_{2}(C_{p^k}(R))) = k.$$
proof_strategy: 1. Formalise circulant graphs as simple graphs on `fin n` with edge set `{(i, i + r) | r ∈ R}` using `simple_graph`. 2. Define the Type‑2 transformation on a set `R` via a divisor `m` of `n` and a unit `x` with `gcd n x = m`. 3. Build the Type‑2 isomorphism graph `G₂` as a finite simple graph whose vertex type is `circulant n`. 4. Prove that for `n = p^k` the group of units modulo `p^k` is a cyclic group of order `p^{k-1}(p-1)`. 5. Show that any two Type‑2‑isomorphic circulants can be connected by a sequence of at most `k` transformations, using the filtration of divisors `p, p^2, …, p^k`. 6. Construct explicit examples attaining distance `k` (e.g., starting from the generating set `{1}` and applying successive multiplications by `p` modulo `p^k`). 7. Conclude that the diameter is exactly `k`.  The proof will rely on lemmas about the structure of the unit group, the behaviour of reflexive reduction, and induction on `k`.
title: Diameter of the Type‑2 isomorphism graph equals the exponent of the underlying cyclic group for prime‑power circulants

description: Conjecture: For an s-connector graph G on N vertices and a q-edge-coloring of its edges, there exists a color j∈[q] such that G contains a monochromatic star K_{1, t_j} (a vertex with at least t_j incident edges of color j) if and only if N ≥ Σ_{j=1}^q (t_j−1) + max{2s, s+max_j t_j}. proof_strategy: Construct explicit generators using colored partition identities from Dousse-Konan, verify they are algebraically independent via Gröbner basis techniques for arc algebras, and establish the isomorphism by showing surjectivity of the induced map from the polynomial ring.
title: Zhu Algebra of $\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_n$ at Level 1 is Polynomial Ring

description: Assuming Hypothesis U (the existence of sufficiently many powersmooth shifted primes), for any ε>0 there exists X0 such that for all x≥X0 and y satisfying exp((log₂ x)^{1+ε}) ≤ y ≤ x / exp((log₂ x)^{1+ε}), the counting function L(x,y) = #{n ≤ x : λ(n) ≤ y} obeys L(x,y) ≥ x · (ℒ(x/y))^{−1−ε} when y ≥ ℒ(x)², and L(x,y) ≥ x · (ℒ(x,y))^{−1−ε} otherwise, where ℒ(x,y) = exp((log x · log₃ x) / log₂ y). This matches the upper bound of Theorem 1.1 in the paper up to the ε in the exponent, establishing asymptotic sharpness.
proof_strategy: Use Hypothesis U to construct many n whose prime factorization consists of primes p with p−1 being y‑smooth, ensuring λ(n) divides a smooth number ≤ y. Combine a weighted sieve (or Turán–Kubilius inequality) to count such n, and optimize the parameters to obtain the claimed lower bound. The argument mirrors the proof of the upper bound but reverses the inequality by exhibiting a positive proportion of integers with small Carmichael function.
title: Sharp lower bound for L(x,y) under Hypothesis U

description: We conjecture that there exist two Gorenstein lattice polytopes P and Q such that their join P*Q is not Gorenstein. This would demonstrate that the Gorenstein property is not inherited under the join operation, extending the paper's findings on Cartesian products to joins.
proof_strategy: Construct explicit counterexamples by considering Gorenstein simplices or low-dimensional polytopes, then analyze the join's Gorenstein property through its h*-polynomial or algebraic structure.
title: Join of Gorenstein Polytopes is Not Necessarily Gorenstein

description: Establishing a precise asymptotic estimate for the extremal supremum of pairwise coprime subsets, with a conjectural refinement outlining the origin and implications of the bound.
domain_bridges: Erdœs problems, conditional regularity, and sieve methods
proof_strategy: Long-interval sieve with Mahler-type weights, conditional cancellation over arithmetic progressions, and refinement via lacunary structure.
title: An Average-Order Conjecture for Shifted Coprime Sums

catalog_references: Wegner, G. (1965). Über die maximale Anzahl von Punktmengen...
description: Formalize the existence of a finite family of axis-parallel rectangles in $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that the ratio of the piercing number $\tau(\mathcal{R})$ to the independence number $\nu(\mathcal{R})$ is at least 2, specifically by constructing a triangle-free rectangle intersection graph where $\tau(\mathcal{R}) \ge n/2$ and $\nu(\mathcal{R}) \le n/4$ for a set of $n$ rectangles.
domain_bridges: Graph Theory (Clique Cover vs Independence Number)
proof_strategy: The proof would involve defining a formal representation of axis-parallel rectangles in Lean (using intervals in $\mathbb{R}^2$). The core of the challenge is to encode the specific construction used in the paper (the triangle-free intersection graph) as a finite collection of rectangles and then use automated or tactic-based reasoning to verify that no point hits more than two rectangles and that the independence number is bounded by $n/4$.
title: Lower Bound on the Integrality Gap of the Rectangle Piercing Problem

catalog_references: Andrews, P.F., Jackson, A.J., et al.
description: A conjecture asserting the validity of a specific congruence modulo Φ_n(q) when n ≡1 mod4, aligning with established hypergeometric summation properties.
proof_strategy: Modular reduction verification
title: Congruence Modulo Cyclotomic Polynomial

description: The paper conjectures that for fixed m > 1, the number of symmetric chain decompositions (SCDs) of the minuscule lattice L(m,n) grows super-exponentially with n. This conjecture is extended to the lattice M(n) of partitions into distinct parts at most n. We propose formalizing the lower bound for the growth rate of #SCD(M(n)) to prove it exceeds any exponential function of n.
proof_strategy: Define the poset M(n) as a subset of the power set of {1,..., n} with a specific order. Define the property of being a symmetric chain decomposition. Use a constructive method to show that for sufficiently large n, the number of ways to extend a partial SCD to a full SCD grows faster than c^n for any constant c, likely by relating SCDs to the number of standard Young tableaux or similar combinatorial structures that exhibit super-exponential growth.
title: Super-exponential growth of the number of symmetric chain decompositions of M(n)

catalog_references: Fang et al., 'Calabi-Yau Manifolds and Their Metrics'
Li et al., 'Extreme Approximations in Geometry'
description: This conjecture posits that for a totally degenerating family of polarized abelian varieties, the existence of a non-Archimedean balanced metric would imply uniform control over the convergence rates of Hilbert–Chow stability criteria, which in turn constrains the possible bounds on the volumes of moduli spaces in such families.
proof_strategy: Constructive existence with uniformity guarantees
title: Non-Archimedean balanced metrics and their implications for totally degenerate abelian geometries

description: Conjecture that for any commutative ring R with 1, if the inclusion graph of annihilators Γ'(R) is connected and contains a cycle, then its girth is exactly 6.
proof_strategy: Analyze minimal prime ideals and their annihilator containments to bound possible cycles, use the existing diameter ≤4 result, and provide explicit rings where the bound is attained.
title: Exactgirth of the inclusion graph of annihilators in connected commutative rings

description: We propose that the boundary correlation matrix of an Ising model on a reduced planar graph in a disk can be expressed as a non-recursive function of the discrete CKP equation variables, which transform under Ising Y-Δ moves. This factorization through discrete CKP variables provides a direct solution to the inverse Ising problem, analogous to the chamber ansatz in electrical networks.
proof_strategy: Construct a correspondence between Ising model parameters and discrete CKP variables using Y-Δ move invariance, then show that the boundary correlations are polynomial functions in these variables, enabling recovery of coupling constants via algebraic inversion.
title: Inverse Ising Problem for Reduced Planar Graphs via Discrete CKP and Y-Δ Moves

description: Let G and H be connected graphs that are 2‑isomorphic via a bijection τ on edges, and let U be a unimodular matrix with L_H = U L_G Uᵀ (as guaranteed by Whitney’s theorem). For distinct vertices a,b of G and c,d of H such that τ maps edge (a,b) to edge (c,d), the restriction of U to the space of harmonic vectors with respect to {a,b} is a linear bijection onto the space of harmonic vectors with respect to {c,d}. Moreover, this map sends the constant all‑ones vector to itself. This statement can be formalised in Lean 4 using the existing libraries for matrices, graphs, and linear algebra.
domain_bridges: potential theory on graphs ↔ harmonic vectors
proof_strategy: 1. Formalise graphs as simple graphs with a finite vertex type. 2. Define incidence matrices N_G, N_H and Laplacians L_G = N_G ⬝ N_Gᵀ, L_H analogously. 3. Use the existing theorem (Whitney–Watkins) that 2‑isomorphism ⇔ existence of unimodular U with L_H = U ⬝ L_G ⬝ Uᵀ, and import it from mathlib or prove a lightweight version. 4. Define the subspace W(S) ⊆ ℝ^n and the harmonic space Har(G,S) = {v | v ⬝ L_G ∈ W(S)}. 4. Show that for any S, the map v ↦ v ⬝ U restricts to a linear map Har(G,S) → Har(H,τ(S)). This follows from the computation (vU) L_H = v (U L_G Uᵀ) = (v L_G) Uᵀ, and the fact that Uᵀ preserves the defining conditions of W(·) because it is unimodular and maps the all‑ones vector to itself. 5. Prove injectivity and surjectivity by linear algebra: dim Har(G,S)=|S| (Lemma 1) and the same for H, together with invertibility of U. 6. specialise to S={a,b} and τ(S)={c,d}. 7. Conclude the theorem and record the constant vector preservation.
title: Unimodular bijection preserves two-point harmonic spaces under 2‑isomorphism

description: The conjecture states that for every integer d ≥ 2, any d‑dimensional grid graph G = P_{n₁} □ ⋯ □ P_{n_d} can be represented as a k‑interval‑PCG if and only if k ≥ d−1, and that fewer than d−1 intervals can never suffice. Equivalently, the minimum number of intervals needed for a k‑interval‑PCG representation of all d‑dimensional grids is exactly d−1. This is falsifiable: a counterexample would be a d‑dimensional grid admitting a (d−2)‑interval‑PCG representation for some d ≥ 3.
proof_strategy: Use combinatorial arguments on the hyperplane decomposition of d‑dimensional grids, combined with lower bounds on the number of disjoint intervals required to encode adjacency in weighted trees. The strategy would involve: (1) translating a k‑interval‑PCG into a weighted tree with a rooted structure; (2) showing that each coordinate direction forces a distinct interval unless merged; (3) proving that merging two coordinate directions inevitably collapses adjacency information, violating the PCG condition for some edge set. The approach would generalize known proofs for d = 2, 3 and extend them inductively to all d. Developing this argument requires building a Lean formalization of weighted trees, leaf distances, and interval PCG definitions, proving structural lemmas about hyperplane layers, and finally a lower‑bound lemma on the number of intervals.
title: Minimal Interval Complexity of d‑Dimensional Grid Graphs

description: For any full-dimensional convex d-polytope P, the top normal-fan shadow T(P) equals zero if and only if every facet F of P has an opposite support face which is a vertex. This extends the 3-dimensional result δ(P)=0 to arbitrary dimensions, connecting the vanishing of the generalized antipodal defect to the existence of vertex-opposite facet pairs in the normal fan structure.
proof_strategy: Construct the antipodal square complex X(P) for general d-polytopes using the normal fan stratification, compute its homology via the Vietoris-Begle theorem, and establish that T(P) = β₂(X(P);ℚ). Then prove T(P)=0 is equivalent to the vertex-opposite condition by showing that non-zero contributions to the defect arise precisely from facet-facet and facet-edge exact opposite pairs, which vanish exactly when all facets have vertex opposites.
title: Higher-Dimensional Antipodal Defect Vanishing Criterion

description: Conjecture: The direct (tensor) product of two finite, simple, connected distance walk regular (DWR) graphs is again distance walk regular.
proof_strategy: Leverage the algebraic characterization of DWR graphs: the set of distance matrices {A_i(G)} forms a basis of an algebra closed under matrix multiplication. Show that for the direct product G × H, the distance matrices are Kronecker products A_i(G) ⊗ A_j(H). The algebra generated by these Kronecker products is the tensor product of the individual algebras, which remains closed under multiplication, thereby proving the DWR property for the product.
title: Closure of Distance Walk Regular Graphs under Direct Product

description: A binary tree-child network on n≥2 leaves displays exactly 2^(n-1)-1 distinct rooted binary phylogenetic X-trees if and only if it can be obtained by starting from a rooted binary tree on n leaves and performing n-1 successive operations that replace a cherry edge by a reticulated cherry; equivalently, it has a unique rooted binary tree displayed twice, and this tree can be recovered by iteratively replacing a reticulated cherry with a cherry.
proof_strategy: structural induction on the number of leaves, analyzing cherry replacements and reticulation placements to characterize extremal networks
title: Conjecture on extremal tree-child networks achieving maximal displayed trees

description: For integers m,n with 1 ≤ m ≤ n, a contiguous m×n matrix over a finite field 𝔽_q is defined by choosing a sequence a_1,…,a_{m+n‑1}∈𝔽_q and forming the matrix whose (i,j)‑entry equals a_{i+j‑1}. Such a matrix is *super‑regular* if every square sub‑matrix obtained by selecting a contiguous set of rows and columns has non‑zero determinant. The paper proves a closed formula for the case (m,n) = (4,4) and gives formulas for (3,4), (3,5), (3,6). The conjecture extends this to all m,n: there exists an explicit polynomial‑in‑q expression P_{m,n}(q) together with a finite set of exceptional primes S_{m,n} such that for every prime power q with char(𝔽_q)∉S_{m,n}, the number of contiguous super‑regular m×n matrices over 𝔽_q equals P_{m,n}(q). Moreover, the exceptional primes are exactly those dividing a certain discriminant D_{m,n} that can be computed from the resultant of the defining polynomial inequalities.
domain_bridges: Finite field counting (Weil conjectures, rational point counts)
Formalized combinatorics in Lean (e.g., counting Latin squares)
proof_strategy: Apply the recursive linear‑substitution procedure of the paper to the system of polynomial inequalities defining super‑regularity for general (m,n).  Show that after finitely many linear eliminations the resulting system consists only of univariate polynomials whose zero‑counts are given by c_i(q).  Prove that the final expression is a polynomial F_{m,n} in q and the c_i(q), and that the only dependence on the characteristic is via the vanishing of a finite list of primes (the primes dividing the discriminants of the intermediate univariate polynomials).  Formalize each step in Lean: define the matrix construction, encode the non‑vanishing of all contiguous minors as a list of polynomial inequalities, implement the recursive algorithm as a computable function, and verify that it terminates and yields the claimed closed form.  Finally, extract from the Lean term the explicit polynomial P_{m,n}(q) and the exceptional set S_{m,n}.
title: Uniform formula for the number of contiguous super‑regular m×n matrices over finite fields

description: This conjecture formalizes the classification of quotient matrices arising from perfect 2-colorings of generalized Petersen graphs GP(n,k), linking their existence to specific divisibility conditions on n and k. The theorem establishes a one-to-one correspondence between these matrices and the intersection arrays of covering radius one completely regular codes in this graph family.
proof_strategy: Reduction to cyclic linear systems and Fourier analysis on roots of unity to establish non-existence; explicit periodic coloring constructions for feasible cases; cross-verification with known GP(n,2) and GP(n,3) classifications
title: Classification of Covering Radius One Completely Regular Codes in Generalized Petersen Graphs via Quotient Matrices

description: For q a power of 2, t an odd prime, let D be an André set on a line ℓ in PG(2,q^t). Let C be a non‑degenerate conic tangent to ℓ at point T with nucleus N, where T,N∉D. Then the set of affine points of C inherited to the André plane obtained by André replacement using D forms an arc if and only if q is a square and T and N are conjugate under the unique subgroup of order t of the stabilizer of D in PGL(3,q^t).
proof_strategy: Use the description of André replacement via spread sets, analyze the intersection numbers of inherited points with lines of the André plane, translate the arc condition into a condition on the quadratic form defining C and the field trace map associated to D, and apply known results on conjugacy in finite fields of characteristic 2.
title: Conjecture on Inherited Arcs from Tangent Conics in André Planes of Even Order

description: For the meromorphic modular form $F = \frac{\Delta}{E_6}$ of weight 6, and any prime $p \equiv 3 \pmod{4}$, the congruence $F|U_p^{2m} \equiv 0 \pmod{p^{4m}}$ holds for all $m \in \mathbb{N}$. This conjecture asserts that the exponent $\kappa_m = 4m$ (i.e., $\alpha = 4$, $\beta = 0$) is valid for all such primes and iterations.
proof_strategy: Leverage the paper's framework: (1) Express $F$ as an overconvergent modular form via supersingularity of $p \equiv 3 \pmod{4}$, (2) Apply the theory of overconvergent $U_p$ operators to establish the $p$-adic congruence, and (3) Show that the exponent $\kappa_m = 4m$ arises naturally from the weight and properties of $F$.
title: Congruence for $\frac{\Delta}{E_6}$ under $U_p$ operator for primes $p \equiv 3 \pmod{4}$

description: We conjecture that there exists a degree-4 pseudoexpectation arising from independent Haar-random rank-1 projectors in C^6 that satisfies all vector-coordinate and projector-coordinate constraints of the mutually unbiased bases problem at degree 4, implying that no degree-4 sum-of-squares proof can rule out the existence of seven mutually unbiased bases in C^6 when the variables are the projectors onto the basis vectors.
proof_strategy: Construct a pseudoexpectation by taking seven independent Haar-random orthonormal bases in C^6, defining random rank-1 projectors P_i^{(k)} = v_i^{(k)} (v_i^{(k)})^*. Show that for any real polynomial of degree at most four in the entries of these projectors, the expectation over the Haar measure yields a linear functional that respects the degree-4 localizing constraints (orthonormality within a basis and cross-basis unbiasedness) and yields a positive semidefinite moment matrix. Verify positivity using Weingarten calculus and the fact that the fourth moments of Haar-random projectors are expressible in terms of pairwise overlaps, which satisfy the MUB constraints in expectation. Conclude that the pseudoexpectation provides a degree-4 SOS obstruction, so any SOS refutation would contradict its existence.
title: Degree-four SoS cannot refute seven MUBs in C^6 in the lifted projector formulation

description: This conjecture formalizes the finiteness of the minimal size of zero-sum subsets in cyclic groups and extends it to a precise threshold condition for all finite abelian groups, grounded in structural properties of their additive rings.
proof_strategy: Symbolic reconstruction with group-theoretic constraints followed by combinatorial counting.
title: Categorical characterization of the zero-sum partition threshold in finite abelian groups

description: Conjecture that a smooth plane quartic over a discretely valued field with semistable reduction admits a unique GIT‑stable plane model if and only if its stable reduction is non‑hyperelliptic; equivalently, no unique GIT‑stable plane model can exist when the stable reduction is hyperelliptic.
proof_strategy: Construct an explicit counterexample: produce a smooth plane quartic over a discretely valued field with semistable hyperelliptic reduction that nevertheless admits a unique GIT‑stable plane model, thereby testing the necessity direction of the stated equivalence.
title: Semistable reduction of smooth quartics

description: This paper investigates a quantitative improvement over the known lower bounds on the image size of non-special polynomials in localization settings, leveraging a carefully constructed error structure.
proof_strategy: Construct explicit polynomial $f$ with controllable growth and uniform distribution of points
title: Split primes and the Elekes-Rónyai problem

description: We conjecture that the maximal density δ_n of a sphere packing in ℚ^n satisfies a polynomial‑factor improvement over the trivial 2^{-n} bound: there exists a universal constant c > 0 such that δ_n ≥ c · n^2 · 2^{-n} for every dimension n ≥ 1. This extends Klartag's lattice bound to general packings and suggests that the stochastic ellipsoid method yields a universal lower bound of the same order.
proof_strategy: Combine the random lattice method of Minkowski‑Hlawka with Klartag's stochastic ellipsoid evolution. Show that for a uniformly random lattice, the expected covering radius of a suitably scaled ellipsoid is O(n·det(L)^{1/n}), which yields a packing density at least c·n^2·2^{-n}. The proof would involve concentrating bounds for the Gram determinant, anti‑concentration of the random ellipsoid's shape, and a careful averaging argument over lattice rotations.
title: Uniform Polynomial Improvement for High‑Dimensional Sphere Packings

catalog_references: A q-analogue of the rational normal curve and linearized Reed-Solomon codes
description: The homogeneous ideal of the q-rational normal curve in P^{k-1} (as constructed in the paper) is generated by homogeneous polynomials of degree q+1. This generalizes the classical fact that the rational normal curve (q=1) is generated by quadrics.
proof_strategy: Extend the Schur-product-based techniques used for certain parameter choices to all parameters by analyzing the Hilbert function of the coordinate ring and showing that the (q+1)-degree hypersurfaces generate the ideal via a Gröbner basis argument or by proving the variety is arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay with the expected regularity.
title: Ideal generation of the q-rational normal curve

description: Every uniformly recurrent aperiodic infinite word has window complexity P^w(n) growing at least as fast as n^(1/3) for infinitely many values of n, i.e., there exists an infinite sequence of indices n_k such that P^w(n_k) ≥ n_k^(1/3).
proof_strategy: Construct a counterexample by attempting to build a uniformly recurrent aperiodic word with bounded window complexity through careful analysis of recurrence gaps and factor distribution, or prove the lower bound by contradiction using the uniform recurrence property to show that any attempt to keep window complexity below n^(1/3) would force eventual periodicity.
title: Lower bound on window complexity for uniformly recurrent aperiodic words

description: Conjecture that for every fixed rank m, the number V(m,n) of concave (or strongly concave) compositions of n with rank m is non‑decreasing as n increases; i.e., V(m,n) ≤ V(m,n+1) for all natural numbers n and m.
proof_strategy: Inductive construction using the difference systems described in the paper, combined with generating‑function coefficient extraction to compare V(m,n) and V(m,n+1).
title: Monotonic Growth of Rank Functions Across n for Concave Compositions

description: Establishes a canonical embedding of the Young subgroup 𝔄ₙ into the parity-alternating permutation group 𝔅ₙ within the symmetric group 𝔖ₙ, preserving Bruhat order containment for all n.
proof_strategy: Characterize Bruhat order relations via permutation statistics and parity patterns, leveraging existing bijections between Young subgroups and DAPs to establish order-preserving embeddings.
title: Bruhat Order Embedding for Parity Alternating Permutations

description: For any integer a ≥ 2, the Eichler integral of the Eisenstein series G_{2a} admits a unique harmonic Maass-Jacobi form completion of weight 2-2a, which transforms under the modular group action with an explicit correction term involving Bernoulli numbers and divisor functions. This completion satisfies a Ramanujan-type inversion formula under the transformation τ ↦ -1/τ.
proof_strategy: Construct the non-holomorphic completion explicitly using the Eichler integral, verify it satisfies the harmonic Maass equation, and establish the transformation law under SL2(Z) by computing its image under the Maass lowering operator. Decompose the proof into modular completion construction, harmonicity verification, and transformation formula derivation.
title: Modular Completion of Eichler Integrals as Harmonic Maass-Jacobi Forms

description: For any integer r ≥ 6, the maximum spectral gap among all connected r-regular graphs with essential edge-connectivity at most r is exactly 2. This bound is achieved by a specific family of graphs constructed in the referenced paper.
proof_strategy: Construct an explicit family of r-regular graphs with essential edge-connectivity exactly r and spectral gap 2, then prove no graph in this class can have a larger spectral gap by analyzing eigenvalue interlacing or using spectral graph theory bounds.
title: Spectral Gap Conjecture for r-Regular Graphs with Essential Edge-Connectivity r

description: This paper explores the Schur-positivity of symmetric functions arising from set partitions via Touchard-Riordan polynomials and their connection to descent sets.
proof_strategy: Constructive existence with consistency checks via Young diagram enumeration
title: Touchard-Riordan polynomials and the Schur positivity of set partitions

description: For any finite field ⁭ˇ and integer n≥4, there does not exist a perfect linear flag-rank-metric code in U(n,⁭ˇ) with minimum flag-rank distance 5.
proof_strategy: Show that the quadratic conditions derived in the paper for δ=5 cannot be satisfied by any code parameters in U(n,⁭ˇ) for n≥4
title: Non-existence of Perfect Flag-Rank-Metric Codes for δ=5 and n≥4

description: The paper establishes upper and lower bounds for the minimum density d(k, Z^2) of a maximal near-k-in-a-row avoiding set in Z^2, with a gap of (8+o(1))k^{-1}. The trivial lower bound arises because each k-in-a-row must contain at least two empty cells, suggesting d(k, Z^2) ≥ 2/k. We conjecture that this trivial lower bound is asymptotically tight, i.e., lim_{k→∞} k · d(k, Z^2) = 2.
proof_strategy: Construct a family of periodic maximal near-k-in-a-row avoiding configurations on Z^2 whose densities approach 2/k as k → ∞. This can be done by analyzing the equivalent problem of finding minimal 2-hitting sets for the hypergraph of all k-in-a-rows on the k×k torus (Z/kZ)^2, and showing that the fractional relaxation has value 2/k, which can be rounded to an integer solution with o(1/k) overhead using the Lovász Local Lemma or iterative absorption methods.
title: Asymptotic tightness of the minimum density for monochromatic k-in-a-row on Z^2

description: For every complex hyperplane arrangement H, the algebraic cobordism ring Ω^*(W_H) is naturally isomorphic to the complex cobordism ring MC(pt) (i.e., Ω^*_ℂ(pt)) as graded rings, and this isomorphism respects the induced grading by codimension
proof_strategy: search_for_counterexample_in_nonrealizable_matroids
title: Conjecture: Algebraic cobordism of wonderful varieties coincides with complex cobordism

description: For every even integer k ≥ 2, the two q‑hypergeometric series F_{2k}(q) and G_{2k}(q) defined in the hierarchy of Yashinski‑Agarwal‑Khan (order‑2k identities) are equal as formal power series. This extends the known equality for orders 0, 2 and the newly proved even orders in the paper, and predicts the same equality for all higher even orders.
proof_strategy: Define the two families of q‑hypergeometric series recursively using the dilations and translations described in the paper. Prove by induction on the even order that the recursive step preserves equality: assume F_{2k}(q)=G_{2k}(q) and use the weighted‑words construction to express F_{2(k+1)} and G_{2(k+1)} as products of the previous series multiplied by a fixed auxiliary factor. Apply the inductive hypothesis and basic q‑product identities (Euler's trick) to show the new factors match, yielding F_{2(k+1)}=G_{2(k+1)}. The base case k=1 corresponds to Capparelli’s theorem, already formalised in mathlib.
title: Even‑order hierarchy generating function equality beyond Capparelli

description: For the Mallows distribution with parameter q=1 (uniform case), the expected number of (S,k1,k2)-arrangements in a permutation of size n is asymptotically (n² / l!) * |S| as n approaches infinity. This conjecture can be verified by explicitly computing the expectation for q=1 and showing the leading term matches this expression.
proof_strategy: Compute the expectation directly for q=1 by noting uniformity of permutations, count valid (k1,k2) pairs, and show asymptotic equivalence using combinatorial arguments.
title: Asymptotic Expectation of (S,k1,k2)-Arrangements in Uniform Mallows Permutations

description: We conjecture that for every n ≥ 2, the cyclic permutation σ_n obtained by alternately visiting the extreme points (0, n-1, 1, n-2, 2, …) attains the maximal possible meander number among all cyclic permutations of length n, and that its meander number equals n^2 - n + 1.
proof_strategy: Define the meander number for a cyclic permutation via the minimal number of intersections of a cyclic meander realizing it. Construct an explicit piecewise‑linear cyclic meander for σ_n with exactly n^2 - n + 1 intersections, establishing the lower bound. Use the quadratic upper bound from the Schwartz conjecture and a careful case analysis to show no permutation can exceed this value, proving optimality.
title: Alternating Extremes Conjecture for Meander Numbers

description: For every edge-regular graph of degree d satisfying CD(κ,∞), there exists an explicit universal dimension parameter n = f(d,κ) such that the graph satisfies CD(κ,n), where f(d,κ) = d/(d - 2κ) when κ < d/2, and the graph is finite otherwise. This conjecture provides the precise formula for the self-improvement phenomenon claimed in the paper.
proof_strategy: Use the edge-regularity condition to derive vertex-transitivity, then apply curvature-dimension inequalities to construct explicit test functions showing that the Γ₂ inequality with n = ∞ forces the same inequality to hold with finite n. The key is to optimize over all possible distance functions and use the regularity to bound the improvement parameter.
title: Explicit dimension bound for CD(κ,∞) to CD(κ,n) self-improvement in edge-regular graphs

description: For any two vertices u and v in a finite graph H, if the matrices tI-L_μ(R(r)⊙H(u)) and tI-L_μ(R(r)⊙H(v)) have the same Smith normal form over ℚ(μ)[t] for every finite rooted graph R with root r, then u and v are cospectral for L_μ(H). This provides a converse to the main coalescence theorem in the paper and would give a complete characterization of when two vertices are cospectral in terms of Smith normal forms of all possible coalescences.
proof_strategy: Constructive approach: assume the Smith normal forms coincide for all R, use the structure of invariant factors to extract spectral information about H[u], H[v] (vertex-deleted subgraphs), apply the spectral excess theorem or related techniques to show the eigenvalues of L_μ(H) at u and v coincide, leveraging the fact that Smith normal forms encode complete spectral data.
title: Smith Normal Form Characterization of Cospectral Vertices for Generalized μ-Adjacency Matrices

description: This conjecture predicts the exact scaling behavior of the order of vanishing of twisted Carlitz zeta values at specific points, tying $t$-modules to the flatness properties of certain $P$-adic modular forms. It extends Anglès et al.'s results and offers a testable condition in Lean 4.
proof_strategy: Construct combinatorial witnesses via modular forms and $p$-adic interpolation
title: $P$-adic $L$-functions and their $t$-modular connections

description: For odd n ≥ 3, the Minkowski shape is a complete invariant among admissible pure degree-n number fields: if two such fields K_a = ℚ(θ) and K_b = ℚ(φ) with θ^n = a and φ^n = b have identical Minkowski shapes, then they are isomorphic as number fields.
proof_strategy: Formalize the dichotomy result by proving injectivity of the shape map for odd-degree pure fields under admissibility conditions, using the explicit integral basis formula and discrete-archimedean factorization from the paper as foundational machinery.
title: Minkowski shape classification for odd-degree pure number fields

description: For fixed integers g ≥ 2 and t ≥ 1, and every ε > 0, there exists a constant c > 0 such that for all sufficiently large n, there exists an n-vertex graph G with δ(G) ≥ (2/(2g+1) - ε)n containing no C_{2g-1}[t], yet γ_2(G) ≥ cn^2. This conjecture asserts that the threshold θ_g = 2/(2g+1) in Theorem 1 is asymptotically best possible by exhibiting extremal graphs whose bipartization number γ_2(G) is proportional to n^2 when the minimum degree condition falls below the threshold.
proof_strategy: Construct explicit families of graphs using balanced blow-ups of small odd cycles with carefully chosen edge distributions, then apply the stability method of Foucaud et al. to show that γ_2(G) remains bounded away from zero when δ(G) stays below the threshold. The construction will involve random graph techniques combined with deletion methods to avoid C_{2g-1}[t] while maintaining high minimum degree.

description: Formalize the lower bound on the expected value of the orbit-contact functional $K_t$ for a stochastic ellipsoid evolution process restricted to lattices with cyclotomic symmetry. proof_strategy: The strategy involves formalizing the stochastic differential equation (SDE) describing the evolution of the ellipsoid's shape matrix. One must define the Haar measure on the space of lattices with cyclotomic symmetry (Venkatesh's construction) and use a concentration inequality for the orbit-contact functional $K_t$. The core technical hurdle is formalizing the'shell-integral' calculation (Lemma 4.1 in the excerpt) as a bound on the expectation of a Gaussian-weighted integral over the sphere $S^{N-1}$ under the symmetry group action.
title: Lower bound for the expected orbit-contact functional of cyclotomic lattice ensembles

description:
# Future Directions — Primality Testing (AKS & Miller–Rabin)

Derived from this cycle's findings in `AKSCriterion.lean` and `MillerRabin.lean`.
Each conjecture is bold, falsifiable, and accompanied by the decisive insight and
a "why now?" justification.

## 1. Introspective-base AKS bound

**Conjecture.** There is an explicit polynomial bound `B(n)` (polylog in `n`)
such that: `n` is prime iff `(X + a)^n = X^n + a` in `(ZMod n)[X] / (X^r - 1)`
for all `1 ≤ a ≤ B(n)`, where `r = O((log n)^c)`. Formalizing this turns the
single-base criterion `aks_criterion` into the full deterministic
polynomial-time AKS algorithm.

The key insight is... the proven exact criterion `aks_criterion` already isolates
the obstruction (the inner coefficient `C(n,q)`); the remaining work is purely
the cyclotomic *order/coprime-base counting* that bounds how many bases are
needed once one quotients by `X^r - 1`.

**Why now?** With the freshman's-dream equivalence fully formalized (0 sorries)
and `not_dvd_choose_prime_dvd` in hand, the algebraic core is settled; the
outstanding piece is a self-contained counting argument that Mathlib's
cyclotomic and `orderOf` API can now support.

## 2. Monier–Rabin 1/4 error bound

**Conjecture.** For every odd composite `n > 9`, the number of Miller–Rabin
non-witnesses in `(ZMod n)ˣ` is at most `φ(n)/4`. Equivalently, the soundness
theorem `miller_rabin_sound` has a quantitative converse: composites have many
witnesses.

The key insight is... `sqrt_one_in_ZMod_prime` fails modulo a composite (there
are ≥ 4 square roots of `1` by CRT), and the strong-liar set is contained in a
proper subgroup of `(ZMod n)ˣ`; bounding that subgroup's index by `4` is the
whole game.

**Why now?** Soundness (the easy half) is verified; Mathlib's `ZMod.unitsEquiv`
CRT decomposition and subgroup-index lemmas make the proper-subgroup counting
tractable for the first time in this codebase.

## 3. AKS strictly dominates Fermat on every Carmichael number

**Conjecture.** For *every* Carmichael number `n` (not just `561`), the Fermat
congruence holds for all bases yet the AKS identity fails for some base coprime
to `n`; moreover the failing base can be taken to be the least prime factor's
co-factor. This generalizes `carmichael_561_fools_fermat_not_aks` to the entire
family A002997.

The key insight is... `aks_identity_imp_fermat` shows AKS ⇒ Fermat, and
`aks_criterion` shows AKS ⇔ primality, so AKS-failure is automatic for any
composite; the new content is identifying a *coprime* failing base uniformly via
Korselt's structure (`n` squarefree, `(p-1) ∣ (n-1)`).

**Why now?** The separation is already proved at `561` with a reusable mechanism
(contrapositive of `aks_criterion`); only Korselt's criterion needs to be
formalized to make the argument uniform over A002997.

## 4. Carmichael numbers are exactly the Fermat-universal composites

**Conjecture.** A composite `n` satisfies `∀ a, a^n ≡ a (mod n)` iff `n` is
squarefree and `(p-1) ∣ (n-1)` for every prime `p ∣ n` (Korselt's criterion),
and these are exactly the composites on which the Fermat test never detects
compositeness.

The key insight is... the universal Fermat congruence decomposes via CRT into
per-prime-power conditions, and `a^n ≡ a` modulo `p^k` for all `a` forces
`k = 1` and `(p-1) ∣ (n-1)` through the cyclic structure of `(ZMod p)ˣ`.

**Why now?** Our `native_decide` evidence already confirms the family begins
`561, 1105` (A002997); a structural Korselt proof would replace finite checks by
a general theorem and feed directly into Direction 3.

## 5. A `ZMod`-native fast modular-exponentiation tactic with a correctness theorem

**Conjecture.** A `csimp`-backed binary modular-exponentiation routine computes
`a^e mod n` with a kernel-checked correctness lemma `powMod a e n = a^e % n`,
fast enough to discharge Miller–Rabin / AKS instances by `decide` rather than
`native_decide`, removing the `Lean.ofReduceBool` dependency from results like
`carmichael_561_fools_fermat_not_aks`.

The key insight is... square-and-multiply is a fold over the binary digits of the
exponent; its correctness is a clean induction, and a `@[csimp]` replacement
keeps the kernel in charge (no `@[implemented_by]` trust gap).

**Why now?** The only non-`propext`/`Classical`/`Quot` axiom in this cycle is the
compiler-trust `Lean.ofReduceBool` from `native_decide`; a verified `powMod`
would let the Carmichael witness be checked by the kernel alone.
title: Derived from this cycle's findings in `AKSCriterion.lean` and `MillerRabin.lean`

description:
# Future Directions

The most natural next step is to attack the residue class isolated by the
prime-core reduction: primes `p ≡ 1 (mod 8)`. The key insight is that the four
elementary families already dispatch every residue except this one, so the entire
difficulty of Erdős–Straus is concentrated in a single arithmetic progression,
and any constructive scheme that handles it would, via
`erdosStraus_of_primes_one_mod_eight`, close the problem unconditionally. A
promising route is to formalize the classical covering-congruence constructions
of Mordell, which solve `4/p` for all `p` outside a sparse set of residues modulo
small moduli (e.g. residues that are quadratic non-residues modulo `4`, or that
fall into specific classes mod `3·8`, `5·8`, `7·8`, …). Why now? Because the
present development supplies exactly the reusable scaffolding — the predicate, the
witness-verification idioms, and divisor inheritance — that such a formalization
would otherwise have to rebuild from scratch.

A second direction is computational certification at scale. The key insight is
that `ErdosStrausSolution n` is witnessed by a finite triple whose correctness is
a single rational identity, so a verified search procedure could emit witnesses
for enormous ranges and check them by `decide`/`norm_num`, turning empirical
tables (which currently confirm the conjecture far beyond `10^17`) into
machine-checked theorems for explicit bounds. Why now? Because Lean's `decide`
kernel reduction and `norm_num` extensions are mature enough to validate millions
of rational identities reliably, and the bounded theorem `erdosStraus_upto_100`
demonstrates the pattern end to end; scaling it is an engineering problem, not a
mathematical one.

A third direction concerns the structure of the witness map itself.
The key insight is that the family witnesses are not ad hoc but instances of a small
number of algebraic identities (the `1/a + 1/(a·n)` split and its halving, and the
`(n+3)/(2na)` collapse), so one could formalize a *parametrized solver*: a single
lemma taking residue data and returning a witness, from which all four families
become corollaries. Why now? Because unifying the families would both shrink the
proof and expose precisely which algebraic degrees of freedom remain unused for
the `1 (mod 8)` case, potentially suggesting the missing construction.

A fourth direction is to connect this development to Mathlib's number-theoretic
infrastructure on quadratic residues and Dirichlet characters. The key insight is
that the obstruction at `p ≡ 1 (mod 8)` is governed by solvability of congruences
that quadratic reciprocity controls, so importing Mathlib's reciprocity and
Legendre-symbol API could let one phrase the open core as a clean statement about
representability rather than as a raw existential over triples. Why now? Because
Mathlib's quadratic reciprocity and `ZMod` character theory are now stable and
well-supported, making it feasible to translate the analytic-number-theory
heuristics for Erdős–Straus into formal, checkable hypotheses.

description: Arrow's impossibility theorem states that no ranked voting system with 3+ alternatives can be Pareto efficient, non-dictatorial, and independent of irrelevant alternatives (IIA). Conjecture: Arrow's theorem is a curvature statement. The space of preference profiles is a Riemannian manifold M with the Fisher information metric. The social welfare function F: M -> M is a mapping from profiles to social preferences. Arrow's conditions translate to geometric conditions: (1) Pareto efficiency means F preserves the direction of unanimous preference (F is 'forward-looking'). (2) IIA means F is a local mapping (the social preference at x depends only on local information near x). (3) Non-dictatorial means F is not a projection onto a single voter's preference. Conjecture: the only smooth, local, forward-looking maps on a positively curved manifold are projections (dictatorships). This is because a positively curved manifold has the property that parallel transport around a small loop rotates vectors (Holonomy), and a local, forward-looking map must preserve this holonomy, which forces it to be a projection. Conjecture: the curvature of the preference space is related to the 'polarization' of the electorate: when preferences are polarized (bimodal), the curvature is positive (sphere-like), and Arrow's theorem applies. When preferences are unimodal (consensus), the curvature is zero (flat), and majority rule works. Test: compute the curvature of the preference space for synthetic election data and verify the connection to Arrow's theorem. Impact: Arrow's impossibility is a theorem of differential geometry. Voting is curved.
proof_strategy: Define the preference space M = L(S)^n where L(S) is the set of linear orders on the alternative set S = {1, ..., m}. M is a discrete space with |L(S)|^n = (m!)^n points. To make this a manifold, we smooth it: replace each ranking with a utility vector u_i in R^m (normalized to the simplex Delta^{m-1}). The preference space becomes M = (Delta^{m-1})^n (n voters, each with a utility vector on the simplex). The Fisher information metric on M: g_{ij}(u) = E[(d/d u_i) log p(x|u) * (d/d u_j) log p(x|u)]. For the multinomial distribution: g_{ij} = delta_{ij} / u_i (the Fisher-Rao metric on the simplex). The curvature of (Delta^{m-1}, g) is constant positive (it's a spherical geometry). Arrow's conditions on F: M -> M: (1) Pareto: F(u_1, ..., u_n) has the same sign as the sum of u_i's (forward-looking). (2) IIA: F is local, i.e., dF only depends on local information (F is a smooth map). (3) Non-dictatorial: F is not a projection pi_i: (u_1, ..., u_n) -> u_i. Theorem: on a positively curved manifold, any smooth local forward-looking map is a projection. Proof sketch: by the Gauss-Bonnet theorem, a map from a positively curved manifold to itself that preserves direction must be either the identity or a projection. The key: the holonomy group of (Delta^{m-1})^n is SO(m-1)^n, and a local map must commute with this holonomy, which forces it to be a projection. Test: for m=3 alternatives, compute the curvature of Delta^2 (which is constant positive = 1/2), and verify that local forward-looking maps are projections.
title: The Geometry of Consensus: Arrow's Theorem as Curvature

description: The key insight is that the Collatz map T(n) = n/2 if n even, 3n+1 if n odd, appears to be a one-way function: easy to compute forward (polynomial time), intractable to invert (finding a preimage requires exponential search). Conjecture: Under the assumption that the Collatz conjecture is true, the function f(a, n) = T^a(n) (a iterations starting from n) is a one-way function with security parameter a. The inversion problem — given (a, f(a,n)), find n — requires O(2^{a/log(a)}) steps. Why now: the Collatz map has been verified to converge for all n up to 2^68, providing empirical evidence for irreversibility. Test: prove that f(a,n) cannot be inverted in sub-exponential time under a reasonable computational model. Construct a collision-resistant hash function from iterated Collatz maps. Impact: a new class of cryptographic primitives based on dynamical systems irreversibility, not number-theoretic hardness.
proof_strategy: Define Collatz hash H_k(x) = T^k(x) mod 2^256. Prove collision resistance: if H_k(x) = H_k(y) for x != y, then T^k(x) = T^k(y) mod 2^256, requiring T to have a period dividing 2^256 within k steps — contradicting empirical data showing no Collatz period below 2^68. Prove preimage resistance: given z, finding x with H_k(x) = z requires trying O(2^{128}) preimages because each Collatz step is a 2-to-1 map on average. Formalize in Lean 4: define the Collatz hash and prove its basic properties.
title: Cryptography from the Collatz Conjecture: One-Way Functions from Iterated Maps

description: Develop a large deviation principle for max-plus probability measures. Prove that max-plus random walks satisfy an LDP with rate function given by the Legendre-Fenchel transform.

description: Prove that the Bergman fan of a matroid M equals the tropical linear space of the matroid's circuit ideal. Formalize the connection between matroid connectivity and the topology of the Bergman fan. Show that nested matroids give tropical linear subspaces.

description: Treat chaotic attractors (Lorenz, Henon, Rossler) as algebraic objects — not just numerical phenomena. Conjecture: The Lorenz attractor's topology can be characterized as the inverse limit of a specific diagram in the category of finite directed graphs. Test: compute the inverse limit and compare its Cech cohomology to the known Lorenz template. Impact: if true, chaotic dynamics become amenable to algebraic topology and category-theoretic methods.
title: Strange Attractors as Algebraic Objects

description: The EML single operator f(x) = e^a * log(b*x + c) is a contraction mapping for suitable parameter ranges. Conjecture: For all a, b, c in R with a > 0 and b, c chosen so that the function maps a closed interval to itself, the iteration x_{n+1} = e^a * log(b*x_n + c) converges to a unique fixed point x* at a rate O(rho^n) where rho = |f'(x*)|. Moreover, the fixed point x* satisfies x* = e^a * log(b*x* + c) and can be expressed as a power series in a. The fixed point is unique because f is a contraction on the invariant interval: the derivative f'(x) = e^a * b / (b*x + c) is bounded by |f'| < 1 when the parameters are in the right range. This makes EML functions well-behaved iterative schemes, unlike arbitrary neural network activations. Test: prove convergence for the specific case a in (0,1), b=1, c in (0,1) and compute the fixed point explicitly as a series. Impact: establishes EML as having well-defined dynamical behavior, enabling EML-based iterative algorithms with certified convergence.
proof_strategy: Define the EML iteration T(x) = exp(a)*log(b*x + c) for parameters a, b, c. Prove T has a unique attractive fixed point when the spectral radius of the Jacobian at the fixed point is < 1. Derive explicit conditions on a, b, c for convergence: |e^a * b / (b*x* + c)| < 1. Show the Banach fixed point theorem applies on the invariant interval. Test: compute the fixed point for a=0.5, b=1.0, c=0.1 numerically, then prove the convergence bound in Lean 4.
title: EML Fixed-Point Theorem: exp-log Iteration Convergence

description: The Stone-Weierstrass theorem guarantees that any continuous function can be approximated by an algebra that separates points and contains constants. Conjecture: The algebra of EML functions (finite compositions of exp, log, +, *) on any compact subset of R^n is dense in C(K) with a Jackson-type rate: for f in Lip_alpha(K), there exists an EML network of width O(epsilon^{-n/alpha}) approximating f within epsilon. The separation property is key: given x != y in K, the function g(t) = exp(a)*log(b*t + c) can separate them for appropriate parameters a, b, c (because g is strictly monotone for a, b > 0). The constants are included via c = exp(a)*log(c) for c > 0. This gives EML networks provable approximation guarantees with explicit rates, going beyond the existential guarantees of universal approximation theorems. Test: prove the separation property (given x != y in K, find EML parameters that separate them) and the rate bound for Lipschitz functions. Construct an EML network of width n approximating x^2 on [0,1] with explicit error bounds. Impact: gives EML networks provable approximation guarantees with explicit rates, surpassing the existential guarantees of universal approximation theorems.
proof_strategy: Step 1: Prove the algebra A of EML functions on compact K separates points. Given x != y in K, the function g(t) = exp(a)*log(b*t + c) is strictly monotone for a,b > 0, so g(x) != g(y) for some parameters. Step 2: Prove A contains constants (c = exp(a)*log(c) for c > 0). By Stone-Weierstrass, A is dense in C(K). Step 3: Prove Jackson-type rate: for f in Lip_alpha(K), construct an EML network of width O(epsilon^{-n/alpha}) achieving error epsilon. Test: construct an EML network of width n approximating x^2 on [0,1] with explicit error bounds O(n^{-2}).
title: EML Interpolation Theory: Stone-Weierstrass for exp-log Networks

description: Formalize diffusion models as solutions to stochastic differential equations.
